npc:aelthalyste.text: Aelthalyste. In the Undercity's War Quarter, Aelthalyste trains Forsaken priests in the power of Shadow. She guides their spiritual discipline and sends troll acolytes to their own elders in Orgrimmar. Aelthalyste trains Forsaken priests in the power of Shadow. While many priests across Azeroth revere the Holy Light, her students have turned from it. She rose as an incorporeal banshee and shares the spectral agony and relentless resolve of Sylvanas Windrunner's followers. From her chamber in the Undercity's War Quarter, she calls aspiring priests from distant outposts to master their darker arts. She teaches them to harness suffering as a weapon. Aelthalyste respects the spiritual traditions of other Horde practitioners. She sends troll initiates away from her shadow teachings, directing them across the sea to Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar, where they can learn Darkspear spiritualism. Her deference lets Horde spellcasters develop within their own traditions and strengthens ties between Kalimdor and Lordaeron.

npc:ahanu.text: Ahanu. Couriers arriving in Thunder Bluff can find Ahanu in Hewa's Armory. He crafts and trades leather armor for travelers and young braves setting out across Mulgore and the wider plains, and helps new couriers find their way across the bluffs. Ahanu works the hides his friend Jahan Hawkwing sends from the Crossroads. In Hewa's Armory on Thunder Bluff's lower rise, he crafts durable leather gear for those who travel Kalimdor's grasslands. Travelers arriving by wind rider from the Crossroads can find him among the city's tradesfolk. He receives their deliveries and directs messengers toward the local flight roosts.

npc:alamar-grimm.text: Alamar Grimm. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm trains young gnome warlocks. The fall of Gnomeregan has left him bitter, wary of outsiders, and intent on teaching them to wield fel magic and summon an imp. At Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm carries a deep resentment over Gnomeregan's fall. While other gnomes in Coldridge Valley focus on recovery and tinkering, he distrusts ordinary adventurers and even the Ironforge dwarves who shelter his people. He grumbles that their allies care more about diplomacy with humans than reclaiming the fallen city. Alamar seeks others who share his belief that his people may need ruthless power. Alamar Grimm guides young gnomes who take up fel magic. A tainted memorandum earns a rare warm welcome, and he begins teaching them basic spells. Before he shares the dangerous knowledge needed to bind a demonic imp, he demands proof of their magical and physical endurance. He sends each novice to retrieve strange feather charms carried by local Frostmane troll novices.

npc:altsoba-ragetotem.text: Altsoba Ragetotem. Altsoba Ragetotem is a tauren weaponsmith stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. From this remote Horde outpost, he keeps passing champions armed with reliable maces, staves, and axes to face the blighted horrors of the forest. Bloodvenom Post is a treacherous outpost, situated in the heart of Felwood amidst demonic corruption and tainted wildlife. Maintaining a supply line out here is a grim necessity, and Altsoba Ragetotem does his part by outfitting Horde scouts and travelers. Whether someone requires a sturdy crescent axe or a heavy war maul, Altsoba ensures warriors heading into the corrupted timberlands do not enter the fray unarmed.

npc:alyissia.text: Alyissia. In Aldrassil, Alyissia trains young night elves to fight with strength and discipline. She teaches warriors how to defend the young world tree. Alyissia trains young night elves inside Aldrassil, where they learn to fight with steel and shield instead of nature magic or the priesthood. Kaldorei forces are known for their Sentinels and stealthy archers, but danger across Kalimdor also calls for fighters who can hold the front line. Alyissia teaches the first techniques: how to direct battle fury, master a stance, and withstand the wild creatures and corrupted grells that press into Shadowglen.

npc:amber-kearnen.text: Amber Kearnen. In Westfall, Amber Kearnen watches the Defias Brotherhood for SI:7. From a hidden vantage point, she tracks their unlawful activity for Master Mathias Shaw. Amber Kearnen scouts for SI:7 in Westfall, far from the halls of Stormwind Keep. She watches an abandoned tower the Defias Brotherhood has taken over. Master Mathias Shaw leads her work directly. Kearnen briefs covert operatives sent to stop Defias threats and gather intelligence across the contested countryside.

npc:andron-gant.text: Andron Gant. In the Undercity's Apothecarium, Andron Gant handles occasional commissions and relic recoveries for local scholars. He is a reclusive Forsaken, often drunk, and rarely leaves the city. Andron Gant spends his time in the Apothecarium, among its noxious fumes, and rarely ventures beyond the Undercity's stone walls. He seems little more than a drunken scholar. For local mages, he sometimes hires couriers to seek obscure relics on distant shores, including the Tablet of Markri.

npc:anduin-wrynn.text: Anduin Wrynn. Anduin Llane Wrynn is the ten-year-old crowned King of Stormwind, reigning in the absence of his missing father, King Varian Wrynn. Due to his young age, the true administration of the kingdom rests in the hands of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and the royal court. Born in the peaceful interlude following the Second War, Prince Anduin was named in honor of both his grandfather King Llane and the legendary knight Sir Anduin Lothar. Following the mysterious disappearance of his father en route to a diplomatic summit in Theramore, the child was abruptly crowned to maintain stability throughout the kingdom. Though intelligent and empathetic beyond his years, the ten-year-old monarch has little actual say in state affairs, leaving rule of the realm divided between Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and royal councilor Lady Katrana Prestor. Within the gilded walls of Stormwind Keep, young Anduin is surrounded by escalating political tension. While Highlord Bolvar manages military defenses and strives to maintain the integrity of the kingdom, the noblewoman Katrana Prestor constantly whispers counsel into the court's ear, actively undermining troop deployments to outlying human settlements. Anduin senses the precarious nature of his court and misses his father dearly, yet for now, he remains a figurehead surrounded by scheming nobles and watchful guardians.

npc:apothecary-helbrim.text: Apothecary Helbrim. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim studies the Barrens for the Royal Apothecary Society. Sent to Kalimdor, he gathers unfamiliar reagents for the Forsaken. Apothecary Helbrim works beneath the harsh sun at the Crossroads, far from the Royal Apothecary Society's quarters in the damp undercity of Undercity. Sent across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he searches the Barrens for useful plants, fungi, and other natural specimens. He depends on travelers to bring him samples, including local fungal spores, and works with Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. Through Helbrim, the Forsaken's alchemists reach beyond the ruined borders of Lordaeron.

npc:apothecary-zinge.text: Apothecary Zinge. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Apothecary Zinge works for the Forsaken. She studies biological specimens and arranges research shipments across Horde lands. Apothecary Zinge works in the Apothecarium beneath the Undercity. Under Master Apothecary Faranell, she searches for chemical and biological compounds that can advance the Forsaken's aims. Her work connects her with field researchers and scouts far beyond Tirisfal Glades, including at distant outposts in Kalimdor. Apothecary Zinge depends on couriers and adventurers to carry test materials across the sea. She regularly writes to Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads in the Barrens. She sends him toxic wolf heart samples from Silverpine Forest so he can study how Lordaeron's toxins affect Kalimdor's beasts.

npc:archaeologist-flagongut.text: Archaeologist Flagongut. At Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut keeps in touch with field researchers across the Great Sea. The dwarven scholar of the Explorers' League is staying at the Deepwater Tavern while bound for the Whelgar Excavation Site. Archaeologist Flagongut rests with a mug at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Like many members of Ironforge's Explorers' League, he traveled west across Khaz Modan to help with discoveries near the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. Though far from the high halls of the library, he keeps ties with field researchers, processing lost relics and reports carried across the Great Sea from distant expeditions. Dwarven curiosity reaches beyond one continent. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus sends Flagongut the mysterious fossil unearthed in Darkshore by the absent-minded Prospector Remtravel. Flagongut is amazed: he once brought a similar fossil to the Explorers' League's annual conference in Ironforge, convinced it held a power that could somehow be unlocked.

npc:archaeologist-hollee.text: Archaeologist Hollee. In Auberdine, Archaeologist Hollee tracks dwarven research across Darkshore. The ancient ruins draw Ironforge scholars to the coast, where she keeps in touch with prospectors searching for relics and unusual geological formations. Archaeologist Hollee works from Auberdine, among the night elves who guard and settle Darkshore. The dwarven scholar is a regional contact for surveyors and expedition teams crossing the wilderness. The Explorers' League sends its people across the sea to uncover traces of ancient history, and Darkshore's ruins give them ground to study.

npc:archbishop-benedictus.text: Archbishop Benedictus. In Stormwind City, Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church of the Holy Light from the Cathedral of Light. He guides the faithful and the Alliance through uncertain times. Archbishop Benedictus took the Church’s leadership after his mentor, Archbishop Alonsus Faol, died. He had seen the First and Second Wars devastate the kingdoms and helped oversee the building of the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City. He vowed to uphold the virtues of the faith. After Lordaeron fell and the Scourge rose during the Third War, the human kingdoms looked to him for spiritual guidance. From the Cathedral, he counsels the royal court, trains newly initiated priests, and directs holy crusades against the undead and demonic forces threatening Azeroth. Across the Alliance, people regard Archbishop Benedictus as a gentle, wise, and benevolent patriarch. He offers the public hope and rallies heroes against dark threats, including Amnennar the Coldbringer in Kalimdor. He also helps purify cursed relics brought by faithful adventurers.

npc:archmage-ansirem-runeweaver.text: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver. Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver is a senior human wizard and a ruling member of Dalaran's Council of Six. Having survived the Scourge's destruction of Dalaran in the Third War, he oversees Kirin Tor operations from the Violet Citadel as Dalaran is rebuilt. Though dedicated to the rebuilding of his city, he also maintains discreet interests abroad—including a willful daughter who ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate. A veteran mage who helped defend Dalaran across decades, Ansirem Runeweaver sits on the Council of Six, the ruling magocracy of the Kirin Tor. He survived the devastation when Arthas Menethil and the Scourge marched upon the city and Archimonde was summoned. In the wake of Dalaran's fall, Ansirem has aided the efforts to rebuild the arcane city, whose protective shield was lifted early, and now works from the Violet Citadel. Despite his scholarly duties and stern wizardly demeanor, Ansirem possesses personal ties far beyond the Alterac Mountains. His willful daughter, Catelyn, ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate, taking with her an ancient troll dagger he had found while researching in Stranglethorn. He has also dealt with Baron Revilgaz there. He has also engaged in arcane studies involving troll antiquities and maintains diplomatic conduits across distant realms.

npc:archmage-malin.text: Archmage Malin. Outside the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind City, Archmage Malin directs arcane affairs. A former pupil of Archmage Trelane, he coordinates field agents seeking magical artifacts and rare reagents across the Eastern Kingdoms. Archmage Malin is the central contact for Stormwind's arcane practitioners, stationed beneath the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter. He learned magic under Archmage Trelane, and now works to protect the scattered legacy of his former master. While acolytes study inside the tower, Malin watches over matters across the realm that need magical oversight. Archmage Malin directs much of his attention north, to the perilous ruins of the Arathi Highlands. He sent his trusted associates, Skuerto and Apprentice Kryten, to recover Archmage Trelane's lost possessions and secure delicate spell components. From the capital, Malin coordinates their work and relies on capable Alliance travelers to carry instructions, supplies, and intelligence to his agents in hostile territory.

npc:archmage-xylem.text: Archmage Xylem. Archmage Xylem is an eccentric and reclusive human wizard dwelling in an isolated tower atop the cliffs of northern Azshara. Known for his volatile temperament and dangerous experiments, he has withdrawn from worldly affairs to pursue esoteric arcane research. Reaching him requires magical teleportation, and he only entertains adventurers who can assist in his peculiar studies or aid his personal vendettas. Perched high upon the jagged cliffs of northern Azshara, Archmage Xylem makes his home in a secluded spire overlooking the ruined elven coastline. Rather than building a road or trail, the wizard isolated his sanctuary entirely, relying on his servant Sanath Lim-yo to magically transport approved visitors up the cliff face. Observers across Kalimdor consider him profoundly eccentric and perilous to deal with; even fellow scholars treat him with deep caution, noting that he behaves unlike almost any other human mage.

npc:argent-guard-manados.text: Argent Guard Manados. At the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Argent Guard Manados watches for corruption across Kalimdor. He serves the Argent Dawn and sends adventurers toward Blackfathom Deeps. Argent Guard Manados keeps the Argent Dawn's watch in Darnassus. While most of the order guards Lordaeron against the Scourge, he stands among the artisans and tradefolk of the Craftsmen's Terrace. His post lets him watch for threats to northern Kalimdor's balance. When word reaches him that the Twilight's Hammer has gained a foothold beneath Ashenvale's waves, he calls on capable heroes to strike at Blackfathom Deeps and recover the cult's artifacts of dark devotion.

npc:argos-nightwhisper.text: Argos Nightwhisper. In Stormwind's Park, Argos Nightwhisper guides Alliance travelers toward Darkshore. His brother Gershala studies the corruption spreading there. Argos Nightwhisper lives among the night elves gathering in Stormwind's Park. The district's quiet groves recall the kaldorei's ancestral woodlands. Like others of his kin stationed in the human kingdom, Argos connects the new allies across the Great Sea. Reports from across the ocean trouble him. He urges capable Alliance champions to travel to Auberdine in Darkshore, where his brother Gershala needs help against the spreading corruption.

npc:ashlan-stonesmirk.text: Ashlan Stonesmirk. At Dun Modr, Ashlan Stonesmirk watches the border with the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. The dwarven explosives expert keeps alert for dangers threatening Ironforge. At Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands, Ashlan Stonesmirk serves the regiment guarding the Thandol Span. His knowledge of explosives makes him a useful contact when suspicious materials threaten dwarven defenses.

npc:austil-de-mon.text: Austil de Mon. In Brill, Austil de Mon trains Forsaken warriors at Gallows' End Tavern. He teaches the newly risen to fight in service of the Dark Lady. Austil de Mon trains Forsaken warriors inside Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Warriors leaving Deathknell come to him among their first instructors. The living once drank and rested in the inn. Now Austil teaches newly liberated undead to master martial discipline and combat against the foes surrounding the kingdom.

npc:ayanna-everstride.text: Ayanna Everstride. In Shadowglen, Ayanna Everstride trains young kaldorei in the hunter’s way. Stationed in Aldrassil, she teaches marksmanship, tracking, and survival beneath the World Tree. Ayanna Everstride trains newly awakened kaldorei hunters inside Aldrassil, in the heart of Shadowglen. To the night elves, hunters are indispensable guardians of the sacred forests, not merely trappers or sharpshooters. Ayanna teaches novices early martial skills, ranged combat, and how to survive Teldrassil’s perilous woods.

npc:ayessa-dawnsinger.text: Ayessa Dawnsinger. Ayessa Dawnsinger is a Skyborne leader found in Valanaar on Zephras Isle. She leads the Windshapers, guiding the Skyborne aligned with the Horde through their trials and politics. Standing within the settlement of Valanaar on Zephras Isle, Ayessa Dawnsinger serves as the paramount guide for the Windshapers—the faction of Skyborne aligned with the Horde. From this vantage, she directs critical efforts across the island, managing external threats, internal fractures, and the overarching survival of her people as they navigate alliances in Kalimdor and beyond.

npc:azar-stronghammer.text: Azar Stronghammer. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Azar Stronghammer guides new dwarven paladins. After completing his own training in the Holy Light, he sends promising recruits to Ironforge for further instruction. Azar Stronghammer guides new dwarven paladins at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Humans are often linked to the great cathedrals, yet the dwarves of Khaz Modan have embraced the virtues of the Holy Light. Azar has mastered his own martial and spiritual vows, and helps newly inducted paladins find their footing on Dun Morogh's freezing slopes. When a novice shows dedication and spiritual maturity, he sends them up the mountain path to Ironforge. There they can study under veteran champions such as Tiza Battleforge.

npc:azuregos.text: Azuregos. Azuregos is an eccentric blue dragon stationed along the coast of Azshara to protect ancient Highborne relics. Entrusted with safeguarding immense magical power by the Spell-Weaver Malygos, he prefers quiet study over violence, but he will readily swat aside any adventurer foolish enough to disturb his vigil. Drawn to the magic-soaked shores of Azshara, Azuregos chose the ancient ruins of Eldarath as his sanctuary. Countless relics survived the Great Sundering along these shattered coasts, and Azuregos considers it his sacred duty as a servant of Malygos to keep such powerful artifacts away from careless mortals. Rather than lurking in a dark cave, he freely roams the crags and beaches, proudly dubbing himself the lord of all magic in the region. Though blessed with a sardonic sense of humor, he fiercely defends Azshara's treasures against the endless stream of adventurers seeking fame or plunder.

npc:bailiff-conacher.text: Bailiff Conacher. In Lakeshire Town Hall, Bailiff Conacher keeps Stormwind law in force under Magistrate Solomon. He relies on travelers to uphold local decrees across the embattled Redridge Mountains. Bailiff Conacher works with Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire Town Hall to uphold law across the Redridge Mountains. Blackrock orcs and local gnolls besiege the town, leaving Conacher without ordinary civic procedures or royal garrisons to rely on. He issues legal decrees that authorize passing travelers to carry out capital justice in the realm's name. When the dark mage Morganth took the Tower of Ilgalar and bent the local Shadowhide gnolls to his will, the Court of Lakeshire judged the beasts guilty of high treason. Stormwind law sentences those who aid a fugitive and criminal to death. Conacher invokes Solomon's Law and sends travelers across the ridges to find Shadowhide gnolls and bring back their pendants as proof that the crown's law has been carried out.

npc:bailor-stonehand.text: Bailor Stonehand. In Thelsamar, Bailor Stonehand’s forge work has been set back by stolen ore. The skilled dwarven smith once taught the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell and makes a specialized alloy for masterwork arms. Bailor Stonehand works the forge in Thelsamar, where his knowledge of minerals and specialized alloys reaches beyond Khaz Modan. He once taught Jordan Stilwell, a human smith, the foundations of metallurgy and shared formulas used to forge blessed paladin weapons such as Verigan's Fist. Mo'grosh ogres in the hills northeast of Thelsamar have stolen ore shipments meant for Bailor's forge. Without the raw material, he cannot make his rare alloys, and needs travelers and allies to recover the supplies from the ogres' encampments.

npc:balir-frosthammer.text: Balir Frosthammer. In Coldridge Valley, Balir Frosthammer rallies recruits against the Rockjaw troggs. The dwarf guards Dun Morogh as the troggs press into dwarven lands. Balir Frosthammer calls new recruits to defend Coldridge Valley. Dwarven and gnomish novices have long found safety and training there, but trouble underground has driven violent Rockjaw troggs to the surface. Balir is among the first to raise the alarm. He urges recruits to thin their numbers before they push farther into Dun Morogh. Balir Frosthammer bears a name shared with Tannok Frosthammer of Kharanos. The two may belong to the same family, whose members stand by Ironforge. They help keep the cold mountain passes safe for travelers, miners, and mountaineers as threats grow across the region.

npc:barithras-moonshade.text: Barithras Moonshade. In Auberdine, Barithras Moonshade looks to the wilds of Darkshore for rare subterranean plants. The night elf seeks travelers willing to explore the shadowy land and gather them. Barithras Moonshade watches over Auberdine and helps the night elves study and manage Darkshore. He sends travelers into nearby caverns to gather fungi, including death cap mushrooms, for study and use. Barithras also guides capable travelers south to meet Onu. The ancient works to heal Darkshore's tainted soil and soothe its restless natural spirits.

npc:barkeep-daniels.text: Barkeep Daniels. At the Lakeshire Inn, Barkeep Daniels keeps drinks flowing as raiders disrupt the roads. The town guards, fishermen, and travelers who gather there depend on the inn for a welcome pause, but supplies are running low. Barkeep Daniels pours drinks and greets visitors at the Lakeshire Inn, near the bridge. Gnolls and Blackrock orcs have kept Lakeshire under pressure for months, and its defenders turn to the tavern after grim patrols. Raids and severed roads have disrupted trade across the region. With liquor running low when the town needs good cheer, Daniels welcomes travelers willing to fetch shipments from safer settlements.

npc:baron-revilgaz.text: Baron Revilgaz. Baron Revilgaz is the cunning goblin leader of Booty Bay and the Blackwater Raiders, ruling the pirate haven on behalf of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Perched high on the balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern, he balances fragile trade neutrality with ruthlessly pragmatic opportunism. He hires passing mercenaries to secure his investments, undermine rivals like the Bloodsail Buccaneers, and retrieve ancient relics of the jungle. From his vantage atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Baron Revilgaz watches the bustling docks of Blackwater Cove through a custom enchanted spyglass. Flanked by his trusted advisor, the tauren Fleet Master Seahorn, Revilgaz exercises firm control over the town's cutpurses, merchants, and privateers. Originally a human settlement overwhelmed by trolls before the First War, the port was claimed and fortified by goblins, eventually evolving into the pirate-leaning commercial nexus of the Blackwater Raiders. Revilgaz ensures the port remains officially open to both Alliance and Horde travelers, strictly enforcing neutrality within harbor limits so that trade continues uninterrupted. Revilgaz's influence extends far past the harbor docks. When business stagnated following recent wars elsewhere in Azeroth, he seized upon the discovery of tastyfish to establish the Stranglethorn Fishing Extravaganza, drawing crowds back to his shores. Across Stranglethorn Vale, he keeps a sharp eye on competitors and potential threats: he commissions sabotage against the Venture Company at Lake Nazferiti, closely monitors Nesingwary's hunting expedition and rogue human military camps in the north, and maintains racing trade ties with Monte Gazlowe and Pozzik at the Mirage Raceway.

npc:bartleby.text: Bartleby. Bartleby drinks and picks fights at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. His stubborn hold on his ale makes him a test for aspiring warriors who must face him in a tavern brawl. Bartleby spends his days at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. The tavern draws a rougher crowd than the taprooms of Cathedral Square. He clings to his favorite mug, drinks cheap ale, nurses grievances, and picks fights with anyone who disturbs him. Stormwind's warrior trainers see a practical test in Bartleby. Harry Burlguard sends fledgling fighters to find him and take his mug. They must trade bare-knuckle blows with the intoxicated brawler, proving they have the grit to face an unruly opponent at close quarters.

npc:bashana-runetotem.text: Bashana Runetotem. On the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, Bashana Runetotem studies plants and corruption. She is the daughter of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem and aids the Cenarion Circle. Bashana Runetotem carries her father Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem’s druidic legacy on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise. While he guides tauren druids and advises Cairne Bloodhoof, Bashana studies unusual plants and regional threats. She gives travelers tools such as evergreen pouches to cultivate mysterious flora, including morrowgrain. She also coordinates Horde efforts against corruption spreading from places such as Blackfathom Deeps.

npc:bath-rah-the-windwatcher.text: Bath'rah the Windwatcher. Bath'rah the Windwatcher is a solitary jungle troll shaman and weaponcrafter dwelling amidst the ruins near Chillwind Point. Far from his tropical homelands, he studies the tempestuous elements of the northern mountains, seeking champions powerful enough to help him craft formidable weapons of wind. While most jungle trolls keep to the warm forests and coasts of the south, Bath'rah has embraced the solitary life of a mountain hermit among the cold ruins of the Alterac Mountains. A seasoned shaman and craftsman, he devotes his days to listening to the howling winds and communing with nature spirits. His obsession is not merely philosophical; he seeks to bind the fury of violent elemental storms into tangible armaments for those who possess the strength to wield them.

npc:beldin-steelgrill.text: Beldin Steelgrill. At Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh, Beldin Steelgrill keeps dwarven war machines running. He is its master technician, renowned in Khaz Modan for repairing siege engines and armored wagons. His work depends on a steady supply of specialized tools. Just down the road from Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot is where dwarven steam tanks and siege engines are tested and serviced. Beldin Steelgrill runs the work as its chief technician, known across Khaz Modan for repairing and tuning armored war wagons. The work is hard on heavy wrenches, cutters, and precision instruments. Beldin needs them constantly, keeping local ironworkers busy supplying his bench.

npc:bingles-blastenheimer.text: Bingles Blastenheimer. On Loch Modan’s southeastern shore, Bingles Blastenheimer waits beside the wreck of his flying machine. Stranded among troggs and beasts, the gnomish aviator needs his tools and parts back. Bingles Blastenheimer took his customized flying craft into the skies, but bringing it down safely proved harder than lifting off. His gyrocopter malfunctioned and crashed on the Loch’s southeastern shore. Bingles survived, but the machine broke apart. Far from Ironforge, he stays near the wreck, wary of hungry crocolisks and hostile troggs. Troggs from a nearby island stole his tools and Blastencapper explosives, and he asks passing travelers to recover them.

npc:bink.text: Bink. Bink is a gnome mage trainer who resides within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Quick-witted and enthusiastic, she guides aspiring spellcasters through the intricacies of the arcane arts and connects them with prominent wizards across the Alliance. Located in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, Bink stands among the gathered scholars, priests, and arcanists in the Hall of Mysteries. Like many gnomes driven from Gnomeregan, she has adapted to life within the dwarven mountain stronghold, offering her keen intellect and knowledge of arcane craft to those learning the path of the mage. She is well connected to wizards across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, regularly pointing promising apprentices toward greater mentors such as High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind or Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:bishop-delavey.text: Bishop DeLavey. In Stormwind Keep, Bishop DeLavey hears the court's quiet concerns. He represents the Church of the Holy Light in the Petitioner's Chamber, where matters of faith and state meet. Bishop DeLavey advises Stormwind's court from within the keep. While Archbishop Benedictus tends to the Cathedral of Light, DeLavey lives among the nobility and petitioners. He brings spiritual counsel to the court while reckoning with the kingdom's politics. His place there lets him hear whispered rumors and delicate grievances before they reach Highlord Bolvar Fordragon or the young King Anduin.

npc:blanchy.text: Blanchy. Old Blanchy is the loyal, hard-working mare belonging to Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, currently resting beside their wagon near the Jansen Stead in Westfall. Renowned for her gentle disposition and hefty appetite, she remains a steady companion to her owners amidst the turmoil gripping the countryside. Long before pulling the Furlbrows' wagon through the dust of Westfall, Blanchy worked the Furlbrows' farm in the breadbasket of Stormwind, where she earned a reputation as an exceptionally sweet-tempered, well-behaved mare. Years of heavy labor have worn her down to 'Old Blanchy,' and the arduous journey fleeing troubled homesteads has left her exhausted. Though visibly weary, her appetite remains hearty, and travelers who bring her nourishing handfuls of oats scattered across the surrounding fields are rewarded by Verna with Blanchy's own treasured blanket and feed pouch.

npc:bloodmage-drazial.text: Bloodmage Drazial. Bloodmage Drazial is a blood elf practitioner of arcane and blood magic camped in the northern reaches of the Blasted Lands. Alongside his sister Lynnore, he studies the native beasts of the red wastes to craft potent alchemical concoctions for traveling adventurers. Perched near the northern pass where the Swamp of Sorrows gives way to the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Drazial pursues a peculiar brand of magic. While many high elves shun the forbidden arts or despair over Quel'Thalas, Drazial and his sister Lynnore harness blood magic to harvest power from the harsh environment. The blighted fauna of the wastes—scorpoks, snickerfangs, and blasted boars—show strange, unnatural vigor, which Drazial and Lynnore believe came from the energy released when the Dark Portal opened. By harvesting specific organs and tissues from these creatures, Drazial brews volatile concoctions that grant immense bursts of physical strength, agility, and endurance. Unlike many factional agents stationed in the Blasted Lands, Drazial operates with practical detachment. He holds no official allegiance to either the Alliance or the Horde, choosing instead to trade his alchemical expertise to anyone hardy enough to brave the wasteland and gather the raw ingredients he requires. As long as travelers bring him the organs of the local predators, Drazial is content to keep his cauldrons bubbling.

npc:bloodmage-lynnore.text: Bloodmage Lynnore. Bloodmage Lynnore is a blood elf practitioner of forbidden blood magic camped with her brother Drazial near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands. She assists adventurers by concocting potent alchemical draughts from the organs of local beasts. Camped near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands alongside her brother Drazial, Bloodmage Lynnore is one of the exceptionally rare elven practitioners of blood magic found in the Eastern Kingdoms. Unperturbed by the harsh and corrupting landscape of the Blasted Lands, she studies the latent arcane and vital energies coursing through native beasts. Travelers who bring her the brains and gizzards of local fauna find that she can distill these gruesome reagents into specialized elixirs granting profound enhancements to intellect and spirit.

npc:bluff-runner-windstrider.text: Bluff Runner Windstrider. On Thunder Bluff's mesas, Bluff Runner Windstrider carries urgent messages across the city. He directs Horde travelers toward distant frontiers, including Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries messages across Thunder Bluff's high plateaus. His swift runs keep the city's leaders and visitors informed. He jogs along the rope bridges and pathways, calling out news and carrying dispatches. When outposts across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms need reinforcements, Windstrider calls on passing champions to carry word and answer the call to arms. Bluff Runner Windstrider's messages reach far beyond Mulgore. He sends adventurers north to join Senani Thunderheart's great hunt at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He points seasoned scouts south toward Camp Mojache in Feralas and carries grave warnings about the ongoing undead menace in the Western Plaguelands. His dispatches connect Mulgore's tribal heart to the wider conflicts of the Horde.

npc:braelyn-firehand.text: Braelyn Firehand. At Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand lives among the Horde and draws travelers into a campaign against the night elves of Stonetalon Peak. At Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand is a blood elf living openly among tauren lodges and orcish tents. The retreat’s shamans and chieftains tolerate her, apparently unaware of her true loyalties. She calls herself an observer of the region’s magic and hires passing Horde mercenaries for dangerous work among the crags.

npc:braenna-flintcrag.text: Braenna Flintcrag. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag guides dwarves in the ways of the Holy Light. She trains priests in healing and spiritual discipline, and tells visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Braenna Flintcrag trains priests in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. From the Mystic Ward, she teaches dwarven acolytes the Holy Light's healing arts and defensive wards, preparing them for a dangerous world. Her work tends the spiritual needs of Khaz Modan, amid a city renowned for its forges and warriors.

npc:brainwashed-noble.text: Brainwashed Noble. Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains captive under Defias control. Magical manipulation has stripped him of his will, and he serves the Brotherhood alongside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

npc:brandur-ironhammer.text: Brandur Ironhammer. In Ironforge, Brandur Ironhammer guides young paladins in the Holy Light and sends them across the Alliance. In the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer trains novice paladins in the ways of the Holy Light. He and Tiza Battleforge watch over young dwarven champions as they face the trials of the Tome of Divinity. Tiza has spoken frankly about Brandur’s personal flaws. He works to master his envy and keep the inner purity expected of a warrior of the Light. Brandur connects Ironforge to the wider Alliance brotherhood. Human initiates who come to the dwarven mountain are sent south to Duthorian Rall in the Cathedral of Light. Seasoned paladins are directed to battlegrounds such as Chillwind Camp in the Western Plaguelands. Veteran crusaders are sent to Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker for the demanding trials of the war charger.

npc:brann-bronzebeard.text: Brann Bronzebeard. Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin, who is believed dead, renowned throughout Azeroth as a peerless explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the Explorers' League. Driven by an insatiable curiosity for titan ruins and ancient history, his wanderlust has led him deep into the deadly wastes of Silithus. His field companions in southern Silithus await news of his latest expedition. While his eldest brother Magni rules Ironforge from the throne and Muradin served on battlefield frontlines, Brann took to the open wilds. He was a veteran warrior of the Second War. Yet peacetime turned his formidable constitution toward uncovering the forgotten past. As a leader of the Explorers' League, Brann charted vast swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms—from Elwynn Forest to the untamed jungles of Zul'Gurub—before turning his gaze across the Great Sea to the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

npc:branstock-khalder.text: Branstock Khalder. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder trains dwarven priests in the Holy Light and watches the trogg threat beyond the outpost. At Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder guides aspiring priests through their first prayers and sacred runes. This easy-going dwarf is devoted to the Light, yet keeps watch on the growing trogg threat to the local mountaineers. When a novice has learned enough of the Light, Branstock sends them through Coldridge Pass to Kharanos for further guidance from his superior, Father Maxan Anvol.

npc:brave-moonhorn.text: Brave Moonhorn. Brave Moonhorn is a tauren scout stationed at the top of the Great Lift on the southern border of the Barrens. From this precipice, he keeps watch over the entry to Thousand Needles and alerts travelers to the local dangers ahead. Perched above the sheer drops of Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn stands guard where the northern plains meet the canyonlands. His primary role is keeping watchful eyes on regional threats moving through the canyon floor below, particularly the hostile centaur clans. Anyone looking to descend into the needles often crosses paths with him first, receiving crucial warnings before they step onto the massive platforms of the Great Lift. Beyond the constant threat of roving centaur, Moonhorn harbors deep misgivings about his fellow tauren from the Grimtotem tribe. He cautions traveling Horde allies to keep their distance from them, noting their increasingly erratic and suspicious behavior around Thousand Needles. To ensure the defense of the region, he dispatches couriers to Freewind Post to deliver warnings to Cliffwatcher Longhorn.

npc:brewmeister-bilger.text: Brewmeister Bilger. Brewmeister Bilger waits in Southshore's inn cellar for deliveries from distant lands. The intoxicated dwarf passes his hours tasting potent spirits. Brewmeister Bilger paces the cellar beneath Southshore's inn, nursing hiccups as he seeks the strongest brews Azeroth can offer. Brewmeister Bilger can judge spirits despite his constant stupor. He favors heavy dwarven moonshines and potent southern liquors, and eagerly receives special batches such as the moonshine Foggy MacKreel sends from the Thandol Span.

npc:brock-stoneseeker.text: Brock Stoneseeker. Brock Stoneseeker teaches mining in Thelsamar, in Loch Modan. At Brock's School of Mining and Surveying, he trains novice prospectors to extract ores and minerals. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches miners at Brock's School of Mining and Surveying. Loch Modan's hills hold rich mineral veins, and miners need skill with a pickaxe and an eye for the rock. Brock teaches the basics of finding ore, extracting raw metals, and surveying underground deposits. His lessons help Alliance tradesfolk supply Ironforge's smithies.

npc:bromos-grummner.text: Bromos Grummner. In Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner trains young dwarven paladins in the Holy Light. He teaches steadfast faith and the bond between dwarves and humans in the Knights of the Silver Hand. In Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner welcomes dwarven novices to the discipline of the Holy Light. He teaches young paladins their martial rites and sacred invocations. Beyond combat, Bromos urges unity. The Knights of the Silver Hand bring Ironforge and the human kingdoms of the Alliance together in a shared righteous purpose.

npc:brother-joshua.text: Brother Joshua. In Stormwind, Brother Joshua guides those who come to the Cathedral of Light to learn the ways of the Holy Light. He trains novice priests to heal wounds and strengthen their allies. Brother Joshua waits near the main altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, ready to teach new servants of the faith. A priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he instructs them in healing, protective wards, and the focus needed to commune with the Light. Young human priests beginning their service to the Alliance find one of their first guides in him.

npc:brother-kristoff.text: Brother Kristoff. In Stormwind's Cathedral Square, Brother Kristoff preaches beneath Uther's statue. A human priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he stands outdoors near the great statue of Uther the Lightbringer and seeks practical books for sermons on spiritual strength. Brother Kristoff serves the Church of the Holy Light in Cathedral Square, beneath the statue of Uther the Lightbringer. He works among the citizens and pilgrims who pass through the plaza, rather than remaining within the Cathedral of Light. For sermons such as the Fortitude of the Spirit, he turns to worldly comparisons. In The Stresses of Iron, he finds a way to explain how the mortal soul endures pressure, comparing the Holy Light's gift of inner resolve to the tempered strength of worked metal.

npc:brother-neals.text: Brother Neals. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Neals keeps watch over the food and drink stores. He oversees shipments and samples wine from the local vineyard. Brother Neals keeps Northshire Abbey supplied with food and drink from his rooms in the upper belfry. He follows the grape manifests from the Northshire vineyards and tastes the wine to check its quality. He also watches the shipments arriving from the fields around the valley.

npc:brother-sarno.text: Brother Sarno. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City, Brother Sarno welcomes visitors and worshipers. The human cleric also directs Alliance travelers to Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark needs help reclaiming Gnomeregan. Inside the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, Brother Sarno greets pilgrims and travelers at the entrance. A brother of the Church of the Holy Light, he welcomes those who come seeking prayer, comfort, or guidance. His kind manner puts visitors at ease amid the cathedral’s daily life. Brother Sarno also helps the Alliance beyond the cathedral. When word reached him that Tinkmaster Overspark in Ironforge needed help with his rogue invention, Techbot, in Gnomeregan, Sarno directed capable travelers toward Dun Morogh. His help supports the gnomes displaced from their home.

npc:brother-wilhelm.text: Brother Wilhelm. Behind Goldshire's blacksmith, Brother Wilhelm trains young paladins in the Holy Light. He guides them as they leave Northshire Abbey and take their first steps into Elwynn Forest. Brother Wilhelm trains new paladins behind Goldshire's smithy. Northshire Valley shelters those who begin their path in the Light, but many seek his guidance when they enter the wider forest. He teaches them their sacred duties as they leave the abbey and take up the work of protecting the realm. Brother Wilhelm guides aspiring paladins toward the Tome of Divinity. Its rite teaches initiates the weight of sacrifice and the power of divine redemption. Through it, they test their devotion and learn to wield the Light to resurrect fallen comrades and uphold justice across the Kingdom of Stormwind.

npc:cain-firesong.text: Cain Firesong. At the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, Cain Firesong guides Forsaken mages in the arcane. He trains them in Tirisfal Glades before sending advanced students to the Undercity for deeper study. Cain Firesong teaches traditional arcane arts in Brill, where Forsaken mages begin their studies. Many Forsaken spellcasters turn to shadow or necromancy, but Cain keeps to the arcane. He mentors mages who set out from Deathknell. The Deathguards point visitors to the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern, where Cain can be found. They joke that he arrived too late to get a room. Cain sends capable students onward when they outgrow their first studies in Tirisfal Glades. He directs them to Anastasia Hartwell, a master sorceress who lives in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity.

npc:calvin-montague.text: Calvin Montague. At Deathknell's gate, Calvin Montague preys on newly awakened Forsaken leaving the graveyard, tricking passersby into errands for him. Calvin Montague waits just beyond Deathknell's gates, where the road leads out into Tirisfal Glades. He tries to talk wandering adventurers into carrying his letters, using false pretenses instead of handling his own correspondence or paying a fair courier's fee. Other prominent undead named Montague manage banking interests in the Undercity. Calvin follows a less reputable path, relying on petty schemes and deception.

npc:captain-danuvin.text: Captain Danuvin. At Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin helps hold Westfall's frontier together. He works with the People's Militia, directing volunteers and recruits to patrol roads and drive back Gnolls and outlaws. His orders protect the supply lines and farmlands from hostile hands. Captain Danuvin coordinates patrols from Sentinel Hill's fortified tower. Stormwind's regular garrison has withdrawn, leaving Westfall's defenses badly weakened. He depends on travelers, farmhands, and volunteer fighters to keep some order across the plains. Captain Danuvin focuses on the roads and open lands around Sentinel Hill. Riverpaw Gnolls raid near the central outposts, so he sends patrols to thin their packs and secure the perimeter. His orders help keep marauders and opportunists from surrounding the camp.

npc:captain-rugelfuss.text: Captain Rugelfuss. At Loch Modan’s southern gate, Captain Rugelfuss faces a sudden trogg uprising. The stern dwarven officer organizes the defense of the border. Captain Rugelfuss guards Loch Modan’s southern gateway from the Valley of Kings. With Alliance forces stretched thin across the world, Ironforge depends on veteran officers like him to defend its home territories. He sets aside military ceremony and turns his attention to the danger at the border. Troggs are surging into the highlands from ancient caverns. They have overwhelmed outlying dwarven patrols and built fortified footholds nearby. Rugelfuss calls on capable travelers to thin their ranks and drive them back from the roadway, defending the King’s lands.

npc:captain-shatterskull.text: Captain Shatterskull. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Captain Shatterskull commands the Horde's northern border defense. A seasoned orc commander, he coordinates efforts to repel night elf forces contesting the border near Warsong Gulch. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Captain Shatterskull guards the Horde's foothold at the edge of Ashenvale. He works beside fellow officers such as Kadrak against night elf sentinels and Silverwing forces seeking to reclaim the borderlands. The struggle over Ashenvale's timber and ancient lands keeps the Barrens frontier under constant threat.

npc:captain-thalo-thas-brightsun.text: Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun. At Ratchet's docks, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun keeps a cordial face toward Alliance travelers. The privateer serves the Steamwheedle Cartel and resents the Theramore forces at Northwatch Hold for firing on his vessels. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers from Ratchet's docks under the Steamwheedle Cartel's banner. Ratchet welcomes merchants of every flag if they bring coin, but danger shadows trade along the Barrens coast. Northwatch Hold lies just south of the port, where its heavy cannons threaten neutral sea lanes. Brightsun stays cordial toward visiting travelers, yet the garrison's attacks on his fleet have tried his patience. An open assault on Northwatch Hold could endanger Ratchet's neutrality, so Brightsun cannot send his fleet against the fort. He turns instead to capable Horde mercenaries to settle the score. Their strikes aim to silence the cannons and free his captured crew. By using Horde auxiliaries, Brightsun protects his shipping interests without provoking direct Alliance retaliation against the cartel or entering the conflict openly.

npc:captured-mountaineer.text: Captured Mountaineer. In Brill, a captured Ironforge Mountaineer is held beneath the Gallows' End Tavern. The Forsaken keep him bound for the Royal Apothecary Society's experiments. Beneath the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, an Ironforge Mountaineer is held far from Khaz Modan. While patrons drink above, the Royal Apothecary Society uses him to test its concoctions. Apothecary Johaan and his peers measure their developing plague against living Alliance bodies, testing how swiftly and painfully their toxins kill.

npc:captured-scarlet-zealot.text: Captured Scarlet Zealot. Beneath Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, a Scarlet Zealot is held captive. Forsaken apothecaries use him to test concoctions for the Royal Apothecary Society. Beneath Gallows' End Tavern, a Scarlet Crusade zealot remains chained and defiant. His unyielding faith reflects his order, and he sees the undead around him as abominations. He calls on the Light to shield him from the foul creatures holding him. The Forsaken did not capture him out of mercy. As a living human, he is valuable test material for Apothecary Johaan, who uses him to measure the lethality of experimental plagues and toxins under development.

npc:caretaker-folsom.text: Caretaker Folsom. Along Stormwind’s Canals near the Park, Caretaker Folsom tends the remains of a noble household. He once oversaw the Flintridge estate; now he sells what survived its bloody end. Folsom followed his father into a life of service as caretaker of the Flintridge estate. That life ended with the massacre of the household. The manor stood abandoned, and its remaining funds eventually ran out. Left to watch over what remained, Folsom now sends the family's surviving heirlooms and possessions to auction.

npc:carolai-anise.text: Carolai Anise. In Brill, Carolai Anise teaches alchemy while her experiments make the guards uneasy. Carolai Anise pursues alchemy in Brill, where she teaches novice alchemists. Many Forsaken researchers work under the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate, but Carolai makes her own strange brews inside the settlement. Her unpredictable experiments and smoking retorts are well known. The Deathguards watching Brill openly grumble that she seems bent on blowing up her own house.

npc:cazul.text: Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, Cazul guides young warlocks toward greater command of demons. Blind and ancient, he remains a keeper of old orc warlock traditions. Cazul waits in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar, where rising warlocks seek his counsel. Blind though he is, he senses the currents of the Twisting Nether and hears the whispers of demons. Those who want to master their craft and bind more dangerous servitors are often sent to him. His sight is gone, but his arcane power remains.

npc:cerellean-whiteclaw.text: Cerellean Whiteclaw. Near Auberdine’s docks and inn in Darkshore, Cerellean Whiteclaw rests with grief for a lost love. The Sundering’s memory haunts him, and he struggles to bring that restless spirit peace. Before the War of the Ancients, Cerellean Whiteclaw shared his life with Anaya Dawnrunner. Ten thousand years ago, the demonic invasion shattered ancient Kalimdor, and Anaya died in the destruction of her city, Ameth'Aran. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Malfurion Stormrage into the long druidic slumber. The Emerald Dream brought little relief from his memories. When he awoke millennia later, he wandered Darkshore in grief and found Anaya's ghost still bound to the stones where she fell.

npc:chef-breanna.text: Chef Breanna. In Lakeshire, Chef Breanna feeds the Stormwind soldiers guarding the Redridge Mountains. She leads the town's kitchen and uses hearty local ingredients to keep the defenders on their feet. Chef Breanna works from a restaurant house in northwestern Lakeshire with her assistants, Crystal Boughman and Gretchen Vogel. She is responsible for feeding the entire local battalion. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs besiege the town, and Stormwind's understaffed garrison must stay strong. Her signature Redridge Goulash uses wild game and beasts from the surrounding ridges to feed the weary guards.

npc:chef-grual.text: Chef Grual. In Darkshire, Chef Grual keeps the Scarlet Raven Tavern's kitchen working. He feeds the Night Watch and weary travelers, though some ingredients raise eyebrows. Darkshire's cook works with scarce supplies. Highwaymen, wolves, and undead harass the roads from Westfall and Stormwind, leaving fresh provisions hard to find. Grual makes do with what the wilderness offers. He cooks wolf flank and meat scavenged by local adventurers, using whatever reaches his kitchen.

npc:chef-jessen.text: Chef Jessen. In Southshore, Chef Jessen works to feed the town amid constant border tensions. He is best known for his famous turtle bisque. Chef Jessen supplies meat and provisions in Southshore, in the southern Hillsbrad Foothills, for locals and visiting Alliance soldiers. He is a skilled cook. Before plague and war disrupted northern Lordaeron, he often traveled north past Dalaran to the shores of Lordamere Lake. There he gathered meat from native snapjaw turtles to make his prized, hearty Soothing Turtle Bisque. He will share the recipe with travelers who help him gather its ingredients.

npc:chief-archaeologist-greywhisker.text: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker gathers reports from the coast. The Ironforge dwarf works outside the Temple of the Moon, where he coordinates the Explorers' League's research and tracks colleagues in Darkshore. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker works outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, far from his home in Ironforge. He represents the Explorers' League, which sent him across the sea to Kalimdor for fieldwork. There, he speaks with night elf scholars such as Tarelvir and seeks knowledge of the ancient lands. In Ironforge, his lectures covered ancient lore and primordial beings, including the Wild God Agamaggan. Now he hopes to learn what the night elves' ancestral lands hold. In Kalimdor, Greywhisker oversees dwarven excavations and follows expeditions searching ancient coastal ruins. He depends on travelers to carry messages to prospectors across the sea in Darkshore. Field research in unexplored lands is perilous, and he waits anxiously for reports from the dig sites, hoping his colleagues are safe among the ruins.

npc:christoph-jeffcoat.text: Christoph Jeffcoat. At Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat supplies the Forsaken with goods for trade and travel. His wares help crafters and travelers in Hillsbrad Foothills, where the Alliance and the Syndicate contest the land. Christoph Jeffcoat tends to the practical needs of Tarren Mill, the Forsaken stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills. He sells reagents, tools, threads, and spices to soldiers and traveling artisans. His goods include the spices used in turtle bisque, rare schematics, and alchemical vials. Horde forces passing through southern Lordaeron rely on such supplies as they face Southshore and the dangers of the region.

npc:chronormu.text: Chronormu. Chronormu, who goes by the mortal name Chromie, is a bronze dragon disguised as an energetic female gnome. Tasked with safeguarding the flow of time on Azeroth, she often works directly with mortals rather than observing from afar. In the Western Plaguelands, she quietly intervenes in the tragic aftermath of the Third War to right disrupted temporal threads. Though she appears to mortals as an eccentric and cheerful gnome named Chromie, Chronormu is a member of the bronze dragonflight serving under the Timeless One, Nozdormu. Bronze dragons are charged by the titans with guarding history and correcting disruptions in the timeways. In the form of a female gnome, she walks beside mortals as an approachable, optimistic peer. Chronormu has taken up residence within the ruined ruins of Lordaeron, particularly watching the devastated Western Plaguelands. The catastrophic downfall of the kingdom and the spread of the Scourge tore deeply into the region's history, leaving temporal anomalies and trapped remnants. Working discreetly from places like the ruins of Andorhal, she enlists mortal adventurers to mend tangled timelines and investigate disturbances without revealing the full terrifying majesty of the dragonflight unless necessary.

npc:clarice-foster.text: Clarice Foster. In the Pools of Vision, Clarice Foster lives among tauren seers and mystics. Far from Lordaeron, the Forsaken woman spends her days in contemplation beneath the bluffs of Mulgore. Most Forsaken remain in Lordaeron, rebuilding their kingdom beneath the Undercity. Clarice Foster has traveled to the heart of tauren lands in Kalimdor. She lives in the cavernous Pools of Vision beneath the mesa of Thunder Bluff, among Forsaken apothecaries and tauren shamans who study the spiritual and elemental mysteries of the earth.

npc:colonel-kurzen.text: Colonel Kurzen. Colonel Conrad Kurzen was once a decorated and noble officer of the Stormwind Army, sent to lead an expedition into northern Stranglethorn Vale. After descending into sudden madness and tyranny, he turned his force into a rogue jungle militia operating out of an armed compound. Today, his former subordinates at the nearby Rebel Camp actively seek his death to end his reign of terror. Before his downfall, Colonel Conrad Kurzen was regarded in Stormwind as an exceptionally capable and noble officer. Trusted by the kingdom's leadership, he was granted command of an expeditionary unit dispatched south into the dense jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. However, deep within the humid wilds, Kurzen began to exhibit erratic behavior and extreme megalomania, declaring absolute sovereignty over the surrounding wilderness and abandoning his allegiance to Stormwind. Kurzen's sudden transformation divided his ranks. While many soldiers succumbed to blind loyalty or twisted zealotry, others grew appalled by his madness and brutality—including his act of throwing Emerine Junis into the compound's prison simply for spurning his advances. Led by Lieutenant Doren, a group of conscience-stricken soldiers broke away to establish the Rebel Camp along the northern road. These loyalist defectors now wage a desperate war against Kurzen to stop his rampaging force.

npc:commander-mar-alith.text: Commander Mar'alith. Commander Mar'alith is the stalwart night elf military commander directing the Cenarion Circle's vanguard at Cenarion Hold in Silithus. Clad in heavy armor and wielding a grand glaive, he coordinates the martial resistance against the silithid swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists. Beneath his resolute leadership lies a deep personal sorrow regarding the mysterious fate of his beloved wife, Natalia. Stationed at the heart of Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith bears the tremendous responsibility of safeguarding the Circle's desert bastion. While the druids unravel the ancient ecological and cosmic anomalies of Silithus, Mar'alith handles the grim, practical necessities of war. He oversees tactical strikes against the bustling silithid hives of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal, ensuring that the relentless insectoid incursions do not overwhelm the expedition's central foothold. Despite his stern military bearing, Mar'alith is visibly strained by a harrowing personal tragedy. His beloved wife, Natalia Mar'alith, ventured into the shifting sands on an assignment for the Circle and failed to return. Caught between his duty to the Cenarion expedition and agonizing grief, the commander appears increasingly distracted, clinging to whatever hope remains while desperate for news of what truly became of her in the wastes.

npc:councilman-millstipe.text: Councilman Millstipe. Darkshire's council grows bitter as Stormwind overrides its judgment. Councilman Millstipe lives in the town hall and wants justice for Duskwood's people. Darkshire faces undead and attacks from ferocious beasts, while its council struggles against Stormwind City's bureaucracy. Councilman Millstipe reflects the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. The notorious grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's leaders sentenced Ward to death, but Stormwind's House of Nobles commuted the execution and locked him away in the Stormwind Stockade.

npc:count-remington-ridgewell.text: Count Remington Ridgewell. In Stormwind Keep, Count Remington Ridgewell tends a collection fit for a noble’s pride. A wealthy human in the House of Nobles, he gathers rare artifacts, heirlooms, and fine art. Count Remington Ridgewell favors antiquities over military campaigns or local uprisings. His family’s personal museum holds jewelry and artifacts, and he spends his wealth gathering relics from fallen civilizations and houses across Azeroth. To fill his gallery, he finances adventurers and sends field agents such as Mayara Brightwing to retrieve rare objects from dangerous ruins, from Alterac’s mountain redoubts to the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes.

npc:crane-operator-bigglefuzz.text: Crane Operator Bigglefuzz. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz is a goblin dockhand working the heavy machinery at the port of Ratchet. After an overloaded crane mishap scattered cargo across the docks, he finds himself desperate to recover a valuable stolen bottle before his superiors notice. Like many goblin dockworkers, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz prioritized efficiency and haste over basic safety margins. While attempting to hoist an excessively heavy haul from a merchant vessel, his crane buckled, sending crates crashing down across the Ratchet wharves. In the ensuing chaos, opportunistic scoundrels swept in, leaving Bigglefuzz to scramble to clean up the mess and salvage the most precious goods before Gazlowe or the local port masters dock his pay. The worst casualty of the accident was not the broken wood, but a crate containing rare ninety-nine-year-old port. Before Bigglefuzz could secure the spill, an elusive vagrant named Mad Magglish snatched a bottle and fled into hiding, threatening to leave Bigglefuzz answering for an irreplaceable loss.

npc:craven-drok.text: Craven Drok. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok keeps to the Cleft of Shadow and seeks travelers for a delicate matter. He wants them to consider how the Alliance sees the Horde. Craven Drok avoids Orgrimmar's sunlit avenues and wanders the winding paths beneath the city. The Cleft of Shadow draws warlocks, rogues, and practitioners of less honorable trades. Drok keeps out of sight and hires passersby to handle discreet errands, including one about the Horde's standing with the Alliance.

npc:cyrus-therepentous.text: Cyrus Therepentous. Cyrus Therepentous is a formidable black dragonspawn residing in the cavernous depths of Slither Rock in the Burning Steppes. Rather than immediately striking down intruders, he tests daring mortals to see if they possess the strength to serve the purposes of the Black dragonflight. Secluded inside a cavern at Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous oversees the volcanic crags of the Burning Steppes. Like many of his kind, he views mortal travelers with immense condescension, declaring that only fools would disturb his lair. Yet beneath his ferocious exterior lies a cold calculation: rather than consuming every trespasser on sight, he offers them a lethal challenge against his minions, willing to exploit those resilient enough to survive the trials of flame.

npc:darcy-parker.text: Darcy. At the Lakeshire Inn, Darcy keeps the town's defenders fed and spirits up. She serves drinks and warm meals, with a special care for Guard Parker. Darcy keeps the Lakeshire Inn's counter working through long days and nights. The town's militia come there for food and drink while gnolls and Blackrock orcs keep Lakeshire under pressure. Darcy also looks out for guards posted around town. She asks travelers to carry hot meals and friendly errands to defenders stationed along the borders. Darcy pays special attention to Guard Parker, who patrols the roads near Three Corners. She thinks he works too hard on an empty stomach and often sends travelers with lunch for him. Darcy watches Martie Jainrose closely, believing her to be jealous and a rival for Parker's favor. Their feelings mingle with the work of defending Lakeshire.

npc:dark-cleric-beryl.text: Dark Cleric Beryl. In Brill, Dark Cleric Beryl guides newly awakened undead priests in the shadows. Stationed in the Gallows' End Tavern, he teaches them shadow magic and helps them adapt to their unholy existence under the Dark Lady. Dark Cleric Beryl mentors new Forsaken priests upstairs in Brill's Gallows' End Tavern. He teaches that a priest's power comes from darkness and shadow, yet mastering the dark also requires knowing the light. Newly risen priests turn their focus to shadow and the dark arts under his guidance. Their early trials include crafting their Garments of Darkness and proving their dedication to this new path.

npc:darkmaster-gandling.text: Darkmaster Gandling. Darkmaster Gandling is the mortal headmaster of Scholomance, overseeing the instruction and training of necromancers for the Cult of the Damned. Operating from the depths of the ruined Keep of Caer Darrow, he serves the Scourge by orchestrating gruesome magical experiments upon the living and dead alike. Within the dark halls beneath Caer Darrow, Darkmaster Gandling governs Scholomance, the premier academy for the Scourge's aspiring necromancers. A living human serving the Cult of the Damned, Gandling worked alongside the lich Ras Frostwhisper to orchestrate atrocities against countless innocent captives taken from the surrounding lands. Students who enter his classrooms are instructed in plague brewing, reanimation, and flesh sculpting. Residing deep within the Headmaster's Study, Gandling commands the dark relics and spirits trapped inside the ancient school. He wields devastating arcane and shadow magic in conjunction with forbidden necromantic arts, cursing intruders and hurling them through shadow portals into the sealed chambers surrounding his study, where they must fight alone against the risen dead while Gandling shields himself from harm.

npc:darn-talongrip.text: Darn Talongrip. Near Malaka'jin, Darn Talongrip watches the Stonetalon frontier. The orc scout tracks threats in the crags and carries word between forward outposts and Horde commanders. Darn Talongrip watches the rugged climbs into Stonetalon from the southern Barrens. At Malaka'jin, he directs recruits toward the Horde's new fronts in Ashenvale. Travelers climbing into the contested peaks can reach the Horde through his post. From Malaka'jin, Darn sends messages and reports from the front to commanders such as Kadrak, at the watch tower in the northern Barrens. Encampments scattered through the mountains face constant pressure, and Darn keeps the Horde vanguard informed as a sentry and courier.

npc:daryl-the-youngling.text: Daryl the Youngling. At Farstrider Lodge, Daryl the Youngling tests his hunting skill among veteran dwarven trackers. He challenges travelers to prove their marksmanship against Loch Modan's beasts. Farstrider Lodge shelters dwarven mountaineers, trackers, and seasoned outdoorsmen who watch over Loch Modan's wilderness. Daryl is a young human trying to earn a place among them. He measures his hunting instincts against other travelers, challenging them to hunt the tough wild boars and beasts that roam the crags and lakeshore.

npc:dashel-stonefist.text: Dashel Stonefist. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known for his quick temper and heavy hands. The dwarf called Fist keeps to Stormwind City's rougher alleys, where dangerous connections draw the attention of covert investigators. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist is known as Fist for the street fights that have earned him the name. Locals and city guards see a drunken, combative dwarf ready to throw a punch outside a tavern. His place in the district puts him at the nexus of Stormwind's underworld, where smugglers, cutpurses, and political agitators trade coin and rumors beyond the eyes of Cathedral Square.

npc:david-trias.text: David Trias. In Deathknell, David Trias trains the newly awakened Forsaken. He teaches stealth and bladecraft so they can serve Queen Sylvanas and the Forsaken. David Trias trains newly risen undead among Deathknell’s tombstones and ruins. He seeks those with a talent for killing unseen. For the fledgling Forsaken, survival calls for more than strength at arms; it calls for precise strikes from the dark. Trias deciphers orders and teaches initiates to wield daggers, hide their movements, and use their reanimated reflexes with lethal precision against the living and the Scourge.

npc:dawnwatcher-selgorm.text: Dawnwatcher Selgorm. At the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Selgorm watches for threats across northern Kalimdor. The human serves the Argent Dawn as an observer and liaison in the night elven capital, tracking reports of shadowy cult activity and dark powers stirring nearby. Dawnwatcher Selgorm keeps watch in Darnassus for the Argent Dawn. The order's fight against the undead Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands does not end its vigilance elsewhere. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, Selgorm gathers reports of emerging threats in Kalimdor's wilds. He connects the night elves with the wider effort against ancient evil and seeks Alliance travelers able to strike at cultists and dark powers before their influence spreads.

npc:dawnwatcher-shaedlass.text: Dawnwatcher Shaedlass. In Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass keeps watch for the Argent Dawn across Kalimdor. From the Craftsmen's Terrace, he seeks word of his fellow order members sent to scout hostile lands. The Argent Dawn fights the Scourge in the Eastern Plaguelands, yet its watch reaches beyond Lordaeron. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass keeps the order's interests in Kalimdor from the night elf capital of Darnassus. At his post on the Craftsmen's Terrace, he follows covert expeditions against dark cults and corrupting powers that threaten the wider world.

npc:dazalar.text: Dazalar. In Dolanaar, Dazalar trains young night elf hunters for the wilds of Teldrassil. He teaches them to aim true and form bonds with the beasts of the great boughs. Dazalar trains young hunters in Dolanaar before they venture beyond Shadowglen. Night elf rangers and sentinels patrol the wilderness, and he teaches newcomers the patience and discipline needed to protect Teldrassil's fragile ecosystem. Dazalar teaches hunters to tame and care for beasts. The Kaldorei seek a pact with forest predators such as nightsabers, owls, and strigid hunters, training them to fight beside their companions with respect rather than force.

npc:deathguard-bartholomew.text: Deathguard Bartholomew. In Brill, Deathguard Bartholomew keeps watch over the town and helps travelers find their way. He helps keep order among the Forsaken defenders of Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Bartholomew keeps watch in Brill, part of the Forsaken guard defending Tirisfal Glades. Like other Deathguards, he protects reclaimed land from the lingering Scourge, fanatical Scarlet Crusaders, and other threats to Lady Sylvanas's domain. He also guides travelers around the town and helps keep order among the newly risen.

npc:deathguard-burgess.text: Deathguard Burgess. In Brill, Deathguard Burgess keeps watch over the town for the Forsaken. He guards the settlement and points travelers toward the services they need. North of the Undercity, Deathguard Burgess guards Brill against the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade. Like other Deathguards in Tirisfal Glades, he guides arriving Forsaken to local tradesfolk, class trainers, and civic services, helping keep the vulnerable outpost running.

npc:deathguard-humbert.text: Deathguard Humbert. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Humbert watches the Alliance presence in Hillsbrad. The Forsaken sentry has lost his military gear to dwarves from Dun Garok. Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok from a hidden camp for High Executor Darthalia. One morning, he left to gather firewood. Dwarven scouts from Dun Garok took his prized sword and other equipment while he was away. Now he must recover his arms and save his pride before high command learns what happened.

npc:deathguard-linnea.text: Deathguard Linnea. At a roadside post in southeastern Tirisfal, Deathguard Linnea watches the roads between Brill and the eastern borders. Her unit guards against the Scarlet Crusade and the lingering Scourge, with passing travelers sometimes helping on patrol. Deathguard Linnea guards a fortified post southeast of Brill. The Forsaken defend their young realm against Scarlet Crusade infiltrators and Scourge still prowling the wilderness. Linnea and her fellow guards patrol the road and coordinate reports with Magistrate Sevren in Brill. Their watch keeps the eastern road toward the Bulwark secure.

npc:deathguard-samsa.text: Deathguard Samsa. In Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa watches the tense frontier and sends travelers against threats near the settlement. Deathguard Samsa keeps watch in Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken hold their ground in the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. Horde sentries face pressure from Alliance outposts such as Southshore and from savage local wildlife. Samsa guards the perimeter and directs capable adventurers against threats before they endanger the encampment.

npc:deathguard-simmer.text: Deathguard Simmer. At Deathknell’s edge, Deathguard Simmer sizes up newly risen Forsaken. He sends them west to raid a human pumpkin farm patrolled by the Scarlet Crusade, gathering reagents Brill’s apothecaries need. Deathguard Simmer guards the ground just outside Deathknell, where the Forsaken hold the line between their haven and Tirisfal Glades. Living humans roam the region, including the fanatical Scarlet Crusade, who see all undead as abominations to purge with fire and blade. Simmer tests newly risen Forsaken by sending them west to Solliden Farmstead. Scarlet Crusade soldiers patrol from a nearby tower. The recruits must steal ten pumpkins and carry them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

npc:deathstalker-faerleia.text: Deathstalker Faerleia. Deep inside Pyrewood Village, Deathstalker Faerleia works against its leaders. From the town hall, she directs covert strikes against the Pyrewood Council, the puppets Arugal uses to rule the village.

npc:deathstalker-lesh.text: Deathstalker Lesh. At Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh watches the human farms in the Hillsbrad Foothills. She serves High Executor Darthalia and gauges when the Forsaken should strike. From Southpoint Tower, Deathstalker Lesh watches the human farmers and town militia in the nearby Hillsbrad Fields. The tower stands on the southern road through the Hillsbrad Foothills. Lesh belongs to the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken's covert network of scouts, spies, and assassins. She tracks enemy movements and numbers for High Executor Darthalia in Tarren Mill. When the moment is right, Lesh sends Darthalia a coded message: “The raven's cry from the west doth beckon.” The words signal that Hillsbrad is ripe for the Forsaken's attack.

npc:deathstalker-rane-yorick.text: Rane Yorick. At a farmhouse in Silverpine, Deathstalker Rane Yorick and her brother Quinn are cut off from the Sepulcher. Sent to scout the northern farms, they must get word to High Executor Hadrec. Across Lordaeron, the Deathstalkers are Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades. Agents like Rane Yorick watch the wilds from hidden posts for threats to Forsaken rule. Rane and her brother Quinn were sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest. Feral dangers closed around them, turning their covert work into a fight to survive.

npc:deathstalker-vincent.text: Deathstalker Vincent. Inside Shadowfang Keep, Deathstalker Vincent lies slain by Arugal. The Forsaken scout entered the stronghold with Deathstalker Adamant to learn its defenses, but the mission ended before the Forsaken could attack. The Deathstalkers needed to learn Shadowfang Keep’s layout before the Forsaken could assault it. Vincent and Adamant slipped past the barricades into the fortress. Their mission failed: Adamant was captured and locked in a dungeon cell, while Vincent was brought before the keep’s master. Vincent refused to serve Arugal or yield to him. The mage executed him, leaving his body on the stone floor.

npc:deathwing.text: Deathwing. Deathwing the Destroyer, once known as Neltharion the Earth-Warder, is the fallen Dragon Aspect of the black dragonflight. Driven mad by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he turned against the other Aspects and plunged the world into fire and turmoil. Though defeated near Grim Batol after the Second War and believed slain or hidden away, the terror of his legacy still haunts the deep places of Azeroth. Before he was known as the Destroyer, Neltharion was granted dominion over the earth and the subterranean vaults of Azeroth by the titan pantheon. Yet dwelling so close to the world's deepest chambers exposed him to the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods. During the ancient War of the Ancients, the madness took complete hold. He deceived the other Dragon Aspects into imbuing a golden disc, the Dragon Soul, with portions of their essence under the guise of halting the Burning Legion, only to turn the terrible weapon against his allies and unleash catastrophic devastation. In the present year, the mortal kingdoms largely assume Deathwing was destroyed or permanently driven from the world. However, the black dragonflight remains an active scourge across Azeroth. Led by his cunning brood, including his daughter Onyxia and son Nefarian, black drakes manipulate the politics of mortals and terrorize the landscape from mountain lairs. The scars of the black Aspect's ancient treachery run deep, and travelers wandering through craggy wastelands and deep subterranean tunnels still fear the stirring of the Great Dragon.

npc:deino.text: Deino. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Deino trains Horde mages in the arcane arts. She teaches spellcasters to master arcane and elemental forces, and sends seasoned mages across Kalimdor to study ancient magic and seek remote tutors. Deino trains Horde mages in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Totems, huts, and quiet waters surround the raised platforms where she teaches. Troll spellcasters balance spiritual reverence with arcane mastery, a path Deino shares with fellow instructors Enyo and Pephredo. Deino sends promising mages beyond Durotar to study arcane mysteries. In Ashenvale's corrupted wilds, they gather tainted Waters of Xavian and enchanted hair from the Laughing Sisters.
