When a student's power outgrows Orgrimmar's instruction, Deino directs them to remote masters, including Tabetha, a hermit sorceress in Dustwallow's swamplands.

npc:demisette-cloyce.text: Demisette Cloyce. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Demisette Cloyce teaches warlocks beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. She guides students in fel magic and sends those ready for more toward other summoners. Warlocks gather in the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, while the city's authorities uphold order and the Holy Light. Demisette Cloyce lives in the catacombs below, teaching those willing to study forbidden arts. She warns that dark energies corrupt only those without the discipline to master them. Demisette guides warlocks beyond Stormwind when they have gained enough mastery. She connects them with summoners such as Menara Voidrender in the Barrens, where they can seek potent artifacts and learn to bind formidable fel steeds.

npc:deputy-feldon.text: Deputy Feldon. South of the Great Lakeshire Bridge, Deputy Feldon watches the road into Lakeshire. Gnoll packs are creeping toward the town, and he keeps a nervous vigil. Deputy Feldon stands watch south of the Lakeshire bridge, guarding a road needed for trade and travel. Blackrock orcs press from the north while gnoll packs overrun the southern hills, stretching the town guard thin. Feldon cannot leave his post without weakening Lakeshire's perimeter. He depends on passing adventurers to drive back the gnolls before they cut the town off.

npc:deputy-rainer.text: Deputy Rainer. Outside Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer holds Elwynn's western border. The Stormwind Army officer faces gnolls and bandits from Westfall, coordinating local defenses while reinforcements fail to arrive. At Westbrook Garrison, Elwynn Forest's westernmost post, the road crosses into Westfall. Political paralysis in Stormwind City leaves much of the army abroad or caught in bureaucracy, and border posts like this one lack troops. Deputy Rainer organizes the defense from outside the tower with the few forces at hand. Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves threaten the local roads, so he depends on passing travelers and mercenary adventurers to keep the forest trails secure. Deputy Rainer watches for the Riverpaw pack and warns travelers about Hogger, the infamous gnoll chieftain. He also carries word of the troubled lands beyond the river. The chaos at Elwynn's border begins in Westfall's lawless farmlands, so he sends capable volunteers across the border toward Gryan Stoutmantle and the struggling People's Militia.

npc:dirge-quikcleave.text: Dirge Quikcleave. Inside Gadgetzan's inn, Dirge Quikcleave holds court as a goblin culinary master and vendor. His inventive dishes are renowned across Azeroth, and seasoned chefs come to him to master artisan cooking. In dusty Gadgetzan, Dirge Quikcleave serves drinks and meat to travelers parched by the Tanaris sands. Though his kitchen is in a frontier tavern, he claims to be Azeroth's greatest living culinary artist. Cooking trainers in cities send their most promising students to him when ordinary lessons are spent. Dirge's demanding recipes call for unusual ingredients, from giant clam meat and eggs for his Clamlette creations to exotic beasts from distant shores. Dirge Quikcleave pairs a gourmand's bravado with a goblin's eye for business. Across Kalimdor, he keeps contacts with eccentric figures and seeks out dangerous culinary ventures. Those who bring him fierce beast cuts, such as meat from the monstrous chimaeroks of Feralas's Isle of Dread, can receive hearty recipes fit to sustain champions on perilous journeys. They must not ask too many questions about Dirge's private dealings.

npc:doan-karhan.text: Doan Karhan. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan studies the Burning Legion’s demonic artifacts. A human scholar and practitioner of the dark arts, he lives alone to pursue his research, especially into the enigmatic Orb of Soran'ruk. Doan Karhan keeps a solitary camp in the southern Barrens, far from the Alliance’s civilized bastions. He withdrew into the wilderness to study dangerous demonic relics without disturbance. He knows much about powerful fel vessels, possesses the Orb of Zargain, and is absorbed by the legendary Orb of Soran'ruk. Warlocks seeking knowledge of artifact crafting and dark rituals often come to him.

npc:doctor-gregory-victor.text: Doctor Gregory Victor. Doctor Gregory Victor is a Forsaken surgeon stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Renowned as the premier trauma physician within the Horde, he evaluates aspiring medics seeking to master advanced triage and battlefield first aid. His cold, clinical efficiency keeps frontline warriors stitched together amidst bitter regional conflicts. While many view Forsaken apothecaries with suspicion, Doctor Gregory Victor serves the Horde through practical battlefield surgery rather than blighted alchemy. Stationed deep within the contested Arathi Highlands at Hammerfall, he operates on soldiers battered by Syndicate brigands, Boulderfist ogres, and Alliance forces. His station doubles as the primary proving ground for Horde field medics, demanding ruthless efficiency and prioritizing critical patients under intense pressure.

npc:doctor-gustaf-vanhowzen.text: Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen. At Foothold Citadel, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen directs Theramore's medical care. He trains healers and tests seasoned medics in field triage and bandage work. On the ground floor of Foothold Citadel, Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen oversees medical care for Lady Jaina Proudmoore's forces and trains Theramore's frontline healers. Dustwallow Marsh makes their work harsh, and VanHowzen demands skill under pressure. He puts experienced medics through a demanding triage test, where they must judge which wounds need care first.

npc:donova-snowden.text: Donova Snowden. Donova Snowden is an intrepid dwarven researcher encamped alongside the thermal waters near Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring. Despite the bitter cold and hostile wildlife, she studies the strange thermal activity of the region and monitors the increasingly corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. While most travelers stick to the safety of Everlook, Donova Snowden has chosen to camp in the freezing wilderness near the Frostfire Hot Springs. She spends her days investigating the curious geothermic anomalies bubbling up through the permafrost, as well as the dark influences encroaching upon Winterspring's native wildlife. Practical and determined, she enlists passing adventurers of both the Alliance and the Horde to gather samples and help curb local threats.

npc:donyal-tovald.text: Donyal Tovald. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s historical works. Under an initiative sponsored by young King Anduin Wrynn, he preserves and copies books for wider public use. Donyal Tovald tends the Royal Library’s collection in Stormwind Keep. The library holds historical accounts, scrolls, and scholarly volumes, chiefly for the nobility and royal court. Young King Anduin Wrynn has sponsored an effort to make that knowledge more accessible to ordinary citizens. Tovald preserves and copies the texts, helping keep the Alliance’s lessons and triumphs recorded amid the kingdom’s political troubles.

npc:doomsayer-wiserunner.text: Seer Wiserunner. At his cave northwest of Bloodhoof Village, Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through sacred rites. The respected elder helps them seek spiritual wisdom in Mulgore. Seer Wiserunner guides young tauren through their ancestral rites. After their first trials of strength and vision, they seek his counsel. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and teaches them how to honor their forebears. His wisdom helps bind Mulgore’s scattered nomadic tribes into one community.

npc:doras.text: Doras. Above Orgrimmar, Doras directs the Horde's wind riders across Kalimdor. He oversees the capital's wyverns, sending couriers, scouts, and travelers on their way. Doras tends the wind riders on a wooden platform above the Valley of Strength. The Horde settled in Durotar, and these clever, leathery-winged beasts became its chief means of communication and travel across Kalimdor. Doras pairs resting mounts with riders and sees that important messages and reinforcements reach distant outposts. Their routes reach the Crossroads, Thunder Bluff, and settlements deep in Ashenvale or Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:doren.text: Doren. Lieutenant Doren commands the Rebel Camp nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Once an officer under Colonel Kurzen, Doren led a mutiny after his superior and fellow expeditionaries descended into madness. Now, he directs a guerrilla resistance determined to uncover the source of the affliction and eliminate Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren initially deployed to Stranglethorn Vale under the banner of Stormwind and the command of Colonel Kurzen. The expedition was meant to establish a foothold in the wild southern jungle, but it quickly soured as Kurzen and his inner circle succumbed to an erratic, violent insanity. Refusing to abandon their sanity or their honor, Doren and a cadre of loyalists broke rank. They fled north and carved out the Rebel Camp along the road, choosing defection over servitude to a madman.

npc:drum-fel.text: Drum Fel. At Hammerfall, Drum Fel directs the Horde’s fight to hold Arathi against trolls, ogres, and human remnants. With his wife Korin, he works to secure a lasting foothold for the Horde in the region. Drum Fel commands Hammerfall’s defenses and the Horde’s push into Arathi. From the fortified refuge, he faces rival factions on every side. The Witherbark forest trolls and the Boulderfist ogres hold Boulder'gor and Boulderfist Hall. Drum knows Hammerfall cannot thrive by keeping to itself; its neighbors’ strength must be broken. He sends veteran champions into hostile territory to disrupt these threats before they can strike the Horde encampment.

npc:drusilla-la-salle.text: Drusilla La Salle. Outside Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle teaches warlocks in the graveyard. The human trainer works beyond the Holy Order’s reach, guiding new spellcasters in shadow and summoning. When forbidden knowledge leaves the abbey, she moves to claim it. Drusilla La Salle teaches novice warlocks among the headstones outside Northshire Abbey. Paladins and priests practice beneath the abbey’s stained glass, while warlocks keep to society’s edges because demonology and fel magic are taboo in Stormwind. Recruits receive tainted correspondence before Drusilla shows them how to wield shadow power without drawing the abbey authorities’ immediate anger.

npc:duke-hydraxis.text: Duke Hydraxis. Duke Hydraxis is a noble water elemental commanding the Hydraxian Waterlords from a remote, wave-battered islet off the coast of Azshara. Pledged to Neptulon the Tidehunter, he rallies mortal adventurers to strike against his ancient elemental rivals, particularly Ragnaros the Firelord. Perched on a solitary rock northeast of the Ravencrest Monument in Azshara, Duke Hydraxis serves as the primary emissary of the Hydraxian Waterlords. While most elementals bound to Azeroth are hostile and chaotic, Hydraxis acts with measured purpose. As a devoted vassal of Neptulon the Tidehunter, he considers water the purest and most essential of the primal forces. He watches the rising turmoil across Azeroth with cold scrutiny, seeking champions capable of shifting the balance of elemental warfare. Hydraxis's central campaign targets the blazing hosts of the Firelord, Ragnaros. He sees the encroachment of fiery elementals as a blight upon the world that must be extinguished. Before bestowing his trust or the tools needed to challenge Ragnaros's fiery stronghold in the Molten Core, Duke Hydraxis demands that mortals prove their strength, resilience, and loyalty by slaying hostile elementals across the continents. Those who prove their worth earn the blessings of the sea and the means to douse the sacred flames guarding the Firelord's domain.

npc:durnan-furcutter.text: Durnan Furcutter. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Durnan Furcutter outfits young dwarves and gnomes. He works inside the settlement as a clothier and leather merchant, selling light attire for the mountain cold. Inside Anvilmar, young dwarves and exiled gnomes prove themselves, and some need more freedom of movement than heavy iron allows. Durnan Furcutter sells light, pliable layers to scouts, rogues, and spellcasters who want to stay agile in Dun Morogh's bitter winds. He works near Anvilmar's hearth, offering everyday tailoring and stitched leather. He claims his stock is the finest in the valley. Durnan appreciates a strong drink as much as an honest trade. To warm himself against the freezing draft, he orders steaming mugs of Scalding Mornbrew from Nori Pridedrift, who sells the brew piping hot across Coldridge Valley. Adventurers running errands in the valley often hurry a hot mug to Durnan before it cools, then carry the empty back to Nori.

npc:ebru.text: Ebru. Ebru is a night elf druid sheltering in the crags above the Wailing Caverns. As one of Naralex's few remaining uncorrupted disciples, she watches helplessly as her master's dream of restoring the Barrens curdles into a nightmare. From her perch, she enlists travelers brave enough to enter the subterranean depths to cull the mutated horrors spawned by the Nightmare. While most of Naralex's followers succumbed to the emerald corruption creeping through the caverns, Ebru managed to escape the nightmare's grasp. Camped inside the cavernous skull formation overlooking the entrance to the Wailing Caverns, she keeps vigil over the descent. She knows that Naralex's noble plan—to tap subterranean springs and transform the arid Barrens into lush woodland—has gone horribly awry, and she desperately directs willing adventurers to eliminate the burgeoning deviate beasts threatening to overrun the surrounding plains.

npc:einar-stonegrip.text: Einar Stonegrip. Along the Wetlands crossroads, Einar Stonegrip keeps to the road and sends his goods to town with travelers. He avoids Menethil Harbor, where his estranged wife lives. Einar Stonegrip hunts crocolisks where the roads meet in the Wetlands. The crossroads link Dun Algaz, Dun Modr, and Menethil Harbor. He sells their sturdy hides to leatherworkers and merchants along the coast. Though rugged enough to wrestle reptiles from the mire, Einar is embroiled in a bitter falling-out with his wife, Sida. He stays on the road and asks travelers to carry his bundles of skins to his trading partner, James Halloran, rather than enter Menethil Harbor himself.

npc:elanaria.text: Elanaria. Elanaria is a night elf warrior mentor and coordinator stationed on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She directs developing fighters across Kalimdor, testing their mettle against dangerous threats such as the satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and spiritual entities like the Shade of Elura. Her guidance serves as a crucial bridge for Alliance soldiers honing their martial prowess in the night elven capital. Standing proudly on the Warrior's Terrace within the boughs of Darnassus, Elanaria serves as an instructor and point of contact for martial champions. In an era where the night elves have formally aligned with the Grand Alliance, her role extends beyond mentoring local Sentinels to preparing warriors of all backgrounds for the harsh challenges facing their lands. Elanaria does not offer easy praise; she expects discipline, resilience, and proven strength. She assigns seasoned adventurers to strike down formidable adversaries plaguing Teldrassil and Darkshore, including the corrupt satyr Vorlus Vilehoof and troubled spirits like the Shade of Elura. She also liaises with skilled craftsmen like Smith Mathiel to ensure that deserving warriors are properly armed for war.

npc:elder-bloodhoof.text: Elder Bloodhoof. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Bloodhoof rests just north of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. The Bloodhoof tribe honors him as a guardian spirit of its ancestors. Near Bloodhoof Village, Elder Bloodhoof watches over his people. The tauren honor him as a spirit bound to their lineage and to the plains of Mulgore. During the Lunar Festival, respectful travelers seek his wisdom and receive his blessings. His presence keeps the guidance of dead chieftains and tribal forebears close to the Bloodhoof tribe.

npc:elder-bronzebeard.text: Elder Bronzebeard. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Bronzebeard appears in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. His name belongs to the clan that rules the city, and his earthen form recalls the dwarves' stone-born ancestors. Near the pool in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Elder Bronzebeard appears in the shape of an earthen. The Titans forged the ancient earthen from living stone, before they became creatures of flesh. Dwarven scholars and explorers are only beginning to uncover their origins through excavations across Khaz Modan and beyond. Elder Bronzebeard's name is that of the ruling clan, and his form suggests he is a direct ancestor of the Bronzebeards. His spirit bears witness to how far his stone-born descendants have changed.

npc:elder-darkcore.text: Elder Darkcore. Elder Darkcore is an ancient spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival within the throne room of the Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity. Representing the honored ancestors of the world, he offers his blessing and festive tokens to travelers who seek him out. His presence marks a peaceful, reflective moment amidst the ruins of a fallen human kingdom. During the annual Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with adventurers. Elder Darkcore takes his vigil in one of the world's most somber locations: the royal throne room in the Ruins of Lordaeron, directly above the entrance to the Undercity. Surrounded by the blood-stained floor where King Terenas Menethil II fell, this spectral ancestor offers a Coin of Ancestry and his blessing to those brave enough to enter the heart of Forsaken territory to pay their respects.

npc:elder-goldwell.text: Elder Goldwell. Near Kharanos, Elder Goldwell appears during the Lunar Festival. The ancient earthen spirit recalls the origins of modern dwarven civilization. Elder Goldwell watches over the snowy slopes near Kharanos as a translucent earthen spirit. His stony form recalls the Titan-forged ancestors from whom the Bronzebeard clan descended. During the ancestor celebrations, travelers can honor that heritage in his presence.

npc:elder-graveborn.text: Elder Graveborn. Near Brill, Elder Graveborn greets travelers during the Lunar Festival. The ancestral spirit honors them and points pilgrims toward other elders in northern Lordaeron. Elder Graveborn greets travelers just southeast of Brill during the Lunar Festival. The spectral elder stands among the haunted woods of Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken town lies nearby. Though the kingdom is troubled, Graveborn offers pilgrims peaceful greetings and ancestral wisdom. He also points them toward spirits in the Undercity, the Sepulcher, and across the Plaguelands.

npc:elder-morningdew.text: Elder Morningdew. Elder Morningdew is an ancient night elf spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. She offers wisdom and ancestral blessings to travelers who seek her out amid the arid canyons and dried salt flats of the Shimmering Flats. Throughout the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to celebrate wisdom, legacy, and peace. Elder Morningdew is one such apparition, visiting Thousand Needles to greet honoring pilgrims. Bound by neither faction nor mortal conflict, she bestows her coin of ancestry upon any adventurer respectful enough to seek her counsel and receive her blessing.

npc:elder-obsidian.text: Elder Obsidian. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Elder Obsidian appears for the Lunar Festival. The ancestral earthen spirit greets travelers among the graves claimed by the Forsaken, offering ancient wisdom and blessings. Elder Obsidian greets travelers at the Sepulcher during the Lunar Festival. His earthen spirit brings the ancient heritage of Azeroth to Silverpine Forest. The surrounding crypts are held by the Forsaken, and feral worgen menace the forest. Yet Obsidian welcomes wayfarers of every allegiance in peace, offering a Coin of Ancestry and ancient blessings to those who seek his wisdom.

npc:elder-runetotem.text: Elder Runetotem. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Runetotem appears outside Razor Hill in Durotar. The tauren spirit offers wisdom and a blessing to travelers who seek her. Elder Runetotem appears beside Razor Hill, far from the grassy plains and sacred burial grounds of Mulgore. Her presence brings the ancient traditions of the Shu'halo to the Horde's home along the Great Sea. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great leaders, shamans, and heroes appear throughout the world to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem carries the name of a line that reveres the Earth Mother and seeks spiritual communion. Travelers who honor her receive ancestral tokens and her blessing.

npc:elder-skyseer.text: Elder Skyseer. Elder Skyseer is the spirit of an ancestral tauren residing atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. As an honoured elder returned from the spirit world, he observes the ongoing journeys of the Horde and remains deeply tied to the resting grounds of his people. Perched high above the salt canyons of Thousand Needles, Elder Skyseer lingers at the windswept mesa settlement of Freewind Post. While the tauren of Freewind Post bustle around the outpost's perilous bridges and wooden platforms, Skyseer watches over the realm as an ancestor who has crossed beyond the mortal veil. He serves as an ancestral beacon for travelers seeking the wisdom of past generations, offering his blessings to those who honor old traditions. Though his spirit commonly manifests among the wind-carved needles, Skyseer belongs to the long line of tauren ancestors whose people honor the sacred soil of Mulgore, where the ancestral spirits of Red Rocks watch over the tribes. Spirits like Skyseer reveal how thin the veil between the physical realm and the ancestral spirits remains for the tauren, guiding future generations through remembrance and ritual.

npc:elder-starweave.text: Elder Starweave. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave rests in Auberdine as a night elf ancestral spirit. She shares ancient wisdom with pilgrims along Darkshore’s coast. In Auberdine, Elder Starweave appears as an ethereal shade among the coastal dwellings. The Cenarion Circle and the peoples of Kalimdor honor her as an ancestor. Travelers pass through the port on their way inland or across the sea, but those who pause before her receive an ancestral blessing. She speaks of the stars, whose paths in this age differ from those of old, and sees them as beacons of hope and fortitude for generations to come.

npc:eleanor-shackleton.text: Eleanor Shackleton. Southwest of Brill, Eleanor Shackleton camps in the woods of Tirisfal Glades. This Forsaken outdoorswoman teaches travelers wilderness survival and field crafts instead of staying in town or the Undercity. Her surname is shared by other Forsaken in the region, a possible link to life before the plague. Eleanor Shackleton camps in the haunted woods southwest of Brill, away from the Undercity. Newly awakened Forsaken often head for those settlements, but she teaches travelers how to live off Tirisfal's blighted land. Her lessons cover setting up campsites, gathering firewood, and keeping trade crafts while roaming far from civilization's fires and kitchens. Eleanor Shackleton shares her surname with Pierce Shackleton and Samantha Shackleton, who live in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Family names can be the only tether an undead person has to mortal life in the shattered remnants of Lordaeron. Whether Eleanor, Pierce, and Samantha are close kin or share only common ancestry, each serves the Forsaken in a distinct way across the blighted kingdom.

npc:elu.text: Elu. Elu is an apprentice wind rider stationed atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Eager to begin his formal training and take to the skies, he tasks Horde travelers with retrieving wild wyvern eggs from nearby roosts. Perched high above the salt flats and canyon floor at Freewind Post, Elu spends his days tending to the settlement's aerial mounts while dreaming of his own flight. As a young tauren apprentice, he longs to join the ranks of the master wind riders who patrol the towering mesas of Kalimdor. Before he can begin true flight training, however, he must prove his capability by supplying the roost with fresh wyvern stock, sending capable adventurers to harvest intact eggs from the fierce wild wyverns nesting at Highperch.

npc:eva-sarkhoff.text: Eva Sarkhoff. Eva Sarkhoff is the spectral remnant of the former head maid of House Barov, lingering alongside her husband Lucien just outside the horrors of Scholomance. Tortured and slain by the Butcher during the fall of Caer Darrow, her spirit seeks brave mortals to avenge their deaths and destroy their cursed remains. Eva served the wealthy Barov family for decades as their head maid, caring for the sprawling keep of Caer Darrow alongside her husband Lucien, the family butler. As the Barovs grew paranoid about their aging mortality and vast wealth, they struck a catastrophic pact with Kel'Thuzad. The manor was gradually handed over to the fledgling Cult of the Damned, warping the grand residence into Scholomance, a secretive academy of necromancy. Eva and Lucien hid in the keep's corridors for six months, scavenging food while watching cultists and monstrosities steadily take over their home.

npc:falfindel-waywarder.text: Falfindel Waywarder. Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid stationed at Thalanaar, the outpost guarding the border between Feralas and the Thousand Needles. From this frontier watchpost, he works to heal corrupted lands and safeguard the southern wilderness of Kalimdor. Travelers wandering down from Stonetalon or the Barrens often find him seeking aid to restore balance to the wild. Thalanaar marks the gateway where the lush forests of Feralas descend into the towering mesas and dry salt plains of Thousand Needles. Falfindel Waywarder stands watch at this remote outpost, greeting weary travelers who have ventured far across the continent. Surrounded by natural grandeur and lurking dangers, he serves as a point of contact for the night elves seeking to monitor both local threats and broader environmental calamities across Kalimdor. Despite his southern post, Falfindel remains deeply concerned with the devastation far to the north in Stonetalon Mountains. The Charred Vale, ruined by dark sorcery and fiery destruction, stands as a painful scar upon Kalimdor's wilderness. When adventurers deliver aid to Falfindel to assist in its recovery, he calls upon the spirits of the forest. Summoning forth swarms of wisps, he directs them to make haste north to Stonetalon to begin mending the scorched earth. In addition to coordinating restoration efforts, Falfindel keeps a close watch on the surrounding region, including the quilboar dens of Razorfen Kraul. By reviewing recovered journals and gathering intelligence on quilboar leadership, Falfindel ensures that the Alliance understands the rising dangers threatening the passes between Feralas and the central deserts.

npc:falla-sagewind.text: Falla Sagewind. On a crag above the Barrens, Falla Sagewind watches the land for signs of trouble. Her camp lies between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, where she studies changes in nature and magic. Falla Sagewind keeps camp on a secluded summit southwest of the Crossroads, high above the Barrens trails. From there, she watches the savanna and the changes in its wildlife. She also studies corruption rising from fissures beneath the Wailing Caverns. Her vigil keeps her apart from the daily trade at the Crossroads, but her attention remains on the spirits and wounds of the land.

npc:fallen-hero-of-the-horde.text: Fallen Hero of the Horde. The Fallen Hero of the Horde is the lingering spirit of an orc warrior standing watch on the southern road out of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bound by regret and dishonor, he warns passing travelers of the horrors awaiting them in the Blasted Lands and seeks champions willing to deliver his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, this warrior was a celebrated champion dispatched with a handpicked regiment of soldiers to investigate the Blasted Lands and report back on the presence of the Burning Legion. His dispatch never made it; the courier sent north toward Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs. Stranded without orders or reinforcements, the commander eventually marched his soldiers south into the shattered wastes to confront the growing darkness. It was a fatal misjudgment. Overwhelmed by demonic forces, his army was scattered, captured, and subjected to horrific torment at the hands of the dreadlord Razelikh the Defiler.

npc:farmer-furlbrow.text: Farmer Furlbrow. Near the Jansen Stead, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife are stranded beside their broken wagon. Driven from their northern Westfall farm by the Defias Brotherhood, they hope to reach Elwynn Forest. Theodore Furlbrow left his pumpkin patch in northern Westfall with his wife, Verna, as criminals drove them from their home. They salvaged what they could and set out for Elwynn Forest, urging neighbors such as Farmer Saldean to leave too. Near the Jansen Stead, their wagon broke down, leaving them exposed to bandits and wild beasts. Verna tends to their horse, Old Blanchy, while Theodore keeps watch over the road. He hopes to recover the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day and warn Sentinel Hill about the approaching bandits.

npc:farmer-saldean.text: Farmer Saldean. At Saldean's Farm in central Westfall, Farmer Saldean keeps working the troubled fields beside his wife, Salma. While other farmers flee or give up, the veteran homesteader faces rogue harvest golems and growing banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers when Westfall prospered, before those years crumbled away. Overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits now surround his farm, but he refuses to yield his land. Other homesteaders have abandoned their acres or turned to thievery. Saldean and his wife, Salma, stay and work to harvest what little grain they can. He asks wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers that have taken over his fields and his neighbors' fields, so he can clear the soil for planting. Between Sentinel Hill and the northern bridge, Saldean's defense of his homestead helps keep civilian life going. He remains tied to the People's Militia despite the hard times, and sends able-bodied travelers to Gryan Stoutmantle once his immediate troubles are settled. Clearing the wild harvest reapers can only give his farm a temporary reprieve. The lawlessness strangling the countryside still has to be dealt with.

npc:feegly-the-exiled.text: Feegly the Exiled. Near the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens, Feegly the Exiled lurks alone. Once praised as one of the expedition’s finest diggers, he was driven off by General Twinbraid after claiming an uncovered relic’s power as his own.

npc:feero-ironhand.text: Feero Ironhand. At Maestra's Post, Feero Ironhand guards the road between Darkshore and Ashenvale. He works with Delgren the Purifier against the Cult of the Dark Strand. Maestra's Post watches the road south from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Feero Ironhand serves at the outpost, keeping communication and trade with Auberdine moving while watching the surrounding woods. He and Delgren the Purifier oppose the Cult of the Dark Strand. Cultists and forest predators threaten the path between Darnassus's supply lines and Ashenvale's front lines.

npc:fel-zerul.text: Fel'zerul. Fel'zerul is an orc warlock stationed at Stonard in the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows. Acting under direct orders from Warchief Thrall, he investigates the ominous presence lurking within the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. While Thrall's Horde generally views dark arts with suspicion, the Warchief recognizes that understanding sinister powers requires those who study them. Fel'zerul was dispatched to Stonard specifically to unravel the corruption surrounding the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. By directing adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls, the warlock seeks to determine what evil stirs beneath the murky waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

npc:felgur-twocuts.text: Felgur Twocuts. Felgur Twocuts is a blunt orc scout stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. He coordinates Horde efforts against the regional centaur clans. Standing watch amid the bleak expanse of Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts has little patience for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he assesses the threats facing travelers and settlers venturing west through the mountains, particularly the local Kolkar centaur. Felgur directs Horde champions to cull the local centaur chieftains and collect bounties on the warring tribes who threaten to overrun the region. He is a central contact for anyone seeking to secure the Horde's foothold in Desolace.

npc:felix-whindlebolt.text: Felix Whindlebolt. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Felix Whindlebolt seeks shelter after fleeing Gnomeregan. He lost his belongings in the rush, and Frostmane trolls carried them away. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan when radiation flooded the city. In his haste, he lost his personal belongings and tools. Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, box and bucket of bolts to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. Now stranded without his gear, Felix relies on travelers to retrieve it.

npc:field-marshal-snowfall.text: Field Marshal Snowfall. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's preparations for war. The dwarven military officer tracks the supplies gathered to face the silithid threat in Silithus and rewards those who aid the realm's preparations. Field Marshal Snowfall directs the Alliance's war preparations from Ironforge's Military Ward. He sees the coming conflict as more than a border skirmish: it is a fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Adventurers gather bandages, metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations in great numbers. Snowfall oversees these stores so Alliance forces can be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins. Blacksmiths, gatherers, cooks, and soldiers across Alliance lands all have a part in preparing for war. Snowfall tracks the effort, accepts commendation signets, and offers supply requisitions to volunteers. Once both factions have gathered the required supplies, the stores are packed and hauled south to Cenarion Hold. From there, the grand assault will target the qiraji swarms and the Old God behind the Scarab Wall.

npc:field-marshal-stonebridge.text: Field Marshal Stonebridge. At Stormwind's gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge helps oversee the city's defenses with General Marcus Jonathan. She also receives reports and trophies from major victories. Field Marshal Stonebridge watches the eastern archway at the entrance to the Valley of Heroes, beside Stormwind's main gates. A senior officer in the Grand Alliance, she works closely with General Marcus Jonathan. From the gate, she watches defenders, travelers, and returning champions enter the capital, ready to organize the garrison if danger breaches the outer defenses. Field Marshal Stonebridge also receives reports and spoils from campaigns against great threats to the kingdom. Senior commanders rely on officers like her to confirm important intelligence and mark victories in the field, including the defeat of warlords and monsters in the crags of Blackrock Mountain.

npc:fizzle-brassbolts.text: Fizzle Brassbolts. Fizzle Brassbolts is a prominent gnomish engineer stationed out on the baked salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Alongside his rival, the goblin Pozzik, Fizzle co-founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision engineering against reckless goblin ingenuity in high-speed rocket car races. He constantly seeks parts, fuel, and strange desert reagents to keep his racing team running. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, political alliances and ancient grudges yield to the roar of motorized engines. Fizzle Brassbolts arrived here with one goal in mind: proving once and for all that gnomish craftsmanship is vastly superior to crude goblin tinkering. Together with his goblin counterpart Pozzik, he helped lay out the Mirage Raceway, bringing race cars, pit crews, and spectators to an otherwise desolate basin. Racing across dry salt beds at breakneck speeds requires constant improvisation, and Fizzle does not shy away from unorthodox experiments. Whether testing volatile mixtures concocted from local creature venom or contracting travelers to fetch replacement mechanical parts, Fizzle is determined to keep his driver's wheels turning faster than any explosive goblin contraption.

npc:fleet-master-seahorn.text: Fleet Master Seahorn. Fleet Master Seahorn is a seasoned tauren mariner who serves as the naval commander of the Blackwater Raiders in Booty Bay. Stationed on the upper balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern alongside Baron Revilgaz, he oversees the goblin port's maritime defenses. His primary duty is protecting the harbor from the looming threat posed by their sworn enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. While tauren are renowned across Kalimdor as plains-dwellers, Fleet Master Seahorn chose a vastly different life upon the ocean. Clad in pirate regalia, he commands the fleet of the Blackwater Raiders, the private naval arm of the Steamwheedle Cartel's operation in Stranglethorn Vale. Stationed atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Seahorn works shoulder-to-shoulder with Baron Revilgaz, coordinating shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for the lawless yet strictly managed port of Booty Bay. Beyond repelling pirate raids, Seahorn manages varied commercial and salvage ventures across the Eastern Kingdoms. He coordinates recovery efforts for lost sunken treasures off the Arathi coast near Faldir's Cove, working with salvage divers to secure elven relics. He also keeps Revilgaz informed of lucrative opportunities passing through town, such as competitive angling and local trade, ensuring the Blackwater fleet stays well-funded and ahead of rival operations.

npc:foggy-mackreel.text: Foggy MacKreel. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel worries about a moonshine delivery bound for Southshore. Stranded on ruined lower masonry above a dizzying drop, the dwarf keeps his mind on the task. Foggy MacKreel waits on broken pylons beneath the Thandol Span, calm despite his dangerous perch. Dark Iron sabotage and war damage shattered the bridge between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. MacKreel gives little thought to rescue; he wants his potent moonshine delivered to the patrons of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He hires passing travelers nimble enough to reach his ledge and finish the delivery for him.

npc:foreman-stonebrow.text: Foreman Stonebrow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Foreman Stonebrow faces a trogg attack that has driven miners from the pits. He speaks for the Miners' League and now needs help defending the excavation. Foreman Stonebrow directs the Miners' League's work at Gol'Bolar Quarry, east of Kharanos. Deep digging broke into trogg burrows beneath the quarry, and the creatures swarmed the pits, driving miners from their tools. Stonebrow remains at the quarry rim, seeking travelers willing to push the troggs back.

npc:foreman-thazz-ril.text: Foreman Thazz'ril. Peons work under Foreman Thazz'ril in the Valley of Trials. The orc labor supervisor keeps crews on schedule and supplies ready for young warriors, but slacking workers and nearby cultists frustrate him. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril directs peons who chop lumber and gather materials for the encampment and young warriors. Building a home in Durotar's harsh red rock takes steady labor, yet the peons often nap under the desert sun. Thazz'ril sends newly arrived recruits to rouse the sleepers with his blackjack, and keep construction moving. While scouting the Burning Blade Coven for mineral resources, Thazz'ril fled the dark cultists inside and accidentally left his treasured enchanted pick behind. Warlocks and their demonic minions now gather in the cave. Too cautious to retrieve the tool himself, Thazz'ril relies on young Horde aspirants to venture into the depths and bring it back.

npc:foreman-thistlenettle.text: Foreman Thistlenettle. In the Deadmines, Foreman Thistlenettle once led a dwarven mining crew. He worked for both the Miners' League and the Explorers' League until a cave-in trapped his crew below Moonbrook. He died with them and rose again as a ghoul, still carrying his guild badge through the dark, collapsed tunnels.

npc:frahun-shadewhisper.text: Frahun Shadewhisper. At Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Frahun Shadewhisper trains night elf rogues. He teaches new scouts and rogues stealth, agility, and covert strikes. Erion Shadewhisper, another rogue trainer in Darnassus, shares his family name. At Aldrassil in Teldrassil, Frahun Shadewhisper teaches new rogues concealment and bladecraft. Night elf society honors priests, sentinels, and druids, yet scouts and infiltrators also help safeguard the World Tree's boughs. Recruits bring Frahun an encrypted sigil. He weighs their potential and guides their first steps in the craft.

npc:furl-scornbrow.text: Furl Scornbrow. At a watchtower northwest of Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow keeps watch over Durotar. Too old for the front lines, he crafts sturdy packs for young travelers. Furl Scornbrow watches the central plains from a wooden tower northwest of Razor Hill. In the tense days after Orgrimmar was founded, sentries like Furl sounded signal horns against hostile quilboar, centaur, and Kul Tiras interlopers. Durotar has since grown more stable, and Razor Hill has secured its borders. Emergencies come less often, leaving Furl long quiet hours at his post. Furl says his old bones and fading strength leave him unable to fight. Still, an orc does not easily surrender their purpose. He uses his hands to make canvas sacks and packs for fresh recruits carrying supplies. In exchange for coarse thread and practical materials, he equips green adventurers setting out to prove their worth to the Horde.

npc:gaerolas-talvethren.text: Gaerolas Talvethren. At Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids in troubled Teldrassil. He seeks aid against aggressive furbolgs and corruption spreading through the boughs. Gaerolas Talvethren guards the Sleeping druids at Starbreeze Village. They slumber in communion with the Emerald Dream, and his watch has grown uneasy as unnatural corruption spreads through the forest and unsettles Teldrassil. Gaerolas calls on travelers to push back the Gnarlpine furbolgs, whose minds have turned to madness and savagery. He hopes to uncover the taint spreading from their shamans and the roots of their distress, preserving what sanctity remains in eastern Teldrassil.

npc:galgar.text: Galgar. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young recruits serving the Horde. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise. Galgar cooks near the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials, feeding young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, where food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen. Galgar's specialty is called Cactus Apple Surprise. He says gathering spiny desert fruit is a simple task meant to ease fresh recruits into adventuring. The dish still feeds hungry trainees. Every Horde warrior begins somewhere, and Galgar starts them with foraging in the desert.

npc:gar-thok.text: Gar'Thok. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok directs recruits leaving the Valley of Trials to secure Durotar. The veteran orc warrior survived the Kul Tiras landings on Durotar's coast and now coordinates defense against human encroachers and native threats. After the Third War, Gar'Thok marched to Durotar under Warchief Thrall and served as a lieutenant under Nazgrel during the first days of building the new homeland. When Rexxar, the half-ogre wanderer, arrived in Durotar, Gar'Thok warned him that quilboar were raiding the settlement's perimeter. He enlisted the beastmaster to protect the fragile new settlement. Gar'Thok's resolve was tested when Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiras fleet landed on Durotar's eastern shores. At an outlying watch post, Gar'Thok saw naval marines overwhelm and slaughter his garrison. His forces were decimated, but he survived. The surprise assault left him vigilant against the surviving marines, who still occupy Tiragarde Keep and the coastal shipwrecks. From the barracks at Razor Hill, Gar'Thok oversees the defense of central Durotar. He quickly sends emerging Horde warriors, shamans, and scouts to drive out hostile Kul Tiran remnants, repossess salvaged supplies, and recover military orders left in the coastal ruins. Durotar's safety is far from assured, and Gar'Thok keeps pressure on those who challenge the Horde's right to this soil.

npc:gart-mistrunner.text: Gart Mistrunner. At Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner guides novice tauren called by the Earth Mother. He teaches their first rites of nature magic on the Red Cloud Mesa. Gart Mistrunner watches over Camp Narache as the Shu'halo rekindle their ancient druidic path. New tauren druids are sent to him when they take their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often with a note commending them to his care. Gart teaches them to commune with the natural world. They draw on nature's restorative power and Mu'sha's lunar radiance to heal allies and strike down threats to the land.

npc:gath-ilzogg.text: Gath'Ilzogg. Stonewatch Keep remains under Gath'Ilzogg's command in the Redridge Mountains. The Blackrock warlord's force holds the fortress and raids Lakeshire, where Magistrate Solomon has placed a bounty on him. Gath'Ilzogg came north from the Burning Steppes to secure Redridge for the Blackrock clan. With help from the renegade human warlock Morganth's foul sorcery, his warband battered Stonewatch Keep's defenders and seized the heights above the region. From the fortress, Gath'Ilzogg directs raids through the valleys and toward Lakeshire's bridge, tightening pressure on the human settlement. Elite Blackrock guards and a vicious black dragon whelp named Singe stay close to him.

npc:gazin-tenorm.text: Gazin Tenorm. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Gazin Tenorm keeps watch near the altar after a dangerous scouting mission in Elwynn Forest. Gazin Tenorm stays in the Cathedral of Light, though his thoughts remain in Elwynn Forest. He and his close friend Henze Faulk went into the woods to gather proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements for the royal court. Defias forces ambushed them. Gazin escaped to Stormwind, but Henze was left in mortal danger. Now Gazin seeks a hero of the Light to help his companion.

npc:gelkak-gyromast.text: Gelkak Gyromast. Along Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded after threshadons sank his ship. The gnome talks like a pirate captain and wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, working again. West of the Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore's northern coast. The gnome talks like an old sea dog and calls himself captain. Threshadons sank his ship just offshore, and he washed up on the misty shore. The key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks. Crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage carried off its pieces.

npc:general-marcus-jonathan.text: General Marcus Jonathan. At Stormwind's gates, General Marcus Jonathan guards the capital and weighs calls for aid from the kingdom's frontier settlements. A veteran of the Second War, he commands Stormwind Defense and oversees the garrison. General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's defense from horseback in the Valley of Heroes. He is the highest-ranking officer at the city gates and its first line of defense. During the Second War, he fought beside soldiers such as Reginald Windsor under General Turalyon. Now he must protect the capital while frontier towns, including Lakeshire, make increasingly desperate appeals for help.

npc:gerard-tiller.text: Gerard Tiller. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works under the warm sun and longs for spring water. He offers a shiny red apple to any traveler who brings him a skin of it. Gerard Tiller works the grounds outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, south of Goldshire. The vineyard is known for its grapes, and keeping the harvest going takes hard labor. The chores leave Gerard thirsty, so he welcomes travelers who bring him a skin of fresh spring water. In return, he gives them shiny red apples gathered from local orchards.

npc:gerrig-bonegrip.text: Gerrig Bonegrip. In Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip keeps a quiet shop of strange texts. At Bonegrip's Runes and Dooms, he buys and sells writings on dark rituals and forgotten ancient powers.

npc:gershala-nightwhisper.text: Gershala Nightwhisper. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper studies what magical corruption does to elves. Concerned by the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, he examines cursed aquatic and demonic creatures for signs of how corruption changes mind and body. From Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond Darkshore's coastal troubles to the danger he sees in the high elves of Quel'Thalas. He watches with dismay as they embrace perilous arcane practices and call themselves blood elves. Gershala wants to understand the bodily and spiritual changes that follow unchecked magic. To study them, he sends seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to gather corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell there. Gershala's interest in naga and satyr brain stems comes from their shared past. Both races were once night elves, before they yielded to Queen Azshara and demonic bargains. Gershala examines the marks that millennia of demonic and abyssal energies have left on their nervous systems. He hopes to find warnings or safeguards that might keep other elven kin from suffering similar monstrous deformity.

npc:gilshalan-windwalker.text: Gilshalan Windwalker. At Aldrassil's roots in Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the corruption spreading through Teldrassil. His work begins with the Webwood spiders and their growing aggression. Gilshalan Windwalker watches Shadowglen from the stone steps at Aldrassil's entrance. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and their harmony with nature, yet signs of spiritual malaise appeared almost at once. Gilshalan studies how the corruption affects the local beasts, beginning with the venomous spiders weaving webs nearby. Gilshalan studies the Webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Once part of the forest's balance, the spiders have grown hostile and tainted. He sends young novices to gather venom sacs and intact eggs. By studying them, he hopes to learn how the venom has changed and whether the corruption passes through generations or spreads from Teldrassil's soil.

npc:gilthares-firebough.text: Gilthares Firebough. Gilthares Firebough waits in a tower at Northwatch Hold, held captive by Theramore. Once a deckhand on a moonshine transport between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he seeks a chance to escape. Gilthares Firebough is held in a tower at Northwatch Hold. His ship carried illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay when naval forces from Theramore blasted it to splinters. The sole survivor, Gilthares was dragged ashore in chains and locked away. He wears vivid red and bears little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew. Still, he cares little who helps him break free, so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

npc:gnoarn.text: Gnoarn. In Ironforge, Gnoarn helps his scattered people find aid. The exiled gnome lives in Tinker Town after the fall of Gnomeregan, directing travelers to fellow engineers and survivors. Gnoarn keeps track of Gnomeregan's scattered survivors from Tinker Town in Ironforge. Troggs invaded the great underground city, and catastrophic radiation made it uninhabitable. The Bronzebeard dwarves gave Gnoarn refuge, as they did many of his people. He now points capable travelers toward gnomes who need help abroad, including the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan and the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

npc:godrick-farsan.text: Godrick Farsan. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Forsaken warlocks beside Carendin Halgar. Though blind, he says he sees in a different way. Among the summoning circles in the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar as he guides aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Godrick is blind, yet says he sees in a different way and does not explain how. He tests those who seek to bind greater demons, sending them to gather pure hearts and essences for intricate summoning rites.

npc:golnir-bouldertoe.text: Golnir Bouldertoe. Beside Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe supplies miners and prospectors and receives dispatches for couriers and travelers. At Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. He sells sturdy mining picks, flux, and coal, supplies that fuel the smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable contact for workers arriving in the city. He directs fresh hands and receives supply messages carried from nearby outposts.

npc:gorbold-steelhand.text: Gorbold Steelhand. In Auberdine, Gorbold Steelhand keeps trade moving along Darkshore’s coast. The dwarven merchant brings goods from far across the Great Sea for travelers, crafters, and night elves. Gorbold Steelhand brings Ironforge trade to Auberdine. Night elves populate much of northern Kalimdor, so Alliance outposts depend on merchants who cross the Great Sea. Gorbold works alongside the kaldorei, selling trade goods, reagents, crafting supplies, and tools. Travelers come to him as they prepare to explore Darkshore’s dangerous shores and forests. Gorbold Steelhand watches the perilous waters off Auberdine as closely as his stock. Reefs along Darkshore have swallowed Alliance vessels, and lost cargo draws the merchant’s interest. Travelers who dive into the deep ocean may find him eager to hear about salvage and lost logs from sunken wrecks.

npc:gordon-wendham.text: Gordon Wendham. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham sells weapons and helps couriers from the surface find their way. Gordon Wendham sells weapons to those who take up arms for the Forsaken. His stock ranges from daggers and hand axes to broadswords and maces. Fledgling fighters can find dependable iron here before they venture into the contested reaches of Lordaeron. Travelers sent by flight masters and couriers are often directed to Gordon Wendham's stall. Some arrive from the bat handlers atop the ruins. His place in the Trade Quarter makes him easy to find when travelers need supplies or have dispatches to carry through the underground city.

npc:gramma-stonefield.text: Gramma Stonefield. At the Stonefield farm in Elwynn, Gramma Stonefield quietly works to ease a family feud. Gramma Stonefield has watched the Stonefields and the Maclures bicker for decades across the road. The oldest living member of the Stonefield clan, she sees their rivalry as senseless and harmful. When her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, Gramma chooses compassion over clan loyalty. She turns to her old friend William Pestle in Goldshire and quietly plans ways for the sweethearts to meet in secret, despite the hostility between their farms.

npc:grand-mason-marblesten.text: Grand Mason Marblesten. In Ironforge's Commons, Grand Mason Marblesten prepares a tribute to Sully Balloo. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned the memorial for the dwarven soldier, who died in the Thandol Span tragedy, and Marblesten seeks stone worthy of the work. Grand Mason Marblesten oversees civic projects and memorials in Ironforge's Commons. Dwarven stonemasons carve halls, pillars, and great effigies from the mountain, carrying on a tradition centuries old. Marblesten is among the city's foremost masters of the chisel, shaping stone to preserve the history of the Bronzebeard line. King Magni commissioned Marblesten to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. The memorial honors Balloo and his grieving widow. For a lasting tribute, Marblesten seeks Alterac Granite, one of the finest stones available, from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad.

npc:granis-swiftaxe.text: Granis Swiftaxe. Inside Kharanos, Granis Swiftaxe trains young Alliance fighters from Coldridge Pass. The dwarf warrior trainer waits in the Thunderbrew Distillery, then sends seasoned warriors to Ironforge. Granis Swiftaxe warms himself among the casks of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, where he trains young warriors crossing Dun Morogh. Proud of the warrior’s path, he openly amuses himself at those from other callings who try to win his attention. When a student proves their skill in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to Muren Stormpike, the master trainer in Ironforge’s Military Ward.

npc:great-father-winter.text: Great-father Winter. In Orgrimmar, Great-father Winter hears children's wishes during the Feast of Winter Veil. Hired by Smokywood Pastures, he brings holiday cheer near Grommash Hold in the Valley of Strength, though the work wears on him. Greatfather Winter in the Valley of Strength is an orc performer hired by the Smokywood Pastures merchant company. Ancient lore tells of a majestic elemental spirit who wanders the land, bringing snow and seasonal renewal, but the figure in Orgrimmar promotes company wares and entertains Horde children. Some critics say the commercial mascot cheapens genuine seasonal traditions. Still, few deny the festive excitement he brings to the city streets. Greatfather Winter works outside Grommash Hold, beneath decorated evergreens. Children climb onto his lap to tell him what gifts they want, while he promotes Smokywood Pastures discounts and offers holiday greetings. The long shift wears him down. He admits he keeps festive spirits in his pack to quiet the noise when work ends, and visiting adventurers bring him snacks to help him endure.

npc:greatfather-winter.text: Greatfather Winter. At winter's turning, Greatfather Winter belongs to both ancient legend and city festivities. Some believe he blankets Azeroth in snow so the land can rest and renew. In the cities, goblins of Smokywood Pastures shape how people know him. Ancient tales tell of Greatfather Winter wandering the world late in the year, spreading his snowy cloak so nature can sleep and be reborn. Dwarves see him as an aspect or herald of the titans, and point to Dun Morogh's frosted crags as proof of his favor. Tauren respect his place in winter's turning, while crediting the Sun and Moon with the cold and storms that let the Earth Mother rest. Across the lands, people gather and feast against the cold, holding to the promise of life returning. In Ironforge and Orgrimmar, goblins of Smokywood Pastures have reshaped the old spirit for city celebrations. The trading company made popular the image of Greatfather Winter as a cheerful elder in red, with a white beard, flying sleigh, holiday treats, and toys. Smokywood Pastures hires a dwarf in Ironforge and an orc in Orgrimmar to hear children's wishlists and accept milk and gingerbread cookies. Beneath lavishly decorated trees, the company also promotes its seasonal wares.

npc:greatmother-hawkwind.text: Greatmother Hawkwind. Beside the well on Red Cloud Mesa, Greatmother Hawkwind guides young tauren. As mother of Chief Hawkwind, Camp Narache's leader, she holds to the tribe's shared duty despite her age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside Camp Narache's fresh water well, guiding young tauren as they begin their rites of passage. Age has slowed her stride, but she still takes part in village life. She believes every member of the tribe, young or old, must help sustain the community. She often asks young tauren to fetch water and help with simple chores. Greatmother Hawkwind is mother to Chief Hawkwind, who leads Camp Narache. She offers counsel as threats face Red Cloud Mesa. Her son organizes hunters and warriors against Bristleback quilboar and local predators. She tends to the settlement's moral heart, reminding the newly awakened that strength begins with humility and service to kin.

npc:greta-mosshoof.text: Greta Mosshoof. Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid allied with the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood. Alongside night elves and fellow guardians of nature, she investigates the foul taint creeping across the ancient forest and directs scouts into the Shadow Council stronghold of Jaedenar. Stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary on the southern boundary of Felwood, Greta Mosshoof works alongside the Emerald Circle to combat the pervasive corruption consuming the ancient woods. Rather than surrendering the blighted lands to the demonic taint left in the wake of the Third War, she coordinates efforts to understand and push back the spreading rot. Her investigations zero in on the poisoned waters of Felwood and the foul cultists burrowed within Jaedenar.

npc:grimbooze-thunderbrew.text: Grimbooze Thunderbrew. In Westfall's Dagger Hills, Grimbooze Thunderbrew brews potent spirits and speaks in verse. The eccentric dwarf belongs to the Thunderbrew clan. Grimbooze Thunderbrew camps in the Dagger Hills, where he tends his private casks. He comes from the Thunderbrew brewing family of Kharanos and left the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh for Westfall's windswept hills. Jovial and devoted to potent spirits, he speaks only in rhymes. A traveler must complete a simple task before he answers any questions, and he is always ready to test a thirsty palate.

npc:grish-longrunner.text: Grish Longrunner. At the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner watches the boundary between the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. The tauren scout carries messages for the Horde and tracks movement across the crossing. Grish Longrunner keeps watch beside the Great Lift in the southern Barrens. Its platform connects the dry southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Quilboar packs roam nearby, and rival groups threaten the crossing. Grish watches travelers and keeps the Horde informed, so reinforcements can be called where they are needed.

npc:grub.text: Grub. At a hut east of the Crossroads, Grub runs a roadside eatery with a cook and a baker. He is known for teaching travelers to cook with the Barrens' local vermin. East of the Crossroads, Grub shares a hut with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. Grub makes use of the Barrens' dig rats instead of letting them go to waste. He offers travelers a recipe for simmering the rodents into stew.

npc:grull-hawkwind.text: Grull Hawkwind. At Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Grull Hawkwind guides young tauren through their first trials. As Chief Hawkwind’s son, he prepares hunters and warriors to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. At Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind helps prepare the tribe’s youth. The son of Chief Hawkwind, he guides new arrivals on Red Cloud Mesa and judges whether they are ready to serve the Shu'halo. He sets trials of stamina, tracking, and survival against plainstriders and mountain cougars. Through these trials, young tauren learn that balance and respect for nature are foundations of life in Mulgore.

npc:grunt-dogran.text: Grunt Dogran. Grunt Dogran waits in captivity deep in the southern Barrens. Once assigned to the Crossroads and then Camp Taurajo, he was taken during a patrol into Agama'gor. Grunt Dogran was sent from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo after rising in the Horde military. He led a detachment of grunts into Agama'gor, where they met the Bristleback quilboar in a fierce clash. Dogran was badly wounded and crippled. His comrades retreated without him, and the quilboar dragged him into captivity.

npc:grunt-logmar.text: Grunt Logmar. At Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar watches the southern Barrens frontier for the Horde. He tracks threats near the camp and seeks aid for missing scouts. At Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar guards the Horde's southern Barrens frontier. The camp lies among the tauren, near hostile quilboar grounds and the mountain passes into Stonetalon and Mulgore. Logmar keeps watch over these dangers and coordinates scouting reports. When his comrades are ambushed or captured by local hostiles, he calls on capable Horde travelers to help find and aid them.

npc:grunth.text: Grunth. In Orgrimmar, Grunth eagerly seeks the company of Horde champions. The young orc lives in the Drag orphanage and, during Children's Week, journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero. Grunth is a young orc orphan in the Drag of Orgrimmar, where Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for him. Raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he watches armored adventurers with awe and asks them questions without end. Are armored warriors truly terrifying? Why does lightning on water not kill every fish? Will he ever see someone fight an actual dragon? During Children's Week, an Orcish Orphan Whistle summons Grunth to travel with adventurers on a tour across the world. He wants to meet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Mulgore, see the ruined throne room of Lordaeron, and visit the rugged frontiers where his people fight for their future.

npc:guard-berton.text: Guard Berton. Outside the Lakeshire Inn, Guard Berton seeks swift justice for Targorr the Dread. The human guardsman is tired of Stormwind's delays while Redridge faces the Blackrock orc invasion. Guard Berton keeps watch outside the Lakeshire Inn as Redridge Mountains faces the Blackrock orc invasion. His concern is Targorr the Dread, an enemy captured and locked deep within the Stormwind Stockade. Sentenced to death for crimes against the kingdom, Targorr remains imprisoned because Stormwind has postponed his execution indefinitely. Berton will not let the brutal raider linger in a cell while Lakeshire bleeds. He hires willing adventurers to bypass the delays and kill the orc.

npc:guard-howe.text: Guard Howe. Near Lakeshire's bridge, Guard Howe watches the road and seeks fighters against the Blackrock orcs. A personal vendetta drives him to offer bounties for proof of their defeat. Guard Howe keeps watch just south of the stone bridge over Lake Everstill, near the heart of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs press into the Redridge Mountains, and Howe sees them as a threat to the valley. He holds a bitter grudge against the clan and recruits passing fighters to hunt orcs in the eastern hills. In return, he offers pay for proof that they have been defeated.

npc:gubber-blump.text: Gubber Blump. Along Auberdine’s shore, Gubber Blump fishes, teaches angling, and looks for fresh crab meat. Gubber Blump fishes on the Darkshore coast, between Auberdine’s flight master and ferry pier. While most dwarves favor stone halls or forges, he chooses the shore. He teaches fishing and sells simple angling gear to travelers. Crab meat is among his favorite foods, and he often relies on travelers to bring in catches from the dangerous coast or recover his family fishing tackle. Gubber Blump speaks freely about his family, especially his cousin Graun Blump, who has a beard and an unusual odor. Travelers who help with coastal work, such as gathering crawler legs or finding his family pole, may receive a handwritten thank-you letter and a shiny fishing lure for their next cast.

npc:gurda-ragescar.text: Gurda Ragescar. Gurda Ragescar fell at a Horde camp southwest of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. She and Feran Strongwind died defending it against dangers in the shadowed forest. Gurda Ragescar and her guards fell at a small Horde camp southwest of Splintertree Post. The outpost stood beneath Ashenvale's dense canopy, deep in territory contested by night elven defenders and wild beasts. Gurda and Feran Strongwind were killed when the camp was overrun. Only remnants of their last stand remain for passing allies to find. Travelers near the trail may find the scene of Gurda's defeat. The camp's possessions and unfinished work point to Horde efforts across the woods, including missing documents and orders disrupted by the ambush.

npc:hagar-lightninghoof.text: Hagar Lightninghoof. Hagar Lightninghoof is a tauren scout stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Driven by rumors of a strange clutch hidden in the canyon depths, he investigates reports of an alien egg guarded fiercely by local wind serpents. While stationed among the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof caught wind of rumors regarding an unnatural egg nestled deep inside a cavern below. The local wind serpents guarded the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts at bay. Seeking an adventurer bold enough to brave the serpents' den, Hagar hopes to study the specimen firsthand and discern what manner of beast could warrant such defensive instincts from the canyon's natural predators.

npc:halaan-hawk-eye.text: Halaan Hawk-Eye. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne lookout stationed atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Lacking both magical sensitivity and the mystic skysight of his peers, he relies instead on keen mundane vision to monitor the surrounding island. From his perch, he tracks the distant anchor pylons and warns visitors of their faltering arcane stability. Perched high above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye serves his people without the gifts common to many Skyborne. He cannot draw upon the arcane power flowing through the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle, nor can he gaze between worlds through the mystical skysight. Instead, Halaan relies entirely on his sharp natural senses. From his vantage point on the watchtower, he scans the horizon to observe the island's anchor pylons, calling attention to their increasingly volatile and inconsistent arcane energies.

npc:hana-zua.text: Hana'zua. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua lies wounded after meeting Sarkoth on the canyon ridges. The Darkspear scout waits for help from young Horde initiates. Hana'zua lies wounded on the ridges above the Valley of Trials. The Darkspear scout met Sarkoth, a vicious scorpid that stalks the cliffs, and its venomous sting nearly killed him. Unable to move or make his way back to camp, he waits in the dust for passing recruits. He needs them to kill Sarkoth and carry word of his plight to the Den.

npc:hands-springsprocket.text: Hands Springsprocket. At Coldridge Pass, Hands Springsprocket struggles to keep supplies moving between the valley and Kharanos. Rockjaw troggs have blocked the route. Hands Springsprocket waits at the mouth of Coldridge Pass, where Rockjaw troggs have stopped his supply runs. He usually carries provisions to the Thunderbrew distillery and the inn in Kharanos. The troggs have overrun the underground tunnel out of Coldridge Valley, halting trade and foot traffic. Hands now depends on travelers able to carry essential crates through the dangerous mountain passage.

npc:hansel-heavyhands.text: Hansel Heavyhands. Hansel Heavyhands is an unusually massive Dark Iron dwarf stationed with the Thorium Brotherhood atop Thorium Point in the Searing Gorge. Tasked with perilous field work by the outpost's overseers, he consistently delegates dangerous jobs to passing adventurers using a colorful array of petty physical complaints. His hulking frame stands out among his kin, even if his enthusiasm for fieldwork does not match his size. Even by the broad-shouldered standards of the Dark Iron clan, Hansel Heavyhands is an anomaly. Towering over his brethren with a massive frame that borders on orcish in width and height, his sheer physical presence suggests a warrior built for frontline slaughter. Yet despite his imposing build and formidable moniker, Hansel appears utterly uninterested in unnecessary physical exertion, preferring the relative security of the Thorium Brotherhood's camp high above the volcanic ash. Taskmaster Scrange and Master Smith Burninate frequently assign Hansel the grim chore of culling the fiery beasts lurking in the slag pits below. When told to clear out the predatory Incendosaurs crawling through the Cauldron, Hansel begs off citing sore feet. When ordered to exterminate the Greater Lava Spiders infesting the searing wastes, he claims the blasted volcanic ridge is afflicted with a 'frigid climate' that has given him a miserable cold. Consequently, any mercenary willing to brave the magma flows finds Hansel ready with an open contract.

npc:harb-clawhoof.text: Harb Clawhoof. Near Bloodhoof Village, Harb Clawhoof tends the tauren’s kodos. He offers them to worthy tauren riders and trusted champions of Thunder Bluff. Harb Clawhoof tends the kodos near Bloodhoof Village. These great beasts carry heavy loads across long distances and are vital to tauren travel and work on the plains. Harb cares for each one, trains it, and pairs it with riders respected by the tauren people. Tauren earn the trust needed to ride Harb’s kodos, while outsiders face closer scrutiny. Their size and temperament make kodos difficult for those unfamiliar with them to guide. Non-tauren allies must prove their loyalty and earn exalted standing with Thunder Bluff before riding one of Harb’s mounts.

npc:harken-windtotem.text: Harken Windtotem. In Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem guides young hunters across Mulgore’s plains. He teaches the traditions of his people and asks hunters and travelers to prove their tracking and foraging skills. Near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, Harken Windtotem guides those learning the tauren hunting ways. Life on Mulgore’s plains calls for respect for the natural world and the skills needed to sustain a tribe. Harken tests young hunters by sending them after the swoops that circle the mesas. They gather the birds’ quills, showing patience, aim, and care in taking only what they need.

npc:harlan-bagley.text: Harlan Bagley. At the Lionheart Armory in Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley tends to the arms and equipment his customers need. He is a human merchant in the Trade District, serving citizens and visiting adventurers from his shop on the district's northern side. Harlan Bagley keeps the Lionheart Armory on the northern side of Stormwind's Trade District. He tends its stock and sells defensive gear from behind the counter. Trade and regional couriers bring supplies to the shop as the capital faces distant border conflicts and shortages.

npc:harlo-barnaby.text: Harlo Barnaby. In Menethil Harbor, Harlo Barnaby bears the wounds of Dun Modr's fall. The dwarven refugee escaped the Dark Iron assault and warns travelers of the tragedy in the northern marshes. Harlo Barnaby fled Dun Modr when Dark Iron dwarves struck the northern stronghold without warning. In the chaos, a stray axe hit him square in the back. The blow knocked him unconscious, yet he survived the trek across the marshland. Harlo awoke bandaged in Menethil Harbor, alive but marked by his wounds and memories of the massacre. He cannot return to Dun Modr, so he urges Alliance adventurers to investigate the smoking ruins of his former home.

npc:hegnar-rumbleshot.text: Hegnar Rumbleshot. On the snowy road from Coldridge Pass to Kharanos, Hegnar Rumbleshot keeps a gunsmith's camp. He supplies local hunters and mountaineers with firearms and ammunition. Hegnar Rumbleshot keeps a small camp between Coldridge Pass and Kharanos, where he serves dwarven marksmen, travelers, and the local militia. At the camp, mountain folk use a popular range to hone their aim against the wild beasts prowling Dun Morogh. The steady stream of shooters leaves Hegnar in need of fresh ammunition from his supplier, the dwarf engineer Loslor Rudge.

npc:henze-faulk.text: Henze Faulk. Near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest, Henze Faulk lies gravely wounded. He shielded his companion Gazin Tenorm from the Defias Brotherhood, and now awaits a paladin's aid. Henze Faulk lies near the stone ring east of Stormwind, at Heroes' Vigil. Defias marauders ambushed him and his friend Gazin Tenorm there. Henze took the attack so Gazin could survive, and fell to the bandits' blades. Gazin reached the Cathedral of Light to seek help. Henze remains between life and death, awaiting the aid of a paladin carrying a Symbol of Life.

npc:heralath-fallowbrook.text: Heralath Fallowbrook. Deep in Razorfen Kraul, Heralath Fallowbrook lies dying in quilboar hands. Sent to investigate the briars around Ancient Agamaggan's remains, he was captured and brutalized. Now he hopes word of his fate and his cherished pendant will reach his wife in Darnassus. Heralath Fallowbrook came to the southern Barrens to investigate Ancient Agamaggan and the briars spreading around his remains. Sent by his people, the night elf druid sought the source of Razorfen Kraul's corruption. The quilboar captured him instead and locked him in a pen, where beatings and fever left him with mortal wounds. Before he faded, Heralath told Henrig Lonebrow, a dwarf captive, what he had learned. He urged Henrig to warn the sentinel outpost at Thalanaar about the aggression stirred by Charlga Razorflank, the quilboar crone.

npc:high-executor-derrington.text: High Executor Derrington. At the Bulwark, High Executor Derrington directs the Forsaken vanguard against threats from the Western Plaguelands. A no-nonsense military officer, he sends seasoned champions toward contested ruins such as Andorhal and Scholomance. At the Bulwark’s barricades, High Executor Derrington gives orders to those crossing from Tirisfal Glades into the Western Plaguelands. He has little patience for political maneuvering in the Undercity and sees the front lines as a crucible of sheer survival. Horde soldiers and sellswords receive direct orders to scout plague-ridden territory and blunt enemy incursions before they reach Tirisfal. The Bulwark faces threats from the Scourge in Andorhal and from the Scarlet Crusade farther north. Scourge forces spread corruption through cauldrons in the countryside, while the Crusade’s zealous fanatics contest northern fortifications and skirmish relentlessly with Forsaken patrols. Derrington coordinates surgical counterattacks, sabotage against Scarlet lines, and systematic disruption of Scourge cauldron fields to protect the eastern border.

npc:high-priest-rohan.text: High Priest Rohan. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan guides the Church of the Holy Light from the Hall of Mysteries. He teaches young priests, helps them deepen their mastery of the Light, and keeps spiritual ties between Ironforge, Stormwind, and distant allies.
