High Priest Rohan paces the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward as the Church of the Holy Light’s highest-ranking representative in the city. Dwarves once honored the titans, yet their priests have embraced the Light’s wisdom, compassion, and justice. Rohan patiently teaches young acolytes to channel holy magic and steel their minds against despair. After priests under his care master the fundamentals, Rohan sends them abroad to learn from other traditions. Human and dwarven students go to High Priestess Laurena in Stormwind City. Night elf disciples travel to Priestess Alathea at Darnassus’s Temple of the Moon to study mysteries such as Elune’s Grace. Rohan also sends healers to aid the Cenarion Circle’s druids in distant Azshara, wherever hardship calls. Rohan keeps sacred relics for the Alliance priesthood and paladin brotherhoods. One is a blessed exorcism censer, used for years to cleanse vile spirits. When the Order of the Silver Hand and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker need it for their knights’ holy calling, Rohan lends it freely. He asks only for charitable alms to replenish Ironforge’s dwindling food reserves for the needy.

npc:highlord-demitrian.text: Highlord Demitrian. Highlord Demitrian is a solitary human hermit dwelling amidst the strange crystals of northwestern Silithus. Describing himself as a loyal servant of Prince Thunderaan, he possesses the esoteric knowledge required to wake the slumbering elemental lord. Adventurers bearing ancient elemental bindings seek him out to unlock the power of the Windseeker. Found lingering at an abandoned encampment in the Crystal Vale, Demitrian appears out of place in the desolate wastes of Silithus. Though he is tied to the Twilight's Hammer whose ravaged camp he haunts, Demitrian acts above all as a herald for Prince Thunderaan, the Windseeker. He treats visitors with aloof indifference unless they carry proof of the Windseeker's shattered essence.

npc:hogger.text: Hogger. In southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger leads the Riverpaw gnolls in raids on farms and travelers. His violent attacks have earned him a bounty from the Stormwind Marshals. Hogger commands the Riverpaw pack from Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest. Since the Third War, the gnolls have grown bolder and more coordinated in their raids on nearby homesteads. The Riverpaw have joined forces with the Defias Brotherhood, exchanging their raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To protect Elwynn's borders and trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has posted a bounty on Hogger's head.

npc:holt-thunderhorn.text: Holt Thunderhorn. On Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, Holt Thunderhorn trains tauren hunters for the Horde. He teaches tracking and survival, and points hunters toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. Holt Thunderhorn trains hunters for the Horde on Hunter Rise, above the plains of Mulgore. He teaches ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like other elders of his craft, he guides young tauren as they move from roaming hunters to disciplined defenders of their new capital.

npc:huldar.text: Huldar. Along Loch Modan’s southern road, Huldar’s powder run has come to a halt. His wagon carries blast powder for the southern dig, but threats on the road have put the delivery in danger. Huldar’s wagon is stranded on the road through southern Loch Modan. He was sent with loads of mining blast powder for the excavation site, where dwarven archaeologists and prospectors need supplies. Local wildlife and troggs threaten the route near the lake’s southern bend. Dark Iron infiltrators also lurk there. With his wagon damaged, Huldar depends on passing travelers to guard the remaining powder kegs and carry the shipment to the dig.

npc:illiyana-moonblaze.text: Illiyana Moonblaze. At Silverwing Grove, Illiyana Moonblaze supplies the Alliance champions fighting the Warsong Outriders. She works alongside the Silverwing Sentinels in Ashenvale. Illiyana Moonblaze keeps supplies for the Silverwing Sentinels at Silverwing Grove. Her post is near the path into Warsong Gulch, where she outfits defenders holding Ashenvale's southern woods against the Warsong clan. Illiyana equips Alliance volunteers preparing to fight the Warsong clan in Warsong Gulch. As champions earn favor with the Silverwing Sentinels, she provides custom rations, specialized draughts, and fine weapons for woodland skirmishes. She also repairs weapons and armor for weary fighters returning from the front, keeping the Sentinels supplied for war.

npc:ilthalaine.text: Ilthalaine. In Shadowglen, Ilthalaine keeps watch over the sacred glade and guides young night elves as they begin their lives in Teldrassil. He teaches them to defend their home and tend its balance. Ilthalaine watches the woodland paths just outside Shadowglen's heart. He sees changes in the forest that ordinary eyes miss. When young night elves awaken to their duties, he welcomes them and grounds them in Kaldorei traditions. His guidance prepares them to care for Teldrassil and shoulder the responsibilities of its defenders. Heavy spring rains have brought more nightsabers and thistle boars to Shadowglen than the glade can feed. Ilthalaine asks young defenders to thin their numbers, leaving room for the woodland's other creatures to flourish and restoring nature's balance. Ilthalaine tests young elves against local wildlife and points them toward their chosen callings. He gives each traveler a class sigil and directs them to their mentors in the Aldrassil sanctuary. Warriors, druids, rogues, priests, and hunters all find where their service to the Kaldorei begins.

npc:innkeeper-allison.text: Innkeeper Allison. In Stormwind's Trade District, Innkeeper Allison keeps the Gilded Rose ready for travelers and merchants. The busy inn stands between the bank and auction house, where she offers hearthstone bindings, drinks, and shelter. Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers at the Gilded Rose in Stormwind. The inn stands between the Trade District auction house and the city's main vaults, and its ground floor sees a steady flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. She keeps order behind the main counter and offers lodging and hearthstone services. Allison also joins local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest in the capital.

npc:innkeeper-farley.text: Innkeeper Farley. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Innkeeper Farley welcomes travelers with food, beds, and hearthstones. Well-liked and observant, he keeps misplaced mail and hears the troubles of those on the road. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall, and Duskwood find Innkeeper Farley behind the Lion's Pride Inn counter in Goldshire. He offers meals, ale, cheese, and a bed, and sets hearthstones for those who need one. With a welcoming hand and a sharp eye, Farley serves all who pass through this busy waystation and keeps order at the inn.

npc:innkeeper-firebrew.text: Innkeeper Firebrew. At Ironforge’s Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew keeps travelers fed and rested at the Stonefire Tavern. His hearty dwarven fare welcomes mountaineers and visiting dignitaries beneath the mountain. Innkeeper Firebrew welcomes travelers at the Stonefire Tavern in the Commons. The tavern sits in the Commons’ central ring, and many travelers entering Ironforge through the Great Gates find it first. Behind a counter laden with ale, stout, and roasted meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to those bound for Dun Morogh’s snowy passes or deeper into the mountain kingdom. Miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather there to escape the drafty tunnels and trade tales around the hearth. The Stonefire remains a lively crossroads in the heart of Ironforge.

npc:innkeeper-grosk.text: Innkeeper Grosk. At Razor Hill, Innkeeper Grosk welcomes travelers on the road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar. His inn offers food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Razor Hill links Durotar’s southern training grounds with Orgrimmar’s high walls. Innkeeper Grosk shelters warriors, scouts, and peons at his inn. Travelers find basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water beneath its sturdy timbers. Grosk also helps the laborers who keep Durotar running. Ukor, a timid peon, hauled food to the Valley of Trials only to learn it was not needed. He asks travelers to carry the load back to Grosk’s inn in Razor Hill.

npc:innkeeper-gryshka.text: Innkeeper Gryshka. At the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers with food, drink, and a hearthstone binding. She keeps the inn supplied with meat from hunters across Durotar and the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka welcomes travelers at the Broken Tusk in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The inn stands just beyond the city's main gates, where warriors, messengers, and newcomers to Thrall's Horde can find shelter. Gryshka keeps the Broken Tusk's kitchen supplied with fresh meat. Trusted hunters across Horde lands send her game, including Zargh at the Crossroads and Grimtak in Durotar, who ship their finest cuts to the inn.

npc:innkeeper-keldamyr.text: Innkeeper Keldamyr. In Dolanaar, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers food, drink, and a place to rest. Young night elves leaving Shadowglen can find shelter at his inn beneath the boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the first village many newcomers reach after leaving the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. At the village's central inn, Innkeeper Keldamyr offers bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath Teldrassil's canopy. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus pause at his counter to rest, bind their Hearthstones, and gather rations for the journey through the boughs. An inn high among the branches depends on steady supplies from nearby settlements and tradesfolk. Couriers bringing goods are often sent to Keldamyr's desk, tying his inn to the daily trade that keeps Dolanaar running.

npc:innkeeper-norman.text: Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman keeps the Trade Quarter tavern ready for travelers in the Undercity. The quiet, diligent Forsaken offers Horde travelers rest, hearthstone bindings, and food for the living and the dead. Beneath Lordaeron's ruined capital, Innkeeper Norman tends the main tavern in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold find lodging there. Travelers come to bind their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for journeys into the Plaguelands. Innkeeper Norman sells provisions and manages rooms through most of the year. During Hallow's End, he joins the holiday revelry and asks adventurous patrons for peculiar displays, such as clucking like a chicken. Those who oblige can earn holiday treats like Undercity mints.

npc:innkeeper-pala.text: Innkeeper Pala. On Thunder Bluff’s lower rise, travelers find Innkeeper Pala tending the Cat and the Shaman. She offers a place to rest, cold drinks, and a hearthstone binding for journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman on Thunder Bluff’s lower rise. Travelers arrive from the central lifts or the plains of Mulgore. In the common room, weary warriors, wandering druids, and the Horde’s visiting allies can find shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar place to rest.

npc:jahan-hawkwing.text: Jahan Hawkwing. At the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing keeps Horde travelers supplied with armor. The tauren armorer works from this outpost in the Barrens, where predators roam the plains. Jahan Hawkwing tends to the armor needs of Horde travelers and defenders at the Crossroads. In the Barrens, durable gear can mean survival against centaur, quilboar, and wild beasts. Jahan works with local leatherworkers, sending cured hides for delivery so his shop stays stocked with dependable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

npc:james-halloran.text: James Halloran. In Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes a living tanning crocolisk hides. Passing travelers and nearby trade channels help him gather raw skins and carry finished leather to buyers across the eastern continents. James Halloran lives and works in Menethil Harbor, earning his living from the marsh just outside town. The dangerous bogs provide crocolisk skins, which he turns into fine leather through rare craftsmanship. Nearby trade channels carry his finished goods to buyers across Azeroth. Halloran tends his curing vats and trade arrangements near the marsh, where danger is constant. He hires hardy travelers to skin young marsh beasts and handle routine deliveries between his work site and nearby settlements. Their help keeps his leather craft supplied while he manages the tanning and trade.

npc:jannok-breezesong.text: Jannok Breezesong. In Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong trains young night elf rogues. He teaches stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to kaldorei setting out beneath the World Tree's boughs. Beneath Dolanaar's boughs, Jannok Breezesong teaches novice night elf rogues. He trains those who work quietly beyond the ranks of Teldrassil's sentinels and druids. His lessons teach them to stalk through shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen among the boughs. When rogues finish their first lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok sends them to more experienced trainers in Darnassus.

npc:jasper-fel.text: Jasper Fel. In Stormwind's Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies daggers and vials from SI:7 headquarters. He keeps watch on visitors and warns them to mind their speech. Inside SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies the agents who work there. He offers simple daggers and empty vials for brewing and applying poisons. Jasper works under Mathias Shaw's intelligence division and warns visitors to mind their speech. In a place built for espionage, careless words can put people in danger.

npc:jen-shan.text: Jen'shan. In the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan teaches young hunters the ways of the wild. The Darkspear jungle troll trains orc and troll marksmen in tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Jen'shan trains new hunters in the Valley of Trials. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls come to her with inscribed tablets and parchments that direct them to her. She teaches them archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, preparing them for the scorpids and boars on the canyon floor.

npc:jennea-cannon.text: Jennea Cannon. In Stormwind, Jennea Cannon guides new mages through their first studies. From the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter, she teaches caution and self-control, and investigates disturbances in local arcane energies. At the top of the Wizard's Sanctum's spiral walkway, Jennea Cannon guides those who come to Stormwind to study the arcane. She teaches more than spells, insisting that students learn caution and self-control. Even those who do not study magic hear her warning: without training, magic can burn its wielder. Jennea sends promising apprentices beyond the city walls to test what they have learned. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, they study how natural water sources meet arcane resonance. As they advance, she sends them to investigate disturbances at the Blue Recluse or gather volatile reagents for their first true wizard's implements. When an apprentice outgrows Jennea's lessons, she points the way to greater masters. Those who show true potential may continue up the Sanctum's hierarchy with High Sorcerer Andromath, or travel beyond the kingdom to practitioners such as Tabetha, deep in the Dustwallow Marsh.

npc:jocaste.text: Jocaste. In Darnassus, Jocaste trains night elf hunters arriving from the wilds of Teldrassil. Jocaste trains night elf hunters in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Young trackers come to her after their first training in Shadowglen, ready to take up the hunt in the capital. She teaches marksmanship and survival in the wild, along with the bond between a hunter and the beasts of Kalimdor.

npc:john-j-keeshan.text: John J. Keeshan. Corporal John J. Keeshan is a human soldier of Stormwind's army who fought the Blackrock orcs in the Redridge Mountains. After being captured during the fighting around Stonewatch, he was dragged deep into Render's Rock as a prisoner of war. John J. Keeshan is a corporal in the service of Stormwind, posted to the Redridge Mountains as the Blackrock orcs pressed against Lakeshire and its defenders. When the fighting flared up around Stonewatch Keep, Keeshan was in the thick of it alongside the other soldiers holding the line for the kingdom.

npc:jorah-annison.text: Jorah Annison. In the Magic Quarter, Jorah Annison helps spellcasters find knowledge scattered across Azeroth. The Forsaken cartographer knows both the land and the ancient texts warlocks seek. Jorah Annison makes maps in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, but the work does not hold his interest. He would trade every map in the shop for one good book. Jorah knows more about ancient texts than almost anyone, and warlocks share his taste for a scholar's work. Warlocks seeking the elusive Tome of the Cabal are often sent to Jorah Annison. His knowledge reaches beyond the ruins of Lordaeron, and he can point them toward places where ancient texts and remnants of dark sects might be found. He joins the study of old lore to the geography of distant lands.

npc:jorgen.text: Jorgen. Jorgen keeps watch beside the water at Stormwind's Valley of Heroes entrance. His quiet perch draws people with matters they cannot discuss openly. Jorgen keeps to the water just right of Stormwind's great entrance. Above him, statues of heroes look over the bridge, while he watches those who come and go below. People seeking information they want kept off the record can find a quiet contact there.

npc:josef-gregorian.text: Josef Gregorian. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Josef Gregorian trains tailors of the Horde. His skill guides them toward enchanted fabrics and specialized garments. Josef Gregorian teaches tailoring in the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, where Forsaken and their Horde allies practice the craft. Tailoring remains vital to warlocks, mages, and priests who channel raw energies through woven fibers. Gregorian teaches foundational patterns and stitches the first robes for young mages who bring him the right materials.

npc:kaal-soulreaper.text: Kaal Soulreaper. In the Undercity, orc warlock Kaal Soulreaper trains apprentices and keeps close ties with practitioners of the dark arts across the Horde. Among the Forsaken, he guides students toward mentors in distant lands. Kaal Soulreaper works in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, where Horde warlocks come to learn from his mastery of demonic entities and curses. Thrall's Horde strictly regulates and monitors fel magic within Orgrimmar, while the subterranean sanctums of Lordaeron offer practitioners like Kaal ample harbor. Beyond teaching, Kaal connects those seeking greater power with mentors across the sea, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens.

npc:kali-remik.text: Kali Remik. In Sen'jin Village, Kali Remik guides young hunters toward their next training. She is a Darkspear troll hunter who knows the tracking and survival ways of Durotar. Kali Remik guides young scouts in Sen'jin Village, where they begin their lives beyond the Valley of Trials. A Darkspear troll tracker, she knows Durotar's dry lands and the Horde's settlements. When a novice is ready to leave the local training grounds, Kali sends promising hunters to Thotar in Razor Hill. There they begin learning to tame beasts, strengthening the Horde's frontier ranks.

npc:kaltunk.text: Kaltunk. At the heart of the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Kaltunk welcomes young orcs and points them toward their first duties for the Horde. Kaltunk watches over new arrivals in the Valley of Trials and directs them toward Gornek and the path of discipline. While trainers and elders set trials and hunting rites, the orc overseer gives recruits clear orders so they know where to go. The Valley of Trials was chosen to test the strength and resilience of the youths who walk its canyon floors. Kaltunk brings the same rugged practicality to his work. He offers no grand speeches or coddling, and expects each orc to find a place in the world and serve the warchief.

npc:kanati-greycloud.text: Kanati Greycloud. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter stationed at Whitereach Post within Thousand Needles. Alongside his hunting companions, he musters what defense he can while enduring constant hostility from the local Galak centaur. Kanati Greycloud makes his camp at Whitereach Post, high atop the sandstone spires of western Thousand Needles. While the canyon offers abundant game and open vistas, it is hemmed in by the Galak centaur, whose warbands contest every inch of the arid flats below. Together with other tauren hunters, Kanati keeps watch over the canyon floor, striving to preserve the post against the brutal depredations of the surrounding marauders.

npc:kaplak.text: Kaplak. In Razor Hill, Kaplak trains young orc and troll rogues for the Horde. He teaches stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft before sending them to Orgrimmar. Kaplak trains new Horde rogues in Razor Hill. Orcish custom favors open combat and roaring charges, but he teaches the quieter skills needed to survive: stalking unseen, picking locks, and striking from behind. When his students outgrow his training in Durotar's dusty red ravines, he sends them north to Orgrimmar, where senior guild operatives can deepen their craft.

npc:karang-amakkar.text: Karang Amakkar. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Karang Amakkar watches Ashenvale's rocky coast and the threats closing in around the Horde. At Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, Karang Amakkar guards one of the Horde's most exposed borders. The camp faces pressure from the sea, the night elves, and wild beasts inland. Karang watches the hostile peoples along the road east, guarding Horde couriers and scouts from ambush by tribes defending their territory. Karang Amakkar gives much of his attention to the furbolgs of the ancient woods, especially the Foulweald tribe. Corruption and primal hostility drive these bear-folk into frenzies. Karang sends capable warriors to bring down their leader and clear their dens before the tribes can gather for an organized assault on Zoram'gar.

npc:kargal-battlescar.text: Kargal Battlescar. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar guards the eastern edge of the Barrens. He watches the crossing from Durotar, judges incoming recruits, and sends capable fighters west to strengthen Horde defenses. Kargal Battlescar watches the road into the Barrens from the Far Watch Post. Travelers and new adventurers cross the bridge over the Southfury River, leaving the Valley of Trials behind. The Barrens is a dangerous, contested land, where aggressive wildlife, centaur raiders, and quilboar tribes threaten the frontier. Kargal inspects those who pass and gathers willing recruits for the Horde. He sends them onward to the Crossroads, where they can aid local commanders in securing the frontier.

npc:karos-razok.text: Karos Razok. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Karos Razok keeps the Forsaken bat roost ready. Karos Razok tends the skeletal bats from the wooden platform above the Sepulcher's crypts. Moonrage worgen, rogue Dalaran magi, and the human remnants of Ambermill make the northern road through Silverpine Forest treacherous. Razok keeps messengers, fresh recruits, and vital supplies moving above the haunted canopy, linking the frontier outpost to the capital in Tirisfal Glades.

npc:katie-hunter.text: Katie Hunter. At the Eastvale Logging Camp stables, Katie Hunter tends horses for Stormwind and trusted Alliance champions. She works with Randal Hunter to keep travelers and soldiers mounted for the kingdom’s roads. Katie Hunter tends the horses at the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. While lumberjacks cut timber for Stormwind’s reconstruction, she raises dependable pintos, mares, and swift steeds for riders. Her horses carry people along the kingdom’s roads and the dangerous routes of southern Azeroth.

npc:kaymard-copperpinch.text: Kaymard Copperpinch. In Orgrimmar, Kaymard Copperpinch sells Smokywood Pastures goods for Winter Veil. He trades in the Valley of Strength, where travelers can find festive wares and help with holiday troubles. Kaymard Copperpinch brings Smokywood Pastures to the Valley of Strength each Feast of Winter Veil. Great-father Winter receives visitors nearby as Kaymard sells fine treats, festive wrapping paper, and other holiday goods. To a goblin, no grand festival is complete without a lively exchange of coin. Kaymard also handles troubles that threaten Smokywood Pastures during the festival. Holiday confections go missing, and Metzen the Reindeer disappears. Kaymard calls on Horde adventurers to solve these problems and keep Winter Veil running smoothly.

npc:keeper-albagorm.text: Keeper Albagorm. At Stonetalon Peak, Keeper Albagorm watches the Charred Vale burn and seeks help healing the wilds. Keeper Albagorm guards the night elven refuge at Stonetalon Peak. Like other sons of Cenarius, he feels the pain of the natural world. South of the peak, the Charred Vale lies scorched by a greedy mechanized army of industrialists. Bloodfury harpies now hold the ruins and prevent new growth. From his sanctuary, Albagorm works to halt the corruption and restore balance to the wounded forest.

npc:keeper-bel-dugur.text: Keeper Bel'dugur. In the Undercity, Keeper Bel'dugur commissions expeditions to recover dark tomes and magical artifacts for his people. The scholarly Forsaken works deep within the Apothecarium. Among the Apothecarium's vats and researchers, Keeper Bel'dugur sends adventurers to recover dangerous arcane and occult relics from across Azeroth. The Book of Ur, a legendary treatise on extra-dimensional beings, is locked away inside Shadowfang Keep and draws his keen interest. While many in the Undercity seek magical knowledge to cure or weaponize undeath, Bel'dugur's curated acquisitions seem chosen to uncover ancient, forbidden powers.

npc:keeper-bel-varil.text: Keeper Bel'varil. At Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil studies magic and alchemy for the Forsaken. His work with Wordeen Voidglare draws Horde adventurers into the search for relics and binding materials across Hillsbrad Foothills. Keeper Bel'varil supports Forsaken magic and alchemy in besieged Tarren Mill. The royal apothecaries and soldiers focus on the Alliance garrison down the road at Southshore. Bel'varil turns to practical sorcery, sending travelers to recover stone tokens and binding bracers from nearby elemental and enchanted threats.

npc:keldran.text: Keldran. North of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar, Keldran works to clear a path toward peace with the Alliance. He directs covert strikes against demonic remnants, hoping to show that the modern Horde has forsaken the Burning Legion. Keldran works from Orgrimmar’s red rock terraces while Thrall governs from the Valley of Wisdom. The Alliance still sees all orcs as bloodthirsty puppets of demonic masters, a reputation forged during the first wars. Keldran believes Thrall is weary of endless conflict, but peace talks cannot begin while demon-worshiping cults endure in Kalimdor. Without the Warchief’s formal sanction, he takes the initiative himself. He directs trusted agents toward distant threats, hoping to erase the demonic stain and clear the way for diplomacy.

npc:kelm-hargunth.text: Kelm Hargunth. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth keeps the Warsong Outriders supplied. He equips Horde champions fighting night elves in Warsong Gulch with care packages and provisions. At Mor'shan Base Camp, Kelm Hargunth manages supplies for the Warsong Outriders. The camp stands on the northern edge of the Barrens, beside the border with Ashenvale. Scouts and raiders skirmish beyond its stockade while Kelm sees that weapons, armor, and rations reach the fighters. The Warsong Outriders face the Silverwing Sentinels, and a steady flow of provisions matters as much as fury in battle. Kelm gives specialized supplies to warriors who have proven themselves in Warsong Gulch. His stores include care packages with field dressings and iron rations, along with armaments marked with the Warsong clan's crimson insignia. These supplies go to fighters serving the Horde's campaign in the forests to the north.

npc:kerlonian-evershade.text: Kerlonian Evershade. At the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade wakes from a long sleep in the Emerald Dream. The night elf Druid of the Claw needs help crossing the troubled wilds to reach Maestra's Post. Kerlonian Evershade follows the bear totem as one of the Druids of the Claw. For centuries, these druids slept in barrows and communed with the Emerald Dream. They were called from their slumber during the Third War. Now Kerlonian rests beneath the ancient trees of the Grove of the Ancients, still shaking off the supernatural grogginess of his long sleep. He must travel through Darkshore's troubled forests to reach Maestra's Post on the Ashenvale border. The road from the Grove of the Ancients is dangerous. Blackwood furbolgs prowl the Twilight Vale, while Dark Strand cultists lurk along the road into Ashenvale. Sleep has weakened Kerlonian, and sudden bouts of exhaustion still trouble him. He depends on sympathetic Alliance travelers for protection as he journeys south to rejoin his fellow night elves.

npc:kernobee.text: Kernobee. Deep within Gnomeregan, Kernobee is trapped among the ruins. The goblin engineer uncovered Dark Iron involvement in the super rig, then was captured, beaten unconscious, and left in the dormitory quarters among the troggs. While doing business or scavenging in Gnomeregan, Kernobee discovered the Dark Iron dwarves had helped build and operate the great super rig burrowing beneath the city. Knowing how dangerous this knowledge was, he tried to flee to Ratchet and warn his associate, Tinkerwiz. The Dark Irons caught him before he could escape. Kernobee's captors beat him unconscious instead of killing him. They threw him into a small room along the dormitory corridor, opposite the Clean Zone. Feral troggs and radiation surround him, and he needs help to wake, reach safety, and get clear of the ruins.

npc:keryn-sylvius.text: Keryn Sylvius. On the second floor of Goldshire’s Lion’s Pride Inn, Keryn Sylvius trains young rogues. In the reading room, she teaches stealth and bladecraft and quietly guides promising operatives toward Stormwind’s intelligence service. Keryn Sylvius keeps to the reading room above the Lion’s Pride Inn. Downstairs, travelers crowd the floor with town guards, while upstairs she watches the steady flow of road gossip. She mentors rogues learning their trade in Elwynn Forest. When promising operatives outgrow petty theft and roadside skulduggery, Sylvius discreetly sends them to Stormwind City to contact SI:7.

npc:khelden-bremen.text: Khelden Bremen. On the upper floor of Northshire Abbey, Khelden Bremen teaches human mages their first spells. He prepares novices to serve Stormwind through the arcane arts. Khelden Bremen teaches new human mages in a study on the upper floor of Northshire Abbey. While clergy and defenders pursue their work below, he shows novices how to focus and shape magical energy safely. His lessons prepare them for the road through Elwynn Forest and for further study in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

npc:kil-hala.text: Kil'hala. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala teaches Horde tailors to work cloth. He also weaves nether-lace robes for young Horde mages who bring him locks of hair from Ashenvale's laughing sisters. Kil'hala trains tailors at the Crossroads, where Horde recruits and travelers can learn his craft. He teaches work with common spun bolts and garments suited to life on the dry plains. At Deino's request, he also makes nether-lace robes for young mages who bring him hair from the laughing sisters, the dryads of Ashenvale's forests.

npc:kin-weelay.text: Kin'weelay. Kin'weelay is a renowned Darkspear witch doctor stationed at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Dispatched directly from Orgrimmar, he offers mystical aid and counsel to the Horde vanguard in the jungle. His spiritual expertise is vital in unravelling dark mojo and aiding the rescue of young Yenniku. Recognized among the Darkspear as one of their most powerful practitioners of traditional witchcraft, Kin'weelay commands deep knowledge of spirits, hexes, and soul magic. When matters involving ancestral spirits or hostile troll enchantments arise, Horde scouts in Stranglethorn Vale look to him to pierce the magical veil.

npc:kindal-moonweaver.text: Kindal Moonweaver. Kindal Moonweaver is a night elf secluded within a concealed nook in the craggy mountains of Feralas, just north of the Grimtotem Compound. Deeply troubled by the mistreatment of wildlife in the wilderness, she watches the aggressive tauren tribe below while seeking help to free captured beasts. She is kin to Jer'kai Moonweaver, sharing a mission to defend the forest's innocent creatures. Perched upon a narrow, winding mountain path partially hidden behind timber east of Dire Maul, Kindal Moonweaver maintains a secret vigil over the valley below. While much of Feralas is contested between the Horde, the night elves of Feathermoon, and the ancient ruins of Eldre'Thalas, Kindal focuses on a more localized and immediate cruelty. Down in the hollow, the Grimtotem tribe operates a fortified compound, capturing and penning up local fauna for reasons far from benign. From her concealed overlook, Kindal watches for anyone willing to brave the enemy camp and undo the suffering inside. Kindal's primary concern lies with the sacred balance and gentle creatures of Feralas that cannot defend themselves against brutish captors. Along with her kin, Jer'kai Moonweaver, she seeks the emancipation of caged beasts and looks out for young animals left stranded by violent poaching. Rather than engaging in grand territorial war, her attention is fixed on compassion: freeing caged sprites and finding a home for an orphaned sprite darter.

npc:kirge-sternhorn.text: Kirge Sternhorn. In the Barrens, Kirge Sternhorn guides travelers crossing central Kalimdor. The tauren keeps watch over the southern trails and sends new Horde adventurers north to the Crossroads. New wanderers often find the sun-baked Barrens daunting. Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers south of the central trails, between the southern camps and the heart of Kalimdor. Marauding quilboar and fierce predators roam the savanna, and Kirge helps young adventurers find their footing. He ensures they seek out the greater Horde presence gathering to the north.

npc:klannoc-macleod.text: Klannoc Macleod. On Fray Island, Klannoc Macleod puts warriors to the test. The human warrior welcomes fighters from both the Alliance and the Horde who seek mastery of combat stances. Those who earn his respect are sent inland to face greater trials of strength. Klannoc Macleod puts seasoned fighters through their paces on Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast in the Barrens. Though human, he leaves Alliance and Horde quarrels aside. He judges each contender by grit, blade work, and resolve under fire. Klannoc Macleod's trial on Fray Island is called the Affray. Contenders climb onto raised iron grating and face relentless waves of eager brawlers as he watches. Those who endure the onslaught and defeat his chosen champion earn his approval and prove they have the temperament for berserker training.

npc:kor-ghan.text: Kor'ghan. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Kor'ghan watches over remedies and toxins. The Darkspear troll stands outside Rekkul's Poisons and seeks help preparing antidotes for Durotar’s venomous predators. Kor'ghan keeps watch over remedies and toxins outside Rekkul's Poisons in Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow. From the capital, he sends travelers into Durotar’s red canyons to gather venomous components from scorpids. He needs them to prepare antidotes for the dangers of the wilderness.

npc:korran.text: Korran. At the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens for threats to the Horde. The Darkspear troll serves Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar and studies the silithid emerging across the scrublands. At the Crossroads, Korran watches for threats beyond the quilboar and centaur clans. Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar stationed the troll scout there to observe changes in the land. Korran coordinates the gathering of intelligence for the Horde's leadership. Korran now focuses on the Field of Giants in the southern Barrens. Strange, aggressive insectoid creatures called silithid have begun burrowing into the earth. To learn where the swarm came from and what danger it poses to the young Horde, Korran asks passing adventurers to dig up intact eggs with his claw tool.

npc:kravel-koalbeard.text: Kravel Koalbeard. Kravel Koalbeard is a scheming dwarven entrepreneur and con artist stationed out at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Rather than cheering purely for the love of the sport, he views the fierce gnome and goblin racing rivalry as a golden opportunity to fill his pockets. From scavenging stray machine parts to fixing race results through blackmail and booze, Kravel is always hunting for his next profitable scheme. While most spectators and crew members at the Mirage Raceway are consumed by mechanical rivalries and the roar of rocket engines, Kravel Koalbeard has his eyes squarely on everyone's coin purses. He is an opportunist who operates in the dusty cracks of the raceway encampment, quick to offer contracts and favors that rarely have clean motives. Kravel sees the high-stakes friction between gnome and goblin engineers not as an inspiring competition, but as a fertile ground for extortion, sabotage, and theft.

npc:kreldig-ungor.text: Kreldig Ungor. Kreldig Ungor is an enterprising dwarven operative representing Reclaimers Inc., stationed high among the crags of Nijel's Point in Desolace. Tasked with managing field operations in the barren wasteland, he hires Alliance adventurers to recover lost cargo and secure valuable local reagents. His salvage and recovery contracts make him a central contact for travelers navigating the hostile region. Nijel's Point offers the Alliance a rare sanctuary amid the blighted canyons of Desolace, making it an ideal staging ground for commercial opportunists like Kreldig Ungor. Representing Reclaimers Inc., Kreldig has ventured far from the safety of Khaz Modan into a desolate wilderness contested by centaur clans, demons, and the Horde. Where others see ruin and ash, Kreldig sees untapped profit and lost assets ripe for recovery. A primary venture bringing Kreldig to Desolace involves the lost vessel of Karnitol, which wrecked along the treacherous western coast. Karnitol's shipment held prized goods, and Kreldig orchestrates efforts to track down the debris and retrieve the scattered cargo before scavengers or coastal sea giants can claim it all. Beyond maritime salvage, Kreldig oversees the procurement of Desolace's strange biological and mineral treasures for Reclaimers Inc. The harsh environment breeds unique fauna and flora, whose parts fetch high prices among alchemists and engineers back in the Eastern Kingdoms. Adventurers willing to brave the wasteland's predators find steady pay beneath Kreldig's ledger.

npc:krolg.text: Krolg. South of Mystral Lake, Krolg lives uncorrupted in an isolated hut in Ashenvale. Cast out from the Foulweald tribe, he kept his sanity when his kin fell to demonic madness. He speaks only with those who appear to be furbolgs. South of Mystral Lake, Krolg remains lucid and untouched by madness. Most Foulweald furbolgs in Ashenvale have succumbed to the demonic taint left by the Burning Legion. In his secluded shelter, Krolg keeps a cautious vigil over the forest. He witnessed his brethren descend into senseless violence, and now speaks only with beings who appear to be kin.

npc:krom-stoutarm.text: Krom Stoutarm. In Ironforge, Krom Stoutarm studies the darker arts in the Hall of Explorers. A dwarven scholar and warlock, he reads arcane texts and demonic rites in the library, and guides Alliance warlocks seeking esoteric knowledge across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Krom Stoutarm pursues occult lore in the Hall of Explorers. While dwarven archaeologists there focus on picks, shovels, and titan artifacts, Krom studies massive tomes and the rites used to bind demons. His work gives a warlock’s craft a place within Ironforge’s mountain halls, though many distrust those arts. Alliance warlocks seeking to bind powerful demons such as the felhunter turn to Krom Stoutarm. He knows of occult volumes scattered across distant lands and directs summoners to recover torn pages and fragments of the infamous Tome of the Cabal, including from the centaur of Thousand Needles.

npc:krusk.text: Krusk. At Tarren Mill, Krusk coordinates the search for his captured scouts and the Syndicate's relics. Sent by Warchief Thrall to investigate Durnholde Keep, he survived an ambush that scattered his team. Krusk leads the effort from Tarren Mill after a failed strike at Durnholde Keep. Warchief Thrall sent him and a small team to scout Syndicate activity and recover relics tied to the fortress's grim past. The human outlaws were more entrenched and coordinated than expected, and an ambush inside the crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scouts. Krusk fought his way out. Drull and Tog'thar were taken captive and locked within the ruins, while Gol'dir, the expedition's leader, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Krusk now directs Horde forces to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and free his trapped comrades. From Tarren Mill, Krusk tracks the Syndicate's movements in Hillsbrad. The fallen nobles of Alterac operate from Durnholde Keep, plotting against Horde outposts and their former Alliance brethren. Krusk watches leaders such as Lord Aliden Perenolde, hoping to break their command before they threaten the Horde's tenuous foothold in Lordaeron.

npc:kuray-bin.text: Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin watches the forest trails outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. The Darkspear scout guards the Horde encampment from night elf scouts. Outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin watches the forest for Alliance scouts. Silverwing Sentinels patrol the canopy and send swift outrunners across the border. Their task is to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Kuray'bin sends Horde fighters to hunt the outrunners before they can report to Silverwing Outpost, since scouts left unchecked can become an ambushing force.

npc:kzan-thornslash.text: Kzan Thornslash. In the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to new Horde recruits. He is an orc merchant in Durotar. Kzan Thornslash supplies weapons to young orcs and Darkspear trolls in the Valley of Trials. They are taking their first steps as Horde warriors. He offers basic hand axes, shortswords, clubs, and staves for recruits facing local wildlife and hazards.

npc:laird.text: Laird. At Auberdine's inn, Laird sells fish and cooking supplies to travelers along Darkshore's coast. Laird sells fish and supplies inside Auberdine's inn. Sailors, locals, and travelers come to him while Darkshore's waters churn with dangers greater than those along Teldrassil's sheltered shores. For anglers willing to cast from the misty beaches, the local catch can bring a handsome profit. Laird stays in touch with fishing operations across the channel in Teldrassil. Shipments come from his fellow fisher Nessa Shadowsong, linking Rut'theran Village with the mainland port and keeping coastal trade moving.

npc:lakota-windsong.text: Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

npc:lanka-farshot.text: Lanka Farshot. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot guides young tauren onto the hunter's path. He is stationed within the Red Cloud Mesa and teaches tracking, marksmanship, and survival on Mulgore's plains. At Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot welcomes new tauren called to the hunter's path. Fresh recruits arrive with an etched note that sends them to seek his counsel. Under his guidance, they learn ranged combat, how to track prey, and respect for the wild beasts roaming Mulgore's grassy plains. He prepares each young hunter to scout and provide for the tribe.

npc:lar-prowltusk.text: Lar Prowltusk. Southwest of Sen'jin Village, Lar Prowltusk watches the Durotar frontier. He guards the young troll settlement and sends travelers against nearby threats. Lar Prowltusk watches the coast southwest of Sen'jin Village. As a Darkspear sentinel, he helps guard the tribe's new home after its people fled their sunken island chain. Hostile neighbors keep harassing Sen'jin Village as the trolls work to secure a permanent home. Lar directs scouts and warriors to watch the coast and curb these attacks, especially those by the Kolkar centaur, giving the settlement room to breathe.

npc:laris-geardawdle.text: Laris Geardawdle. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth. The gnome researcher gives his academic life to their strange nature and origins, and welcomes adventurers who bring him noxious slime samples. In the Library of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle studies how oozes begin. His dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, but Laris searches the vile, gelatinous horrors of Azeroth for alchemical and biological secrets. He asks roving explorers to gather caustic samples from remote corners of the world. With them, he tests his unusual ideas about how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

npc:lars.text: Lars. At a camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars struggles to survive Duskwood with Sven Yorgen. The woods around them hold beasts, undead, and worgen. Lars keeps to a small camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, away from the uncertain safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is dangerous, and the surrounding woods hold ferocious beasts, undead, and worgen. He stays close to Sven Yorgen, trying to survive in the hostile forest. Starving dire wolves prowl the woods around Lars and Sven's camp. Lars cannot keep watch or drive them off alone, so he depends on travelers to thin their packs before the predators overrun the camp.

npc:lelanai.text: Lelanai. In Darnassus, Lelanai cares for the night elves’ saber mounts in the Cenarion Enclave. She offers nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of the city. Lelanai tends the great cats of Kalimdor in the Cenarion Enclave, beside riding instructor Jartsam. Night elves have long bonded with the fierce predators of northern forests. They train nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged ground with a predator’s grace. In the capital, Lelanai provides these mounts to riders. Lelanai offers saber mounts to night elves with the proper skill, while outsiders face a higher bar. The cats are sacred to the kaldorei, who keep their distance from strangers. She entrusts a mount to a non-night elf only when they have earned the highest respect and renown with Darnassus.

npc:lieutenant-haggerdin.text: Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone. Serving the Stormpike Expedition, Haggerdin ensures that only tested warriors represent Ironforge and the Grand Alliance in the valley. Through challenges like the Proving Grounds, he tasks recruits with recovering banners and relics, and bestows official commendations, insignias, and rank recognitions as soldiers rise through the ranks of the Stormpike Guard.

npc:lieutenant-lisande.text: Lieutenant Lisande. On Thunder Bluff’s high mesas, Lieutenant Lisande watches for signs of the Scourge. Lieutenant Lisande serves the Argent Dawn from Thunder Bluff, where human faces are rare. The holy order watches for signs of the Lich King's taint, even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, Lisande calls on Horde champions to ride out and investigate before the Scourge can defile the sacred earth.

npc:lieutenant-nevell.text: Lieutenant Nevell. Outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh, Lieutenant Nevell watches for the Scourge. The Argent Dawn officer coordinates local defenders and warns arriving adventurers of undead threats near the dwarven kingdom. Lieutenant Nevell watches Ironforge's snowy approaches for the Scourge. Though the Argent Dawn is best known for holding the line in Lordaeron's shattered Plaguelands, its watch reaches farther south. From outside Ironforge, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front when Scourge activity stirs in Dun Morogh's mountain passes. The dwarven city's borders remain under watch.

npc:lieutenant-orrin.text: Lieutenant Orrin. At Stormwind's gates, Lieutenant Orrin watches for Scourge incursions and calls for scouts. The Argent Dawn officer stands in the Valley of Heroes, where he directs recruits to investigate undead threats beyond the capital. Lieutenant Orrin watches the road from the Valley of Heroes. The Argent Dawn is known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, but it also guards strongholds farther south, including Stormwind City. When necromantic magic stirs beyond the capital, Orrin sounds the alarm and rallies adventurers before the undead can threaten the people within. Lieutenant Orrin connects the Argent Dawn with volunteers in the southern kingdom. When signs of the Scourge appear beyond Stormwind's gates, he sends scouts to gather intelligence and secure hazardous artifacts. Cracked necrotic crystals are among the objects they recover, helping the order understand and repel the undead threat.

npc:loganaar.text: Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites. Beyond fundamental spellcraft, Loganaar prepares students for the ultimate destiny shared by Kalimdor's traditional protectors: the deep slumber of the Emerald Dream. He instructs initiates on the sacred connection between Azeroth's primal spirit realm and the waking world, reminding them that true mastery will one day require hibernating for centuries to walk among nature's purest, unblemished forms under the guidance of the demigods.

npc:lomac-gearstrip.text: Lomac Gearstrip. In Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues gnomish inventions. He formulated the NG-5 explosive and keeps in contact with fellow researchers in Kalimdor. Lomac Gearstrip works on gnomish ordnance in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Like many gnomes who fled Gnomeregan's tragedy, he has brought his tinkering operations to the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions meant to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds. Lomac's proudest contribution to combat engineering is the NG-5 explosive. The compound is made for maximum destructive yield and requires precise handling and rare chemical reagents. To refine and use such hazardous inventions in the field, Lomac stays in contact with former colleagues stationed in distant theaters. They exchange technical orders and dangerous supplies across the Great Sea.

npc:longbraid-the-grim.text: Longbraid the Grim. Outside fallen Dun Modr, Longbraid the Grim keeps watch over the northern Wetlands. He mourns his brother and the loss of the Thandol Span, while leading the surviving dwarves against the Dark Iron clan. Longbraid the Grim rallies the dwarven garrison near the bridge to the Arathi Highlands. The Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr in a sudden assault that devastated the defenders. Longbraid's brother died during the siege of the Thandol Span. Grief and hatred keep Longbraid at the northern boundary, where he directs travelers and surviving mountaineers in strikes against the Dark Iron advance. Longbraid also directs dwarven operations across the Wetlands. He sent soldiers to escort Prospector Whelgar into the marshlands and works to reclaim Dun Modr's lost fortifications. He vows retribution against the Dark Iron saboteurs.

npc:loramus-thalipedes.text: Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

npc:lord-arkkoroc.text: Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

npc:lord-baurles-k-wishock.text: Lord Baurles K. Wishock. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock lives among the petitioners and dignitaries. Barkeeps know him for unpaid tabs and a taste for strong drink, but his nights in the city’s underbelly brought him near darker dealings. Lord Baurles K. Wishock moves among petitioners and dignitaries in Stormwind Keep, where he belongs to the influential House of Nobles. Though his station is high, he often drinks in the Mage Quarter’s dive bars, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, and leaves large bills unpaid. There, he hears of a warlock coven practicing dark arts in cellars beneath the floorboards. Wishock sets out to have the tavern closed and asks fellow nobles for a formal investigation. Uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

npc:lord-grayson-shadowbreaker.text: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker trains champions of the Light. A veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he guides promising knights and oversees the sacred trials senior paladins must complete to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker leads the Silver Hand's work in Stormwind City and ranks among the Alliance's foremost defenders. A veteran of the order, he trains recruits in arms and tests their faith in the Light. When promising knights are ready, he sends them north to the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands. There, they aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

npc:lord-jorach-ravenholdt.text: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

npc:lord-maxwell-tyrosus.text: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade. Tyrosus now leads the Argent Dawn and oversees the defenses of Light's Hope Chapel. From his command post within the chapel, he oversees broad military operations across the Plaguelands, including tactical assaults led by Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff against Baron Rivendare inside the ruins of Stratholme.

npc:lord-shalzaru.text: Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering. During excavations south of the primary ruins across the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru personally uncovered a strange, ancient relic. The purpose and power of this artifact remain a mystery, but its recovery by such a powerful naga warlord presents a clear threat. Operatives on the mainland seek brave champions to venture into the serpent's den, end Shalzaru's command, and secure the odd relic before the Hatecrest can turn it to darker ends.

npc:lorekeeper-raintotem.text: Lorekeeper Raintotem. South of Red Rocks, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends Mulgore’s sacred burial grounds. He asks travelers to drive off Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Lorekeeper Raintotem tends his people’s sacred burial grounds near Red Rocks in Mulgore. Bristleback Interlopers disturb the resting place, and he asks travelers to drive them away so the ancestors may rest in peace. Lorekeeper Raintotem watches over the burial sites at Red Rocks. Bristleback quilboar disturb the resting places of tauren chieftains and shamans. Raintotem calls on travelers to restore quiet and dignity to the grounds and their dead.

npc:loslor-rudge.text: Loslor Rudge. At Steelgrill's Depot, Loslor Rudge keeps Dun Morogh's tinkerers supplied. His tools, parts, and munitions reach craftsmen across the snowy ridges, including gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot. Loslor Rudge supplies engineering goods from Steelgrill's Depot, just down the road from Kharanos. His stock includes copper modulators, bronze tubing, blasting powder, and spanners. Harsh weather and scattered tinker operations keep practical parts in demand, and Loslor works to keep local gearheads supplied. The wilderness between outposts makes deliveries perilous. A courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was driven off by wendigos, leaving behind an ammunition shipment meant for Loslor's valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot.

npc:lotwil-veriatus.text: Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

npc:lucius.text: Lucius. At the Lakeshire docks, Lucius watches the Redridge waterfront. The dwarf works undercover for Stormwind’s SI:7, helping agents with reconnaissance and trade skills. Lucius watches the Lakeshire docks for SI:7, Stormwind’s intelligence service. He keeps an eye on trade, unusual traffic, and threats moving into the Redridge Mountains. Agents sent east from Stormwind come to him to coordinate covert work and practice field skills such as lockpicking. Through Lucius, Stormwind keeps a hidden reach beyond Elwynn Forest.

npc:lyria-du-lac.text: Lyria Du Lac. In Goldshire, Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors behind the village smithy. She teaches them to master their stances and arms. Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors in the yard behind Goldshire's forge. She teaches those fresh from Northshire Abbey, judges their readiness, and introduces specialized combat techniques. Warriors take up shield and blade for Stormwind, facing the threats of Elwynn Forest.

npc:ma-stonefield.text: Ma Stonefield. At Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn, Ma Stonefield tends to hardships close to home. Beside Auntie Bernice, she faces farm troubles, neighboring rivalries, and pests. Ma Stonefield watches over the farm beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, with Auntie Bernice Stonefield at her side. The neighboring Maclure homestead and nearby pumpkin patches bring little peace. Wild boars threaten the Stonefield crops, and Princess causes the greatest trouble. The enormous prize sow tramples fields and devours the harvest the family worked hard to grow.

npc:mad-magus-tirth.text: Magus Tirth. Magus Tirth is an eccentric human wizard dwelling out on the salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Known locally for breeding chickens and tormenting his polymorphed apprentice, he is also a scholar of formidable arcane lore who has squandered valuable tomes on racing bets. While most mages of his caliber study in the libraries of Dalaran or Stormwind, Magus Tirth has taken up residence amid the grease and roar of the Shimmering Flats. Surrounded by speeding rocket cars, Tirth peddles chickens to passersby, drinks, gambles, and has long since cursed his unfortunate apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, into poultry form. Despite this eccentric demeanor, Tirth possesses genuine arcane mastery, having authored esoteric texts on magical power before losing them to reckless wagers on the speedway.

npc:magga.text: Magga. Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Magga welcomes new arrivals. The orc lives in Durotar and greets Horde travelers beginning their journey through the valley. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls first meet the wider world in the Valley of Trials. Near the Den, Magga greets those arriving in the valley. Trainers and recruits keep busy nearby, while Magga helps bring the small camp together.

npc:magis-sparkmantle.text: Magis Sparkmantle. In Kharanos, Magis Sparkmantle trains gnome mages inside the Thunderbrew Distillery. He guides fledgling spellcasters who travel from Coldridge Valley into Dun Morogh. Dwarves gather at the Thunderbrew Distillery for ale, and Magis Sparkmantle teaches among its casks and kegs. Gnome mages work closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh. Magis helps novice spellcasters deepen their knowledge of the arcane and put it into practice. Magis teaches beginners their first incantations and points promising students toward wider circles of magic. When they outgrow his early lessons or need specialized guidance, he sends them to other practitioners, including Bink, or to mentors in the Alliance’s main hubs.

npc:magistrate-henry-maleb.text: Magistrate Henry Maleb. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb keeps order in the Alliance's chief coastal stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills. The port town faces threats from the Forsaken and the Syndicate. Magistrate Henry Maleb governs from Southshore's town hall, one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. Forsaken forces threaten the town from the north and west, while highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb took office after the previous magistrate was mysteriously assassinated, an act he blames on the Syndicate. He means to avoid the same fate. His investigations seek hidden assassins, Syndicate supply networks, and the nobles directing them from the ruins of Alterac.

npc:magus-rimtori.text: Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

npc:mai-ah.text: Mai'ah. At the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Mai'ah trains young Darkspear trolls in magic. She guides new spellcasters as they begin their path among the Horde. Young Darkspear trolls come to Mai'ah in the Valley of Trials to learn magic. Orcs favor the elements or the warrior's path, but trolls have a rare gift for arcane study. Candidates bring glyphic inscriptions, and Mai'ah teaches them to shape raw power into controlled incantations. That control matters in Durotar, where danger waits beyond the den.

npc:major-mattingly.text: Major Mattingly. At Stormwind’s main gates, Major Mattingly helps guard the capital and advises crafters on protection from dragons. Major Mattingly is a high-ranking officer responsible for Stormwind City's landward defense. He stands watch in the Valley of Heroes under General Marcus Jonathan, alongside the city's garrison. His duties include overseeing gate patrols and travelers entering the city. Mattingly also knows the lethal nature of dragons and guides skilled crafters who seek to make protective dragonscale gear for facing dangerous lairs.

npc:major-samuelson.text: Major Samuelson. In Stormwind Keep, Major Samuelson commands the city guard and its personnel. The high-ranking veteran officer serves in the throne room and once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Before Stormwind's royal court, Major Samuelson leads the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and military orders across the realm. He mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, who serves at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders struggle or seek transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel across the kingdom to Samuelson's desk in the capital.

npc:mankrik.text: Mankrik. At the Crossroads, Mankrik carries grief and a thirst for vengeance. A quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, and he now hunts the bristled beasts across the Barrens. Mankrik and his wife Olgra traveled through the Barrens when quilboar swarmed them during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. The fighting tore them apart, and Mankrik saw Olgra vanish beneath tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Fury drove him to fight recklessly until a blow left him unconscious. Along the Gold Road, a passing tauren druid found Mankrik bleeding out and bound his injuries. He survived the ambush, but Olgra was gone. At the Crossroads, Mankrik recovers, paralyzed by grief and consumed by bloodlust. Thork and other local leaders warn that hatred has clouded his judgment, and they refuse to send official war parties. Mankrik refuses to move on. Uncertain of Olgra's fate, he calls on any willing Horde travelers to search the Barrens for signs of his lost mate and slaughter any quilboar they meet.

npc:marcus-redpath.text: Marcus Redpath. In Southshore, Marshal Marcus Redpath holds Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts against nearby ogres, murlocs, and naga. Marshal Marcus Redpath guards Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. The town endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion. Redpath now leads its defense, protecting the survivors who remain there. Southshore stands virtually alone against hostile forces pressing in from every side. Marshal Redpath coordinates the defense across the Hillsbrad Foothills and enlists seasoned adventurers to push back the Crushridge ogres advancing from Alterac. He also sends them against dangerous naga and murloc encampments along the coast. The Forsaken occupy the north, and nearby Tarren Mill is heavily fortified. Redpath's vigilance helps keep the Alliance presence in the region from collapsing.

npc:mardant-strongoak.text: Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

npc:marek-ironheart.text: Marek Ironheart. At the Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart tests those who seek the respect of its hunters. The veteran dwarven hunter is stationed in south-eastern Loch Modan and keeps to the traditions of the wild. At the Farstrider Lodge, Marek Ironheart expects hunters to prove their skill. The lodge overlooks the lake from a ridge in south-eastern Loch Modan and gathers marksmen and trackers from across the dwarven lands. Marek pays little heed to titles or boasts. Anyone seeking the lodge’s respect must show practical skill against the beasts roaming Loch Modan, with the patience and nerve of a true hunter.

npc:marisa-du-paige.text: Marisa du'Paige. In the caves outside the Deadmines, Marisa du'Paige fights beside Moonbrook's outlaws. Rare among their laborers and highwaymen, she uses arcane magic in the tunnels of southwestern Westfall. Deep in the caves leading toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs guard the tunnels. Marisa du'Paige is a skilled human mage among them. Many spellcasters train in Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, but Marisa has joined the outlaws and brigands in Westfall's underground passages.

npc:marleth-barleybrew.text: Marleth Barleybrew. At Brewnall Village, Marleth Barleybrew works to prove her family’s ale can rival Thunder Ale. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan’s hold on the local beer trade, she schemes to put Barleybrew brew before drinkers. In Dun Morogh, beer matters as much as steel, and the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families have long been rivals. Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin control nearly all the trade from their distillery in Kharanos, to Marleth Barleybrew’s frustration. She believes her family’s brew is just as strong. Rather than challenge the Thunderbrews openly, Marleth turns to quiet tricks. She recruits travelers to secretly replace Kharanos tavern casks with Barleybrew kegs.

npc:marryk-nurribit.text: Marryk Nurribit. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Marryk Nurribit teaches young gnomes the arcane arts. He favors local brews over strict lessons and often asks his pupils for spare coins to buy a drink. Marryk Nurribit teaches young gnomes magic inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He knows the arcane arts, though he takes a casual approach to teaching. A flagon of dwarven ale often holds more of his attention than a lesson, and he asks his new pupils for spare pocket change. He also warns aspiring spellcasters about the dangers beyond Coldridge Valley, where Gnomeregan's ruins remain radioactive and infested with troggs.

npc:marshal-maxwell.text: Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

npc:martie-jainrose.text: Martie Jainrose. In Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends a garden beside Lake Everstill. She gathers herbs and flowers for the town while wild beasts threaten her plots, and she seems fond of Guard Parker. Martie Jainrose tends herbs and flowers for Lakeshire as its herbalist. Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the Redridge Mountains, but Martie keeps the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Wild animals disrupt her work, especially Bellygrub, a monstrous boar that often ravages her garden beds. Martie also seems fond of Guard Parker. Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

npc:marukai.text: Marukai. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai holds a remote Horde beachhead against the Wrathtail naga. The Darkspear jungle troll coordinates efforts to drive the naga back along Ashenvale's foggy northwest coast. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. The outpost sits on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline. Marukai directs Horde champions to push them back into the tide and collect their heads, keeping the outpost a viable coastal stronghold.

npc:master-apothecary-lydon.text: Apothecary Lydon. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon studies poisons for the Royal Apothecary Society. Bored and sunk in gloom, he takes pleasure in lethal brews and the suffering they cause. His research seeks to secure Hillsbrad for the Forsaken and advance Sylvanas's New Plague. Inside Tarren Mill's chapel, now a laboratory, Apothecary Lydon carries out the cold work of the Royal Apothecary Society. Flowers in bloom and Hillsbrad Foothills' crisp air only deepen his languid melancholy. Deathcraft is the one diversion that lifts his gloom. Left alone, he poisons, dissects, and reanimates his pet frog, Umpi, again and again while he waits for new reagents.

npc:master-vornal.text: Master Vornal. In Sen'jin Village, Master Vornal brews for the Darkspear trolls and keeps his craft to himself. The elderly jungle troll refuses to take on apprentices despite his deep knowledge of alchemy. Master Vornal brews draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls in Sen'jin Village. Age is catching up with him, but he remains fiercely independent and refuses to train an apprentice. He mixes his remedies and volatile brews by his own hand. Master Vornal sometimes sends young adventurers to gather harsh or unusual ingredients from the surrounding lands. The materials go into solvents and other mixtures. He rewards those who help, but guards his methods and recipes, keeping the work of brewing to himself.

npc:mastok-wrilehiss.text: Mastok Wrilehiss. At Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale, Mastok Wrilehiss helps hold the Horde’s ground. He directs scouts and warriors to watch nearby borders and confront corrupting elemental forces amid the night elves’ hostility. Deep beneath Ashenvale’s canopy, Splintertree Post is surrounded by hostile night elf territory. Mastok Wrilehiss helps defend the outpost and watches its supply routes and the forest around it. The Sentinels see the settlement as an intrusion that despoils their lands, and they strike quickly at any sign of weakness. From within the stockade, Mastok gives passing adventurers duties tied to the Horde’s defense. He watches the borders toward the Stonetalon Mountains and sends scouts to speak with shamans such as Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring at Zoram'gar Strand.
