His work also follows the strange corruption afflicting local elementals.

npc:mathredis-firestar.text: Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself. Adventurers who bring Mathredis the proper tomes—such as the Librams of Constitution, Resilience, Rumination, Tenacity, or Voracity—along with rare reagents will find him eager to trade his craft. The process binds volatile magical reagents directly to the text, concentrating their essence into an arcanum that can permanently enchant headwear or leg armor. So long as adventurers supply the components, Mathredis receives both payment and the ambient arcane sustenance he desperately craves.

npc:maur-grimtotem.text: Maur Grimtotem. Deep in Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Maur Grimtotem lies dead. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent him to seek peace with the troggs, and his remains and satchel are still in the caverns. Maur Grimtotem went into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar as an envoy to the troggs. Most of the Horde saw them as savage brutes beyond negotiation, but Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought peace might be possible, or at least said so. Maur carried her offer into the winding caverns. The troggs killed him, and his body remains under the watch of their chieftain, Oggleflint.

npc:maur-raincaller.text: Maur Raincaller. In Bloodhoof Village, Maur Raincaller watches over Mulgore’s herds and wild beasts. He attends to concerns tied to the plains’ natural and spiritual life. Maur Raincaller lives near the heart of Bloodhoof Village, on the shore of Lake Stonebull. He watches over matters involving Mulgore’s wildlife and the balance of the elements. After the strider Mazzranache bites him and infects his wound, Maur asks young travelers to gather animal parts for a remedy.

npc:maurin-bonesplitter.text: Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it. Maurin directs most of his malice toward the Burning Blade cult entrenched across Desolace. He harbors utter disgust for their reckless ambition, mocking the cultists for failing to understand that their borrowed power merely binds them as thralls to their demonic masters. Through scrying spells and ritual knowledge, Maurin enlists Horde adventurers to systematically disrupt the cult's summonings and undermine their operations across the barren landscape.

npc:maxan-anvol.text: Maxan Anvol. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Maxan Anvol trains dwarven priests in the Holy Light. He tests young acolytes before they earn the Church’s vestments. Maxan Anvol tends to the hamlet’s spiritual welfare from the Thunderbrew Distillery, where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes gather. Kharanos lies between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and its inn draws those who pass through. Maxan offers prayers and counsel to anyone who enters, with pints of stout close at hand. Maxan Anvol tests novice priests before they venture into the wider world. He has initiates use basic healing prayers on Dun Morogh’s wounded defenders. Those who show devotion and skill receive their first priestly vestments, marking their recognized place in the Church of the Holy Light.

npc:maybell-maclure.text: Maybell Maclure. At the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest, Maybell Maclure loves a Stonefield in secret. Her family’s bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields keeps her apart from Tommy Joe Stonefield. Maybell Maclure works the family vineyards under the shadow of a long feud with the Stonefields next door. She has fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, heir to the rival farm. Their relatives keep them apart, and Maybell searches for a way to speak with him beyond her family’s watchful eyes.

npc:melithar-staghelm.text: Melithar Staghelm. Outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm guides young night elves. He sends them to learn why the dryad Tarindrella has returned to the glade. His Staghelm name links him to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, though their connection is unknown. Melithar Staghelm waits outside Aldrassil, where night elves first step into the world. A druid who listens to the forest spirits, he has learned that Tarindrella, a woodland protector, has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing trouble, Melithar sends newcomers southwest of Aldrassil to find the dryad and learn why she has come back to the grove. The Staghelm name draws notice because Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus, after Malfurion Stormrage disappeared into the Emerald Dream. Melithar makes no claim to a grand heritage and says nothing of his lineage. Whether he belongs to the Archdruid's family or shares an ancient Kaldorei name remains unknown. For now, Melithar tends to his humble duties at the roots of Aldrassil.

npc:merissa-stilwell.text: Merissa Stilwell. At Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell welcomes newcomers to Northshire Valley. The young human townsperson offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to those training nearby. Merissa Stilwell greets fresh recruits arriving in Northshire Valley from her place at Northshire Abbey. She offers newcomers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting and finding their way. Her surname is shared by craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom, including the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell. Merissa remains a peaceful local presence amid the kingdom's rising tensions.

npc:merrin-rockweaver.text: Merrin Rockweaver. On a ridge above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Merrin Rockweaver waits with the survivors. A raptor infestation drove them from the dig, where she represented the Explorers' League. Merrin Rockweaver came to the Wetlands for the Ironforge Explorers' League, seeking ancient Titan secrets beneath the muck. The expedition fell apart when the large bones the crew unearthed drew raptors to the dig. The beasts swarmed the trenches, and Merrin and the surviving crew fled, leaving their equipment, notes, and progress behind. Now Merrin is trapped with a few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins. The survivors on the bluff still hope to save what they can of the expedition. Ormer Ironbraid plans vengeance against the beasts, while Prospector Whelgar seeks tablet fragments in the raptor-infested trenches. Merrin worries about her husband Tarrel, who has heard nothing from her in weeks. A scout Longbraid sent to find the team can carry word of their plight back to him.

npc:miles-welsh.text: Miles Welsh. In the Pools of Vision, Miles Welsh teaches priests beneath Thunder Bluff. The Forsaken trainer offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline in the tauren capital. Miles Welsh teaches priests in the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. Far from Lordaeron's plague-scarred ruins, the Forsaken priest makes his home in the grotto beneath the city. He instructs travelers in divine and shadowy energies. His place in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous ties between the Forsaken and the Horde. There, he shares sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in shadow and faith.

npc:milli-featherwhistle.text: Milli Featherwhistle. At Steelgrill's Depot, Milli Featherwhistle keeps Gnomeregan's mechanostriders in motion. She builds and maintains these clockwork mounts for her kin and trusted allies among the exiles. Outdoors in the biting chill at Steelgrill's Depot, just east of Kharanos, Milli keeps clockwork steeds ready for Gnomeregan's displaced people. Dwarves and night elves favor living mounts, but Milli builds each mechanostrider herself. She calibrates its gears, pistons, and balancing gyros so it can travel across Dun Morogh's snowy crags. Milli builds her mechanostriders from blueprints first drawn by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque. She has improved their performance by lightening the chassis and refining the exhaust vents, while keeping to the High Tinker's original designs. Her work carries gnomish ambition forward even in exile.

npc:milton-sheaf.text: Milton Sheaf. In Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf guards the kingdom's written history. He tends the Royal Library and calls on Alliance travelers to recover lost books and records. Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. While the court handles politics, noble disputes, and military concerns, he preserves the written record. He sees accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms as a duty, especially amid war, loss, and instability. Milton Sheaf sends travelers to recover books scattered across the realm. Volumes wear with use, while records lie in monastic archives, distant outposts, and forgotten ruins. He sends Alliance adventurers from Northshire Abbey to Southshore in the north to retrieve misplaced books, examine ancient texts, and return rare manuscripts safely to the keep.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-earth.text: Minor Manifestation of Earth. At sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar, Minor Manifestation of Earth waits unseen. Fledgling shamans who drink Earth Sapta can meet the spirit and receive rough quartz for carving their first earth totem. Earth spirits dwell beneath dirt and stone, but reaching them takes a deliberate rite. At Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger beyond ordinary sight, surrounded by lesser elemental presences. Only initiates who drink Earth Sapta, a draught brewed by shamanic mentors, can cross the veil between the physical world and the elements. When an initiate makes contact, the spirit grants the earth's blessings and a piece of rough quartz. The novice can use it as the spiritual focus for making an Earth Totem.

npc:minor-manifestation-of-water.text: Minor Manifestation of Water. Along North Tide's Run, the Minor Manifestation of Water awaits shamans on Silverpine Forest's coast. Its corrupted counterpart must be cleansed before the peaceful spirit can be consulted. The Minor Manifestation of Water waits west of the Sepulcher, along North Tide's Run. For developing shamans, meeting the spirit is an essential rite. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, yet malevolent blight can corrupt them. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation before the pure spirit reveals itself. Once cleansed, the Minor Manifestation of Water guides shamans on their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

npc:misha.text: Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles. Misha is far more than a tame pet; she is a seasoned warrior. She fought alongside Rexxar in the brutal conflict against Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, helping ensure the young Horde's survival. When not in battle, her keen senses and strength serve as an extension of Rexxar's will. Currently, travelers venturing along the long tracks through the Stonetalon Mountains, Desolace, and Feralas can spot Misha padding quietly beside Rexxar. Though fierce enough to tear apart any predator foolish enough to threaten them, she remains Rexxar's steadfast anchor in an otherwise untrustworthy world.

npc:misha-tor-kren.text: Misha Tor'kren. At the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, Misha Tor'kren waits for word of her son. Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks, but has not returned. Misha Tor'kren tends her farm near Thunder Ridge, southeast of the ridge. Her son Kron went west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never came home. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching the orcish watchtowers thin, Misha has no word of where he is. She needs travelers willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her son.

npc:mitsuwa.text: Mitsuwa. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Mitsuwa mourns the trolls slain on their journey through Ashenvale. He calls on Horde champions to recover their stolen charms. Mitsuwa serves the Horde at Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand, alongside Marukai. Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale ambushed and slaughtered a group of traveling trolls bound for the outpost. Mitsuwa sees their deaths as a grievous offense. He sends warriors to the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms and honor the spirits of his kin.

npc:monte-gazlowe.text: Monte Gazlowe. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe keeps a neutral port open to traders from every side. He founded the town with the fortune he earned as the Horde’s chief engineer during the building of Durotar and Orgrimmar. At Ratchet, Monte Gazlowe runs a port where rivals can trade under the Steamwheedle Cartel. He founded the town on the barren coast after earning a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde. Horde, Alliance, and independent traders may barter there, so long as they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy. After the Third War, Warchief Thrall hired Monte Gazlowe as Durotar’s chief engineer to solve urgent problems for the new orc capital. Gazlowe took on the dangerous work of securing freshwater for Orgrimmar. His tunnels broke into underground kobold dens, but the wandering beastmaster Rexxar arrived in time to help blast the caverns shut. Gazlowe finished his assignments and remains a favored contractor and friend to Thrall. He has even sent his foreman, Rezlak, to keep helping with orc construction across Durotar. Trade brings good earnings to Ratchet, but maritime rivals and thieves trouble Monte Gazlowe’s business. The Southsea Freebooters have camps along the nearby Merchant Coast, where they seize cargo bound for Ratchet and steal goods from raw ore to Gazlowe’s custom-ordered boots. To protect his profits, the port boss often hires passing sellswords of any allegiance to clear pirate camps, recover stolen shipments, and settle scores with troublemakers at the docks.

npc:moon-priestess-amara.text: Moon Priestess Amara. West of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara watches Teldrassil’s road to Darnassus. Two huntresses guard her as she keeps watch over the woodland paths. Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west of Dolanaar with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. As a priestess of the Sisterhood of Elune, she brings spiritual guidance to her post, while her watch helps keep Teldrassil’s roads secure. Travelers heading west can seek her direction toward Darnassus. Those burdened in spirit can also seek a path of redemption from her.

npc:mor-rogal.text: Mor'rogal. In Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal guides travelers toward the dangers and promise of the Stonetalon Mountains. Mor'rogal watches the deep crevices and caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains from Sun Rock Retreat. Their twisting passages offer riches, but can also bring deadly danger. He sends brave Horde wanderers to troubled places such as Boulderslide Ravine. To Mor'rogal, facing those depths tests the spirit of anyone who seeks glory by following heart and soul.

npc:morgan-pestle.text: Morgan Pestle. In Stormwind, Morgan Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. He works with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, handling supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Morgan Pestle sells alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. His brother William keeps a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, while Morgan tends their family trade in the capital. He receives supplies from the rural heartlands, including candles sent by William.

npc:morgan-the-collector.text: Morgan the Collector. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Morgan the Collector directs Defias extortion and gathering across Elwynn Forest. A high-ranking operative, he coordinates local theft from the farmhouse while Goldshire's guard keeps watch nearby. Morgan the Collector skims gold from Elwynn Forest's mines for the Defias Brotherhood. While common bandits harass travelers on the roads, he directs organized shakedowns and gathers stolen coin and supplies for the Brotherhood's wider network. His headquarters is the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor surround him.

npc:mountaineer-barleybrew.text: Mountaineer Barleybrew. At South Gate Outpost, Mountaineer Barleybrew watches the pass from Dun Morogh toward Loch Modan. He relies on dwarven brews to help sentries endure the cold. Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew watches the snowy road to Loch Modan from South Gate Outpost. He is part of Ironforge's border watch. Like other mountaineers in Dun Morogh's bitter winds, he values the strength of fine dwarven drink. His name links him to the renowned Barleybrew clan. He also helps send potent Shimmer Stout to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts in the mountain passes.

npc:mountaineer-kadrell.text: Mountaineer Kadrell. Across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps watch over Loch Modan. Mountaineer Kadrell keeps watch in Thelsamar and organizes the dwarven defenses of Loch Modan. Outposts along the valley’s fringes face pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts. From the center of town, Kadrell organizes reinforcements, relays orders, and weighs reports from scouts in the field. Mountaineer Kadrell keeps in touch with Thelsamar’s remote forward posts. He coordinates with Mountaineer Stormpike and sends adventurers to report to sentries such as Mountaineer Rockgar. The outposts guard the mountain passes, and Kadrell helps get them supplies, reinforcements, and word of threats.

npc:mountaineer-stormpike.text: Mountaineer Stormpike. At Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike watches the road into the Wetlands. A proud member of the Stormpike clan, he guards Ironforge’s supply routes from troggs and kobolds. At Algaz Station, Mountaineer Stormpike guards the northern road out of Loch Modan. The station stands before the descent through Dun Algaz into the Wetlands, where rocky crags and threats from the wilderness surround it. Stormpike keeps communication open and the road clear for travelers and supply convoys crossing the pass. Kobolds in nearby digs and troggs from beneath the ground trouble northern Loch Modan. Stormpike asks passing adventurers to disrupt these threats. Kobolds have moved into Silver Stream Mine and taken the Miners' League's stored dwarven tools.

npc:mountaineer-thalos.text: Mountaineer Thalos. At Coldridge Pass, Mountaineer Thalos warns travelers of troggs in the tunnel. He guards the route from Coldridge Valley toward Kharanos and guides couriers carrying urgent reports. At the mouth of Coldridge Pass, Mountaineer Thalos guards the route out of Coldridge Valley. Troggs have burrowed up from below and overrun the tunnel, making the crossing dangerous. Thalos warns travelers who are not ready to turn back and judges whether couriers can brave the passage toward the wider kingdom. After Grelin Whitebeard reports Frostmane troll movements in the secluded valley, a courier carries the report to Grelin's brother Senir in Kharanos. Before entering the tunnel, the courier is told to speak with Mountaineer Thalos. He sends capable travelers onward through the pass to Kharanos, where regional commanders coordinate Dun Morogh's defense. The route carries vital intelligence toward Ironforge's military leaders.

npc:mupsi-shacklefridd.text: Mupsi Shacklefridd. Outside Ratchet in the Barrens, Mupsi Shacklefridd helps travelers repair ties with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Mupsi Shacklefridd works along the coastal road just outside Ratchet. Steamwheedle guards patrol the port town's edge as merchants come and go. Travelers on poor terms with the goblins can seek a way back into the cartel's good graces through Mupsi, if they bring the supplies and labor it demands.

npc:mux-manascrambler.text: Mux Manascrambler. Mux Manascrambler is an eccentric goblin engineer dwelling in the desert outpost of Gadgetzan. Unlike many of his peers focused strictly on explosives or mining equipment, Mux harbors a peculiar fascination with the supernatural and occult energies. Tucked away inside a building in central Gadgetzan, behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots, sits Mux Manascrambler. While the Steamwheedle Cartel trades heavily in oil, guns, and salvage, Mux focuses his ingenuity on more esoteric pursuits: the realm of spirits and supernatural anomalies. He uses his technical acumen to design bizarre devices capable of detecting, distilling, and interacting with spectral remnants, bridging crude goblin craftsmanship with the invisible worlds of the dead.

npc:mydrannul.text: Mydrannul. At the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mydrannul keeps basic supplies ready for sentinels, soldiers, and visitors. Mydrannul keeps a supply stall among the Warrior's Terrace military pavilions and training grounds. Darnassus's defenders and travelers can find everyday field gear there, including ammunition for archers and gunners, throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. His stall helps sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil find the basic sundries they need.

npc:nalpak.text: Nalpak. Nalpak is a tauren druid disciple who watches over the troubled Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. Stationed in the high cliff-cave overlooking the cavern entrance, he enlists passing adventurers to help contain the nightmare twisting the subterranean ecosystem. Perched inside a hidden cavern directly above the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak remains loyal to the vision of Naralex. While his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber deep below, Nalpak works to keep the spreading corruption at bay. He asks adventurers to gather deviate hides for use as leather.

npc:nara-meideros.text: Nara Meideros. In Stormwind's Park, Nara Meideros guides young seekers in Elune's teachings. As a night elf priestess in the human capital, she offers a familiar spiritual presence to her kin. Nara Meideros serves Elune far from Kalimdor, across the Great Sea in Stormwind City. In the Park, night elf druids and priests have tended a green refuge. Nara guides young seekers in devotion to the Moon Goddess. Human priests serve the Holy Light in nearby Cathedral Square, while Nara gives night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms a connection to their own faith.

npc:narain-soothfancy.text: Narain Soothfancy. Narain Soothfancy is an eccentric gnome dwelling in a secluded beach hut just north of Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. While he loudly advertises himself as a master soothsayer capable of divining the future, those who know him consider his psychic talents a complete farce compared to his genuine engineering genius. Perched on the eastern coast of Tanaris just north of the goblin docks, Narain Soothfancy lives as a retired engineer turned self-proclaimed master fortune teller. He routinely greets visitors by pressing unopened envelopes against his forehead or making wildly inaccurate guesses about their business, such as wondering if they have arrived seeking the legendary Ashbringer. Despite his theatrical charade, Narain possesses deep technical knowledge. Even ancient beings like the blue dragon Azuregos note that while Narain is a terrible psychic, his engineering aptitude is undeniably brilliant. A handbook titled 'Soothsaying for Dummies' rests nearby. Before settling by Steamwheedle Port, Narain suffered a catastrophic flying machine crash far to the south along Land's End Beach. He survived the wreck thanks to an unexpected rescue, though his eccentric personality and strange obsessions have kept him isolated on the desert shores, tinkering with arcane-adjacent technology and peddling dubious prophecies to anyone who passes by.

npc:nat-pagle.text: Nat Pagle. Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience. Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals. Pagle makes his camp on a small spit of land along the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, far from the bustling taverns of the Eastern Kingdoms. He remains fiercely independent and uninterested in the politics of factions, welcoming Alliance travelers sent by trainers like Grimnur Stonebrand as well as Horde aspirants directed to him by Lumak in Orgrimmar. For Nat, anyone willing to scour the corners of the world for rare specimens deserves a lesson in genuine angling. Pagle has ventured into perilous waters, including an excursion into the ruins of Zul'Gurub where he misplaced his favorite measuring tape and tackle box near the waters prowled by the monstrous hydra Gahz'ranka.

npc:natalia-mar-alith.text: Natalia Mar'alith. Mistress Natalia Mar'alith is a night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher lost deep within the silithid nests of Hive'Regal. Once part of the expedition investigating Silithus alongside her husband, Commander Mar'alith, she has succumbed completely to the maddening influence of the Old Gods. When the Cenarion Circle established their outpost at Cenarion Hold to monitor the awakening sands, Natalia accompanied her husband, Commander Mar'alith, into the wastes. Eager to unravel the mystery behind the resurgence of the silithid and the ancient Qiraji ruins, she joined an exploratory party led by the famed explorer Brann Bronzebeard, accompanied by the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

npc:nathanos-blightcaller.text: Nathanos Blightcaller. Nathanos Blightcaller, once Nathanos Marris, stands at his ruined homestead in the Eastern Plaguelands as the deadly champion of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. In life he was the first and only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, and in undeath he trains Forsaken hunters while guarding the eastern frontier with biting contempt for all who approach. Before the Third War, Nathanos Marris was an extraordinary marksman and tactical genius hailing from the rural outskirts of Lordaeron. Trained by the high elves of Quel'Thalas and close to Sylvanas Windrunner, he became the only human to ever attain the prestigious rank of Ranger Lord. His home remained the family estate in Lordaeron, the Marris Stead. When Prince Arthas and the Scourge swept through Lordaeron following the purge of Stratholme, the plague consumed the kingdom. Nathanos made a desperate stand at his estate, but fell to the monstrous abomination Ramstein the Gorger. Raised as a mindless undead thrall, he roamed the blighted fields killing in the Lich King's name. After Sylvanas shattered the Scourge's mental grip and established the Forsaken in the Undercity, she came for him, as he had somehow known she would, and tore his consciousness free from the Lich King's will, returning his tactical brilliance and fiery loyalty to her side.

npc:nida.text: Hilary. At the Lakeshire docks, Hilary cries over the necklace she lost in Lake Everstill. Hilary waits in tears by the Lakeshire pier, afraid her father will be angry. She dropped the necklace he gave her into Lake Everstill, and hopes someone brave will dive in to find it. Gnoll invasions and Blackrock orc warbands press upon Lakeshire, but children there still face troubles of their own.

npc:nikova-raskol.text: Nikova Raskol. In Old Town, Nikova Raskol grieves for her murdered grandson. The elderly Stormwind townswoman seeks justice against the Defias Brotherhood rioters held in the Stockade. Nikova Raskol wanders Old Town, carrying the grief of a recent loss. Her beloved grandson, Mac, was slain by Defias Brotherhood brigands. While the kingdom faces treason on a grand scale, Nikova bears the private cost of the Brotherhood's lawless rampage. Many criminals who wrecked havoc were captured and locked in the Stockade, but a violent inmate rebellion has seized the prison. The guards have failed to restore order, and Nikova turns to adventurers heading inside. She asks them to bring back red Defias bandanas as proof that her grandson's killers have faced retribution.

npc:nissa-firestone.text: Nissa Firestone. Above Ironforge’s Great Forge, Nissa Firestone teaches field medicine to travelers and soldiers. Nissa Firestone tends patients on the upper floor of the Ironforge Physician shop. The Great Forge’s clang and heat rise around her, but the work is keeping wounds bound. Dwarven warriors can endure much, yet blades and claws still break their skin. Before travelers and soldiers head into the snows of Dun Morogh or farther afield, Nissa teaches them basic bandaging and field dressings to help keep themselves and their allies alive. Nissa Firestone teaches field medics the basics of cloth and lint. When a practitioner has learned all she can teach, she points them toward specialized triage officers in far-flung outposts. Skilled healers go where the Alliance’s casualties are heaviest.

npc:nogg.text: Nogg. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Nogg puts his craft to work for the Horde. The goblin engineer studies strange mechanical salvage from deep within Gnomeregan. Nogg runs an independent engineering workshop in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Adventurers and craftsmen come to him for the mechanical skill only a goblin can offer in a city known for orcish steel and strength. He is eager to examine unusual devices and trinkets brought back from Alliance lands or underground ruins. Salvage from Gnomeregan draws Nogg's special attention. When Horde operatives recover intricate rings and other remnants from the fallen gnomish capital, few minds in Durotar can take apart, decipher, and adapt those strange clockwork devices for Horde use.

npc:nori-pridedrift.text: Nori Pridedrift. In Coldridge Valley, Nori Pridedrift carries steaming Mornbrew to those facing the cold. He makes his living brewing and selling the hot drink, and hires swift couriers to deliver it while it is still warm. Nori Pridedrift sends hot Mornbrew across the frozen reaches of Coldridge Valley. The valley's cold bites hard, and a draught of Scalding Mornbrew offers welcome warmth. Nori brews the coffee-like drink and sends it to mountaineers and freezing sentries. It must reach them while still scalding, so his couriers race against the mountain air. Nori also has only a limited supply of sturdy mugs, and expects runners to bring them back promptly.

npc:novice-elreth.text: Novice Elreth. Inside Deathknell's chapel, Novice Elreth guides the newly risen Forsaken. She sends them against the mindless Scourge near the graves and helps them face the plague's sorrowful aftermath. Novice Elreth guides newly risen undead inside the desecrated chapel at Deathknell. They struggle to understand their horrific awakening, while the Forsaken must organize quickly to secure their territory. Elreth sends them south to gather paws from wolves and wings from bats. She also points them toward Lordaeron's tragic aftermath, including the sorrow of her friend Marla Fipps, whom her husband Samuel killed after joining the mindless Scourge.

npc:oben-rageclaw.text: Oben Rageclaw. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Oben Rageclaw's spirit wanders, unable to wake or pass on. His sleeping body remains under the Gnarlpine furbolgs' control. Oben Rageclaw entered Ban'ethil Barrow Den to commune with nature and wander the Emerald Dream, as many Druids of the Claw do. When the Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to corruption and overran the barrows, Oben lay defenseless in his trance. A corrupted Gnarlpine shaman used dark rituals to take control of his comatose body. His spirit was left behind as an anguished ghost, unable to wake or pass on.

npc:ogtinc.text: Ogtinc. Ogtinc is an independent furbolg hunter perched on a high ridge overlooking the Ruins of Eldarath in Azshara. Having parted ways with his tribe to serve the balance of nature, he acts as a trusted ally and mentor for the Cenarion Circle. Skilled hunters seeking to test their craft against the fiercest beasts of Kalimdor often seek out his guidance. While most furbolg in Kalimdor remain fiercely bound to their tribes—or have succumbed to corruption following the Third War—Ogtinc chose a distinct path. Departing from his kin, he dedicated his bow and survival lore to aiding the Cenarion Circle. He makes his camp high on a bluff southeast of Timbermaw Hold, vigilantly watching over the ancient, shattered lands of Azshara. Ogtinc is renowned among seasoned trackers for his intimate understanding of Kalimdor's wilderness. He tests hunters who have honed their skills across the continents, dispatching them to gather rare trophies—such as the antlers of courser beasts, the scale of wave-thrashed sea serpents, and parts from green dragonkin. Through these trials, he teaches that true hunting honors the natural world and preserves balance rather than mindlessly taking life.

npc:ogunaro-wolfrunner.text: Ogunaro Wolfrunner. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Honor, Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends the Horde’s foremost wolf kennel beside the Hunter’s Hall. He breeds and trains fierce wolves for orc champions and their trusted allies. Ogunaro Wolfrunner tends Orgrimmar’s battle wolves beside the Hunter’s Hall in the Valley of Honor. Orcs and wolves have shared a bond for generations, across Draenor’s plains and Durotar’s wilderness. It rests on mutual respect, not simple domestication. Ogunaro entrusts only the hardiest beasts, from dire wolves to agile timber prowlers, to warriors who have proven their strength and worth to the warchief.

npc:old-murk-eye.text: Old Murk-Eye. Near the Westfall Lighthouse, Old Murk-Eye prowls the southern coast. His kind revere him, and sailors fear the lethal menace he poses to anyone who wanders near the lighthouse. Old Murk-Eye prowls the surf around the Westfall Lighthouse, where he is far tougher and more aggressive than the murlocs common along Westfall’s shores. His attacks have brought enough grief to local mariners that the spectral Captain Grayson seeks his death. Grayson offers a bounty for Old Murk-Eye’s pristine scales, hoping to break his hold on the shallows.

npc:orendil-broadleaf.text: Orendil Broadleaf. At Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale, night elf Orendil Broadleaf tends to the sick. His knowledge of forest plants helps him make remedies for young lives in the troubled woodlands. At Maestra's Post on Ashenvale's western border, Orendil Broadleaf cares for the sick. The skilled healer knows the local herbs and how to use them in restorative remedies. He depends on travelers passing through to gather rare plants and other natural ingredients. Tension and conflict press closer to the forest, but Orendil remains focused on protecting his kin and easing their ailments.

npc:orenthil-whisperwind.text: Orenthil Whisperwind. Beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves of Shadowglen. Orenthil Whisperwind lives among the night elves beneath Teldrassil’s canopy in Shadowglen. Little is known of his personal history.

npc:ormak-grimshot.text: Ormak Grimshot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Ormak Grimshot trains hunters for life in the wild. Beside his wolf, Grimfang, he teaches Horde hunters to track, shoot, and tame beasts. Ormak Grimshot trains Horde trackers and marksmen in the Hunter's Hall. With his wolf, Grimfang, at his side, he teaches the skills needed to survive Kalimdor's wilderness. Orc and troll hunters who have completed their trials in Durotar learn from him how to tame and command wild beasts, and to form a lasting bond with an animal companion.

npc:ormer-ironbraid.text: Ormer Ironbraid. At Whelgar's Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid faces a raptor threat that has driven the dwarven workers away. He remains at the dig, seeking allies to reclaim it. Ormer Ironbraid came to the Wetlands with the dwarven effort to uncover Titan relics and ancient history at Whelgar's Excavation Site. The work stirred packs of fierce Wetlands raptors, or at least drew them to the dig. Now beasts prowl among the ruins where Ormer's team hoped to study ancient earthenware and tablets. The raptors have disrupted their work, and Ormer's anger toward them runs deep. Ormer will not abandon the dig, though he cannot drive the raptors out alone. He asks passing travelers to kill the beasts, beginning with smaller ones and taking on larger, fiercer raptors in turn. Reclaiming the excavation means recovering the artifacts, but the fight has become personal: Ormer wants vengeance for the work the raptors disrupted and the dwarven pride wounded by their presence.

npc:orokk-omosh.text: Orokk Omosh. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh keeps his family's smithing craft alive. The aging orc has no children to inherit it, so he seeks worthy Horde apprentices to learn the Omosh armorcraft secrets. In the Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh is the last smith of the Omosh line. He has no children to inherit his craft, and he will not let his family's techniques die with him. Capable Horde blacksmiths can undertake his demanding trials of metalwork. Those who prove their dedication earn the revered secrets of Omosh armorcraft. Among fellow artisans, Orokk is known for his boisterous delight in true mastery. Those who complete his craftsmanship trials often see him perform the Omosh Dance of Joy, a jubilant celebration of traditional smithing that echoes through Orgrimmar's halls.

npc:orphan-matron-battlewail.text: Orphan Matron Battlewail. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children left without families by war. With Tosamina, she gives them shelter and raises young orcs. Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for children who have lost their kin to violence. In Orgrimmar, where war's toll reaches even the young capital, she and Tosamina shelter and nurture the next generation of the Horde. The orphanage in the Valley of Honor opens its doors to passing adventurers. During Children's Week, travelers are called upon to mentor the children.

npc:orphan-matron-nightingale.text: Orphan Matron Nightingale. In Cathedral Square, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s orphaned children. She and Matron Shellene give them shelter and guidance, and invite Alliance adventurers to spend Children's Week with them. Outside the orphanage, south-east of the Cathedral of Light, Orphan Matron Nightingale cares for Stormwind’s most vulnerable children. Recent wars, gnoll attacks, and the rise of the Defias Brotherhood have left many without homes or parents. Nightingale and Matron Shellene give them shelter, basic care, and guidance under the Church of the Holy Light’s watch. Matron Nightingale believes children need hope as well as food and shelter. Each Children's Week, she asks Alliance heroes to take an orphan on journeys across Azeroth. She hopes meeting celebrated champions will build their confidence, show them the wider world beyond the city walls, and remind them they are not forgotten.

npc:osric-strang.text: Osric Strang. In Stormwind's Old Town, veteran armor merchant Osric Strang supplies weary travelers and Alliance defenders with sturdy gear. His shop, Limited Immunity, specializes in heavy mail and plate armor, along with shields. Osric Strang runs Limited Immunity, where fighters find heavy armor and shields. He also helps arriving couriers who need a point of contact in the capital, including those coming from nearby settlements such as Sentinel Hill in Westfall.

npc:overlord-mok-morokk.text: Overlord Mok'Morokk. Overlord Mok'Morokk is the brute chieftain of the Stonemaul ogres, presiding over Brackenwall Village in Dustwallow Marsh. Originally appointed by Rexxar for his strength, he has become a tyrannical and cowardly ruler who refuses to defend his clan against the black dragonflight. When Rexxar bested the previous chieftain Kor'gall and led the Stonemaul clan in defense of Durotar, he left Mok'Morokk in command, seeing promise in his sheer martial strength. That faith proved misplaced. Mok'Morokk quickly succumbed to the corrupting influence of absolute authority, ruling through intimidation and self-indulgence rather than stewardship. Instead of caring for his kin, he demands unearned tribute, lounges in Brackenwall Village, and bullies anyone who questions his command.

npc:pao-ka-swiftmountain.text: Pao'ka Swiftmountain. Pao'ka Swiftmountain is a young tauren naturalist stranded among the wild wyverns of Highperch in Thousand Needles. Having traveled south under the guidance of Motega Firemane, his youthful curiosity got the better of him when he ventured too close to a nesting site and ended up cornered in the cliffs. Pao'ka came to the canyon country of Thousand Needles alongside Motega Firemane, eager to catalog and study the dangerous beasts of the canyons. His father had been reluctant to let his son go on such a perilous journey, and Pao'ka's recent misadventure proves those concerns were warranted. Fascinated by the magnificent wyverns inhabiting Highperch, the young scholar crept up the mountain trail behind a solitary tauren totem. Unsurprisingly, the territorial beasts took offense to his intrusion, driving him deep into the crags where he found himself trapped and terrified, unable to slip past the swooping predators to return to Whitereach Post.

npc:parqual-fintallas.text: Parqual Fintallas. Parqual Fintallas is a Forsaken scholar and former human historian of Lordaeron, currently residing in the Undercity's Apothecarium. Despite the grim surroundings of his undead existence, he retains a polite demeanor and an enduring passion for ancient lore, often assisting travelers sent to consult his deep historical expertise. In life, Parqual was a respected human scholar of Lordaeron who knew all there was to know of the kingdom, immersing himself in historical texts. When the plague of undeath struck, Parqual was among the many citizens slain and raised, only to eventually break free under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. While the Forsaken largely embrace cold pragmatism and turn away from their former lives, Parqual retains his scholarly passion and pleasant manners, still seeking enlightenment, though of a different nature than in life. Parqual dwells among the bubbling vats and alchemists of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Despite his macabre surroundings, he remains an invaluable font of knowledge regarding Azeroth's history. When adventurers undertake rigorous intellectual trials—such as the elusive 'Test of Lore'—they are directed to Parqual, who sends them to the Scarlet Monastery's library for a book and then puts a question of his own to them.

npc:pilot-bellowfiz.text: Pilot Bellowfiz. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz keeps a dwarven siege engine ready for battle. Known as “Fizzer,” he belongs to the Ironforge Siege Brigade and tends Jetsteam. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz keeps Jetsteam ready for battle. The depot lies just outside Ironforge, where he tends the heavy war machine he pilots. He tunes its parts and gathers what it needs for the field. Fellow driver Pilot Stonegear joins him in talk of vehicle designs, armor plating, and engine output. Their work keeps the mountain kingdom's mechanized strength ready across Khaz Modan.

npc:pilot-hammerfoot.text: Pilot Hammerfoot. Near the mountain passes, Pilot Hammerfoot watches over the Siege Brigade’s engines and worries for a missing fellow pilot. He seeks travelers to search the hills, where the high ridges put dwarves in danger. At North Gate Outpost, Pilot Hammerfoot watches the passes between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan and guards the Siege Brigade’s engines. Ironforge’s siege engines are prized by the brigade, but rough mountain ground makes them dangerous to drive. When a pilot goes missing, finding him matters, especially with savage beasts roaming the nearby hills.

npc:pilot-longbeard.text: Pilot Longbeard. Pilot Longbeard is a dwarven siege engine pilot of the Ironforge Siege Brigade, stationed in the Hall of Arms within Ironforge's Military Ward. Though posted in the mountain city, he maintains close ties with gnomish tinkerers and fellow racing enthusiasts operating far away in the Shimmering Flats. Found amongst the martial displays and weaponsmiths of Ironforge's Military Ward, Pilot Longbeard represents the proud siege engine corps of Khaz Modan. While his duties keep him within the fortress city, Longbeard keeps an eager ear out for innovations and news from fellow mechanics across the continent, including the Brassbolts brothers tinkering out on the salt flats of Kalimdor. Longbeard serves as a point of contact for adventurous travelers heading south into Kalimdor. He frequently directs promising recruits and couriers toward the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles, where gnomish inventors push mechanical boundaries alongside their goblin rivals.

npc:pilot-stonegear.text: Pilot Stonegear. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear keeps the Trollplow ready for battle. Known as “Stone,” the dwarf mechanic and driver serves in the Ironforge Siege Brigade, working to improve the engine's performance and armor. Travelers in Dun Morogh help him find rare materials for the war machine. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear drives for Ironforge's Siege Brigade. His pride is Trollplow, a heavy siege tank built to break enemy lines. He knows a driver's life in battle depends on sound gears, strong plates, and steady steam pressure. So he keeps refining the tank's fighting power and making its cramped cockpit more livable. Pilot Stonegear spends his time off duty debating engineering plans with fellow pilots such as Pilot Bellowfiz. He is never content with the depot's standard designs. To improve Trollplow's armor and munitions, he seeks unusual ores and volatile minerals. Travelers venture through Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness and dangerous caves to find the supplies he needs.

npc:pixel.text: Pixel. At Splintertree Post, Pixel carries Warsong goods through dangerous lands for a fee. She keeps the saw blades until she is paid, and looks for other cargo worth carrying. Pixel carries freight for the Warsong Clan from Splintertree Post, where the Horde holds a fortified post in Ashenvale. She takes goods through active war zones to support the clan’s logging work, but coin and contracts guide her choices. The saw blades stay with her until she receives payment. For this shipment, she wants a deadly blunderbuss to guard herself on the road. Pixel also pays travelers for satyr horns, which are in high demand in Ratchet.

npc:piznik.text: Piznik. Deep in Windshear Mine, Piznik watches the Venture Company at work. Once second-in-command, he was pushed aside by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle and now plots against his former boss. Before Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took control of Windshear Crag, Piznik ranked second across the entire operation. When Gerenzo seized authority, the Venture Company pushed Piznik aside and sent him into the depths of Windshear Mine. Piznik has not accepted the demotion quietly. Underground, he watches the mine's movements and waits for a chance to take revenge on the boss who demoted him.

npc:pozzik.text: Pozzik. Pozzik is an esteemed goblin tinkerer and racer stationed at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Once one of the most respected engineers in Undermine, he now dedicates his technical genius to constructing experimental rocket cars and settling the ultimate debate of engineering supremacy against his gnome counterpart. Before retiring to the harsh salt flats of Thousand Needles, Pozzik built a legendary reputation among the goblins. As one of the most respected tinkerers out of Undermine, his technical expertise spans complex internal combustion, propulsion, and hazardous chassis construction. Rather than settling into comfortable obscurity, however, Pozzik took his mechanical mastery into the desert to push high-speed machinery far past its breaking point. At the Mirage Raceway, Pozzik teamed up with his perennial gnome counterpart, Fizzle Brassbolts. Despite the historic rivalry between goblin explosives and delicate gnomish calibration, the two worked together to construct the sprawling racetrack across the dried lakebed. They field opposing racing outfits, testing prototype rocket cars to definitively prove whose racial design philosophy dominates the track. Naturally, Pozzik is always on the lookout for resourceful adventurers willing to acquire parts and shave weight off his designs.

npc:priestess-a-moora.text: Priestess A'moora. Priestess A'moora is a devout night elf servant of the Moon Goddess residing within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Working closely under the guidance of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind's priesthood, she attends to rituals of spiritual purification and communion with Elune. Travelers exploring Teldrassil are often directed to her when matters involve sacred offerings and the mystical wildlife of the boughs. Within the serene marble halls of the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora spends her days in contemplation and service. As an ordained priestess of Elune, she assists in tending the spiritual needs of Darnassus and preserving the delicate rituals passed down through millennia. While much of the Sisterhood oversees military defenses or diplomacy, A'moora focuses on traditional devotions and sacred matters concerning the natural spirits of Teldrassil. A'moora is tied to the sad fate of Lady Sathrah, a great spider once beloved of Elune whose silvery dew was kept in the temple for its healing powers. When Sathrah descended into madness, A'moora sent young adventurers to the northern borders of Teldrassil near Wellspring Lake to end her suffering and bring back her silvery spinnerets. Offered at the temple's fountain, the spinnerets become a sacrifice to Elune so that Sathrah might be reborn at peace.

npc:priestess-anetta.text: Priestess Anetta. Inside Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta teaches new priests their first rites of the Holy Light. She is a human cleric and a member of the Brotherhood of Northshire. On the ground floor of Northshire Abbey, Priestess Anetta keeps to the quiet library wing. Defias bandits and kobolds trouble the valley, and she reminds those who pass that the Light may be the one thing that saves them someday. New human priests come to Priestess Anetta in the cloister with a hallowed letter of introduction. She teaches them to channel holy words to mend flesh and call down smiting radiance against evil. Under her guidance, the young acolytes prepare to carry the Light beyond Northshire's secluded walls.

npc:priestess-josetta.text: Priestess Josetta. In Goldshire, Priestess Josetta guides young priests beyond their first trials in Northshire. She teaches faith, devotion, and the work of serving others. Priestess Josetta tends to the people of Elwynn Forest from an upstairs room in the Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers, guards, and local workers come within her reach there. She offers spiritual care among ordinary folk, showing that service to the Holy Light can be given wherever people need comfort. Priestess Josetta guides young priests who have finished their first studies at Northshire Abbey. She sends them into the countryside to help wounded guards and comfort those who suffer. Their work teaches them that priesthood asks more than prayers learned by heart. They must put the Light to work and help mend a broken world. Priestess Josetta regrets that she did not travel farther when she was young. She chose familiar ground over the wider roads of Azeroth. Though she is content with her sacred service in Goldshire, she urges the young disciples who visit her to be bolder and carry their faith to distant frontiers.

npc:prospector-ironband.text: Prospector Ironband. At Ironband's Excavation Site, Prospector Ironband directs a dig into Khaz Modan's buried past. He leads the Dwarven Explorers' Guild's work in southeastern Loch Modan, seeking the heritage of the dwarven people and sending reports and relics to Ironforge despite setbacks and hostile creatures. Prospector Ironband leads the dig at Ironband's Excavation Site in the hills of southeastern Loch Modan. Like other field researchers in the Explorers' Guild, he believes Khaz Modan's soil holds truths about the origins of the dwarven race. His camp digs trenches and sifts rubble for ancient relics, stone tablets, and earthen artifacts. The work moves slowly, but Ironband remains resolute and welcomes capable travelers who can safeguard the operation. Local troggs and wildlife threaten the excavation in Loch Modan's rugged wilds. They put the dig's supply lines and equipment at risk, and relics and survey tools may be stolen or wrecked before the Guild can examine them. Ironband relies on visiting Alliance travelers to guard cargo shipments, hold off raiders, and look into missing Guild contacts in the neighboring badlands.

npc:prospector-remtravel.text: Prospector Remtravel. In southern Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel leads an Explorers' League dig among ancient relics. The dwarf's scattered focus and the dangers around camp make his work perilous. The Explorers' League sent Prospector Remtravel across the sea to establish a dig in southern Darkshore. Night elves guard their ancestral lands, yet the League's drive to uncover Azeroth's origins carries its prospectors into forgotten places. Remtravel unearths fossilized history and ancient stones, while aggressive wildlife and hostile local threats make the camp difficult for one scatterbrained dwarf to manage.

npc:prospector-ryedol.text: Prospector Ryedol. Prospector Ryedol is an Explorers' League surveyor stationed on a dusty rise overlooking the eastern Badlands. Watching over the perilous excavations below, he strives to recover lost dwarven relics and maintain hope in a barren wasteland overrun by troggs and beasts. Perched upon a rugged hill just south of Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol represents the ongoing efforts of Ironforge's Explorers' League in the Badlands. The arid valley is rich in ancient titan secrets and earthen heritage, but field expeditions here are constantly beleaguered by savage troggs, ravenous coyotes, and territorial drakes. Ryedol coordinates retrieval efforts for dwarven gear stolen by the Dark Iron dwarves and seeks signs of hope amid the ruined outposts, determined not to let the League's sacrifices in the wastes be in vain.

npc:prospector-stormpike.text: Prospector Stormpike. In Ironforge, Prospector Stormpike oversees support for distant archaeological digs. A blunt, short-tempered dwarf of the renowned Stormpike clan, he also uses his sharp mind to decipher coded messages. Prospector Stormpike coordinates excavations from the Library of the Hall of Explorers. His work sends supplies, including blasting powder, to distant sites across Khaz Modan and beyond. He is impatient with idle chatter, but his dedication to uncovering dwarven history runs deep. His keen mind can break intricate ciphers, making him a useful ally to scouts facing secret threats.

npc:prospector-whelgar.text: Prospector Whelgar. At Whelgar's Excavation Site, Prospector Whelgar's search for titan relics has stalled. Vicious raptors overran the dig, and he seeks hardy adventurers to recover ancient artifacts. Prospector Whelgar leads a dwarven dig in the Wetlands. His camp, Whelgar's Excavation Site, lies east of Menethil Harbor, where he searches for the history of the dwarven race. Ancient stone relics once filled the valley, but territorial raptors drove his team into hiding. Whelgar refuses to leave his duty unfinished. He still hopes to recover valuable relics, including the Goaz Stone, before predators or rival scoundrels ruin the site.

npc:quartermaster-lewis.text: Quartermaster Lewis. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Quartermaster Lewis keeps supplies moving to the People's Militia. He serves local defenders and travelers holding the frontier against the Defias Brotherhood. Quartermaster Lewis keeps the militia's supplies in Sentinel Tower. Stormwind's royal leaders offer little aid to impoverished Westfall, so Sentinel Hill depends on local volunteers and whatever provisions they can gather. Lewis hands out field necessities, including dry rations, fresh water, arrows, shot, and throwing blades. The fighters standing watch need these basics to endure Defias raids.

npc:quinn-yorick.text: Quinn Yorick. At the Ivar Patch, Quinn Yorick hides from the ghoul that wounded him. The Forsaken scout waits in a ruined farmhouse, unable to finish his mission or retreat alone. Quinn Yorick lies gravely injured upstairs in a ruined farmhouse at the Ivar Patch. Ivar the Foul, a ghoul lurking in the farm’s barn in northern Silverpine Forest, wounded him in a vicious clash. Quinn and his sister Rane were sent to scout Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. Too hurt to finish the mission or make a safe retreat alone, he remains in hiding. Passing travelers working for the Forsaken bring him healing and deal with the creature that nearly tore him apart.

npc:ragnar-thunderbrew.text: Ragnar Thunderbrew. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Ragnar Thunderbrew keeps the family tavern supplied and its patrons fed. The dwarven brewer is known across Dun Morogh for the family's Beer Basted Boar Ribs. Ragnar Thunderbrew tends the kitchen and brewing work at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Mountaineers, travelers, and gnome refugees fleeing Gnomeregan gather there. His Beer Basted Boar Ribs, made with dwarven ale, are a Dun Morogh specialty. Supplies have grown hard to find since his usual meat provider enlisted in the King's Army. Ragnar now relies on wandering mountaineers and hunters to bring fresh crag boar flanks to the kitchen. Across Ironforge territory, the Thunderbrew name is known for dwarven drink and tavern life. Ragnar has kept the distillery running since his older brother, Grimbooze Thunderbrew, disappeared in a drunken haze a few harvests ago. He guards the family's brewing heritage against thieves such as the Dark Iron dwarves, who stole the recipe for Thunderbrew Lager. With patrons restless, supplies scarce, and disputes breaking out in the tavern, Ragnar keeps the taps flowing and travelers fed in Kharanos.

npc:rahauro.text: Rahauro. On Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, Rahauro sends Horde fighters against threats beneath Orgrimmar. He serves Magatha Grimtotem, coordinating the response to troggs in Ragefire Chasm and the search for a fallen agent’s possessions. Rahauro attends Magatha Grimtotem on the high terrace of Elder Rise. He speaks and acts for the elder crone, who relies on trusted servants to recruit others. When wild creatures swarm beneath the orcish capital, Rahauro handles the arrangements and sends Horde mercenaries to face them. Troggs in the caverns of Ragefire Chasm rejected Magatha’s attempt to make peace. Her envoys went below Orgrimmar to parley, but the troggs attacked and killed them. Magatha sees the creatures as a threat to the Horde, and Rahauro sends champions into the caverns to thin their numbers and learn their strength.

npc:raleigh-andrean.text: Raleigh Andrean. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean lives among the Forsaken. His requests show how little regard he has for his human life and those he once knew. Before the Third War, Raleigh Andrean lived in Lordaeron as a human. He was married to Deliah and counted Valdred Moray as a friend. The Scourge swept through the kingdom, killing Raleigh and raising him as a mindless thrall in service to the Lich King. After the Lich King's grip shattered and Sylvanas Windrunner led her uprising, Raleigh regained his free will and joined the Forsaken in the Undercity.

npc:randis.text: Randis. In Cathedral Square, Randis waits for a chance to see the world beyond Stormwind. During Children's Week, he eagerly joins willing adventurers across Alliance lands. Randis lives in the orphanage near Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, one of many children left without family by the realm's conflicts. When Children's Week comes each year, Orphan Matron Nightingale gives sympathetic heroes a whistle and entrusts them with his care. Curious and full of questions, Randis dreams of adventure, asks riddles, and declares that he wants to be king of Stormwind when he grows up. For Randis, who spends most days in Cathedral Square, leaving the capital is a grand adventure. He remarks that places like Ironforge smell odd, and his wonder shows what Alliance heroes fight to protect.

npc:ranger-glynda-nal-shea.text: Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea. Near Auberdine's watch, Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea directs the defense of Darkshore. The seasoned night elf sentry sends travelers to meet threats and investigate strange signs along the coast. From Auberdine, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea coordinates scouts as corruption grows and hostile forces press into Darkshore. She watches the wilderness around town and relies on capable travelers to guard the perimeter and protect night elf holdings along the coast. Glynda watches for dangers gathering along the shore, especially the bolder murlocs south of town. She oversees bounties on threats such as Murkdeep and sends scouts to examine strange finds, including a crimson crystal reported near Darkshore's eastern mountain range.

npc:rau-cliffrunner.text: Rau Cliffrunner. Rau Cliffrunner is a tauren scout and scholar stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to protecting his people from regional threats, he studies the history and origins of the hostile Galak centaur through their ancient relics. Working closely with allies in Thunder Bluff, Rau coordinates ventures into dangerous enemy strongholds across the canyon. Perched on the perilous bluffs of Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner maintains a watchful eye over the sweeping, sun-scorched expanse of Thousand Needles. The tauren outpost serves as a crucial Horde sanctuary in an otherwise hostile territory teeming with ferocious predators, quilboar, and aggressive centaur clans. Rau acts as both an outpost organizer and a dedicated investigator, keen on neutralizing emerging threats before they can overwhelm the vulnerable mesa settlements.

npc:razzle-sprysprocket.text: Razzle Sprysprocket. In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket works to recover gnomish machinery. He tinkers with Ozzie Togglevolt and seeks lost parts scattered through the snowy hills. After Gnomeregan's fall, Razzle found refuge in Dun Morogh and set up his workshop in Kharanos. He has a gift for delicate mechanical parts and works beside fellow engineer Ozzie Togglevolt. Together, they recover gyro-mechanisms and cog assemblies lost or scavenged during the flight from their irradiated homeland. Wild beasts roam Dun Morogh's frozen ridges, and local Frostmane trolls raid the area. These dangers keep Razzle's work from being safe. Still, he labors to keep gnomish contraptions working and recover the lost wonders of Gnomeregan.

npc:red-jack-flint.text: Red Jack Flint. In Menethil Keep, Red Jack Flint connects sailors with travelers bound across the sea. He is a seasoned human mariner and crew member of the Maiden's Virtue, helping travelers find passage and contacts toward Kalimdor. Red Jack Flint is a seasoned sailor in Menethil Keep. A crewman of the Maiden's Virtue, he knows the sea routes from Khaz Modan to distant shores. He also directs capable travelers to allies across the Great Sea, including Fiora Longears in Kalimdor.

npc:rema-schneider.text: Rema Schneider. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider works from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is a human citizen who often helps local shopkeepers and artisans with trade deliveries. Rema Schneider manages daily trade from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. The shop stands just west of the stone bridge into Cathedral Square, along Stormwind's canals. Cloth and finished garments move between local craftsmen, and Rema relies on helpful couriers to carry supplies between workshops.

npc:remulos.text: Remulos. Keeper Remulos is a demigod son of Cenarius and the venerable protector of Moonglade. Alongside Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and Hamuul Runetotem, he helps guide the Cenarion Circle in the absence of his fallen father and the sleeping Malfurion Stormrage. Unlike Staghelm, Remulos prioritizes the broader balance of nature over night elven isolationism. Keeper Remulos is an immortal keeper of the grove, bearing the lower body of a great stag and the antlered torso of an ancient dryad-father. He watches over Moonglade, the sacred sanctuary of Azeroth's druids nestled north of Mount Hyjal. While Malfurion Stormrage remains trapped in the Emerald Dream, Remulos provides divine authority and counsel to the mortals of the Cenarion Circle. He remains deeply invested in healing Azeroth's scars, offering aid to druids pursuing their sacred rites around Lake Elune'ara. Remulos frequently finds himself at ideological odds with Archdruid Fandral Staghelm. While Staghelm champions night elven supremacy and sought to restore their lost immortality through Teldrassil, Remulos vehemently opposed the planting of the new World Tree as an act of hubris. Defying Staghelm's isolationist faction, Remulos welcomed Hamuul Runetotem and the tauren into the Cenarion Circle, sharing nature's closely guarded mysteries with their shamans-turned-druids to restore the land collectively.

npc:remy-two-times.text: Remy "Two Times". In Goldshire, Remy "Two Times" trades goods and pays for raw materials. He came from the Redridge Mountains and repeats the ends of his sentences. Remy "Two Times" trades from Goldshire, where he deals with travelers. He came west from the Redridge Mountains. When he speaks, he usually repeats the last words of each sentence twice. The odd habit gives him his nickname, but it does not keep him from seeking a profit in troubled Elwynn Forest. Kobolds overrun the local gold mines, and aggressive murlocs infest the riverbanks, disrupting trade in Elwynn. Remy turns to travelers for help. He pays for pouches of gold dust gathered from kobolds in the mines and keeps watch on suspicious murloc movements near Crystal Lake.

npc:renato-gallina.text: Renato Gallina. In Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina calls travelers toward his family's winery. Renato Gallina calls to passers-by among the Trade District stalls, proclaiming his family's vintages the finest in Stormwind. The Gallina family runs a winery along the Canals, and Renato promotes it with pamphlets. Travelers can bring one to his sister Suzetta at the shop for a free bottle of wine.

npc:renee-lauer.text: Innkeeper Renee. Travelers find food, drink, and shelter with Innkeeper Renee at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Innkeeper Renee welcomes weary newcomers to the Gallows' End Tavern, Brill's central inn. She sells food, drink, and general goods from behind her counter, and remarks that the Forsaken have huge appetites. Her tavern offers the undead of Tirisfal a cozy place to rest as plague victims make their way in the world. Newcomers to Brill often stop first at Renee's inn. Calvin Montague of Deathknell sends fresh adventurers to her with a nondescript letter, the word she has eagerly awaited. Beneath the tavern's floorboards, the cellar also holds a captured Scarlet Crusade zealot.

npc:renzik-the-shiv.text: Renzik "The Shiv". In Stormwind's Old Town, Renzik "The Shiv" directs SI:7's new rogue recruits. The goblin is Spymaster Mathias Shaw's trusted second-in-command, receiving promising agents sent from across the Alliance. Renzik keeps his past to himself. In Stormwind, he is known as a goblin who rose to become Spymaster Mathias Shaw's second-in-command in SI:7. He has little patience for pleasantries. When new recruits arrive, he asks whether they are ready to work or need a nap first. Renzik works inside SI:7's secretive fortress in Old Town, second-in-command to Mathias Shaw. Rogue mentors across the Alliance, from Ironforge to Darnassus, send their most promising agents to him. He sends them to field instructors such as Lucius in Redridge, where they can hone the skills needed to survive in the field.

npc:rezlak.text: Rezlak. Along Durotar's roads south of Orgrimmar, Rezlak waits for help with his supply lines. The goblin entrepreneur belongs to the Tinkers' Union and hires travelers to recover missing supplies and drive off harpies. Rezlak waits beside the canyon road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. He represents the Tinkers' Union, a goblin syndicate focused on engineering, supply lines, and practical business. The factional tensions of Kalimdor matter little to him while trade runs smoothly. Dustwind harpies have raided his cargo caravans and made the routes unsafe. Rezlak remains at his post and hires passersby willing to earn a profit by recovering supplies and dealing with the harpies.

npc:rhinag.text: Rhinag. Among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border, Rhinag waits, weakened by scorpids' venom. The Darkspear troll depends on passing travelers to find him a remedy in time. Rhinag shelters among the rocks near Durotar's northwestern border after a Venomtail Scorpid stung him. The poison has left the Darkspear troll weak and isolated. He needs a venomtail antidote, and his survival depends on whether a passing traveler can find one before the toxins take their toll.

npc:ringo.text: Ringo. Ringo is an unfortunate goblin explorer who ventured up the blistering heights of Fire Plume Ridge in Un'Goro Crater. Overwhelmed by the volcano's stifling heat and noxious vapors, he collapsed inside a cave, desperate for someone to help him back down. His close friend Spraggle Frock remains worried sick back at Marshal's Refuge. While goblins are known for braving hazardous environments in search of wealth or oddities, Fire Plume Ridge proves harsh even by their standards. Towering in the center of Un'Goro Crater, the active volcano spews ash, magma, and boiling steam. Ringo climbed about halfway up the southern face before the suffocating heat finally proved too much for him. Leaving his belongings scattered just outside, he crawled into a cave to shelter from the sweltering atmosphere, completely incapacitated by heat exhaustion.

npc:rivern-frostwind.text: Rivern Frostwind. Rivern Frostwind is a night elf riding instructor stationed high atop Frostsaber Rock in northern Winterspring. Accompanied by his frost tiger companion Glacier, he watches over the native wintersabers and trains riders deemed worthy by his order. Only the most dedicated champions of the Alliance are granted the honor of riding one of his prized mounts. Perched on the icy promontory of Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind oversees the breeding and stewardship of the legendary Winterspring frostsaber. While nightsabers roam the lush forests of Teldrassil and Ashenvale, their sub-arctic cousins are bred to endure the bitter cold of northern Kalimdor. Rivern acts as a gatekeeper for these majestic predators. He demands that outsiders prove their commitment to preserving the beasts—gathering fresh meat from the tundra, clearing out Winterfall furbolgs, and driving back rampaging frost giants—before he will even consider entrusting one of the sabers to them.

npc:roetten-stonehammer.text: Roetten Stonehammer. Roetten Stonehammer works from the Library in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. He represents Reclaimers Inc., organizing expeditions and hiring adventurers for salvage work in distant lands such as Desolace. In the Hall of Explorers' Library, Roetten Stonehammer handles practical recovery for Reclaimers Inc. He connects mercenaries with salvage work across Kalimdor. His associates seek valuable cargo, wreckage, and rare reagents in dangerous lands such as Desolace.

npc:royal-historian-archesonus.text: Royal Historian Archesonus. At the High Seat, Royal Historian Archesonus records catastrophes for the Ironforge crown. A dwarven scholar serving King Magni Bronzebeard, she writes of recent calamities in the northern human kingdoms and oversees research into ancient dwarven tragedies, including the scorched remains of the Dark Iron kingdom. Royal Historian Archesonus keeps Ironforge’s records near King Magni Bronzebeard’s throne in the High Seat. Her studies reach beyond the Khaz Modan mountains. She wrote 'The Fall of Lordaeron and the Scouring of the Eastweald' and 'On Plagues, Curses, and Blights,' tracing the Scourge’s ruin of humanity’s northern realm. Archesonus faces these dark histories with care, seeking to record the truth of ruinous magic and political collapse. Royal Historian Archesonus also oversees research into the War of the Three Hammers and the destruction of Thaurissan. She seeks recovered relics and charred tablets from the Smoldering Ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes, and sends adventurers there to search. Her work examines the cataclysm that scorched the Burning Steppes and bound the Dark Iron clan to the Firelord.

npc:ruga-ragetotem.text: Ruga Ragetotem. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem trains warriors for the Horde. He tests them against the silithid in the southern Barrens before sending the proven toward custom armor. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem trains warriors who want to prove their strength in Kalimdor. Silithid have suddenly appeared to the south, carving hives into the Field of Giants. Ruga sends young fighters to hunt the insectoids and cut off their antennae. Those who endure the trial earn his respect and a recommendation to Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned armorsmith.

npc:rutgar-glyphshaper.text: Rutgar Glyphshaper. Rutgar Glyphshaper is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at the Bronzebeard Encampment in the southern reaches of Silithus. As a member of Brann Bronzebeard's expedition, he studies ancient silithid relics and runes, striving to uncover the mystery of the hives even after Brann wanders off into the desert. Rutgar Glyphshaper traveled to Silithus under the leadership of Brann Bronzebeard to investigate the vast silithid hives and unearth lost relics buried beneath the desert wastes. Establishing their base at the Bronzebeard Encampment south of Cenarion Hold, Rutgar and his companions frequently ventured directly into the bug hives to harvest inscribed stones and runic artifacts, often cooperating with Cenarion night elf researchers.

npc:ruul-eagletalon.text: Ruul Eagletalon. At Bloodhoof Village, Ruul Eagletalon watches the settlement’s borders. He keeps an eye on Mulgore’s wildlife, especially the aggressive Windfury harpies pressing into tauren lands. Ruul Eagletalon tends to Bloodhoof Village’s security as young braves arrive from Camp Narache. Mulgore is a peaceful homeland beside the arid wastes of the Barrens, yet territorial predators and hostile creatures still press against its pastures. Ruul watches for dangers on the nearby plains and directs capable travelers against the savage Windfury harpies, which prey on unwary nomads and game.

npc:ruul-snowhoof.text: Ruul Snowhoof. Deep in northern Ashenvale, Ruul Snowhoof waits for rescue. The tauren druid is trapped in bear form inside a crude cage at Thistlefur Hold, relying on Horde adventurers to free him and guide him to safety. Ruul Snowhoof entered northern Ashenvale and fell into the hands of the corrupt Thistlefur furbolgs. He took the shape of a bear, and his captors mistook him for a wild beast. They locked him in a wooden cage deep within Thistlefur Hold instead of killing him. Now weakened and unable to safely leave his form or fight his way out alone, Ruul waits for Horde allies to open the cage, drive off his captors, and clear a path through the den. He hopes to return to his sister, Yama Snowhoof, at Splintertree Post.

npc:rwag.text: Rwag. In the Den, Rwag teaches the first steps of a rogue's craft. The orc trains newly arrived orcs and trolls in stealth, subterfuge, and dirty fighting in Durotar's Valley of Trials, under the Horde's watch. Deep in the Den, Rwag trains fledgling rogues, cutpurses, and thieves before they venture beyond the cave into Durotar. The new Horde champions martial honor and battlefield valor, but Rwag knows subtlety, poisons, and a well-placed dagger remain tools for survival in the unforgiving desert. He keeps watch over business in the Valley and distrusts the dark practitioners sheltering in the cave, especially the warlock Nartok.

npc:saelienne.text: Saelienne. On the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, Saelienne keeps an inn for travelers and artisans. She offers food, drink, and a place to bind a Hearthstone in the night elven capital. Innkeeper Saelienne welcomes residents and visitors to her inn on Darnassus's Craftsmen's Terrace. She gives travelers a calm place to rest and serves night elven refreshments and goods brought through the city port. Tradesfolk come in after long hours at the forge or loom. Saelienne's inn gives them a place to gather and recover.

npc:sally-whitemane.text: High Inquisitor Whitemane. Whitemane is the High Inquisitor of the Scarlet Crusade, presiding over the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A powerful priestess of the Holy Light, her consuming hatred for the undead drives the Crusade's uncompromising zealotry. Together with Scarlet Commander Renault Mograine, she directs the order's military and ideological campaigns across Lordaeron.
