Rising rapidly through the Scarlet Crusade's hierarchy, Whitemane became its High Inquisitor and took command of the Scarlet Monastery's grand Cathedral. Renowned for her fearsome mastery of Holy magic, she has become one of the Crusade's foremost symbols through her absolute conviction, wielding the Light as an unrelenting weapon against any deemed unclean.

npc:salma-saldean.text: Salma Saldean. At Saldean's Farm, Salma Saldean keeps a welcome place for travelers. She and her husband, Farmer Saldean, tend the homestead in Westfall, where bandits threaten the farms and Stormwind has left the region. She offers meals in return for help around the farm. Salma Saldean welcomes travelers to a farm that has endured where neighboring homesteads have burned or fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. A hearty pot waits on the stove, and she looks for capable hands to help around the farmstead. Salma feeds her family and visitors with what Westfall provides. She teaches travelers to make Goretusk liver pie and Westfall stew with wild boar, vultures, murlocs, and stray okra.

npc:sara-balloo.text: Sara Balloo. In Ironforge's Military Ward, Sara Balloo mourns her husband Sully and holds fast to the words he left behind. Sara Balloo keeps vigil in Ironforge's Military Ward, amid the clang of weapons and the drill of soldiers. Her husband, Sully Balloo, fell in battle far from home, leaving her alone with grief and memories. A final letter, carried across the mountains from where he died, gives Sara words from his last days and a measure of closure.

npc:sara-timberlain.text: Sara Timberlain. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain stitches gear for the Stormwind Army. She makes useful armaments from salvaged cloth and leather. Sara Timberlain works with needle and thread outside a small cottage on the western edge of Eastvale Logging Camp. Axes sound through the camp as workers fell trees. Though Eastvale lies far from settled lands, wolves and murlocs prowl nearby, and Sara still offers travelers hospitality. She turns scraps of linen and salvaged bandanas into sturdy gear. Her skill has earned official recognition and commissions to supply cloth and leather armaments to Stormwind's military forces.

npc:scooty.text: Scooty. In Booty Bay, Scooty runs a teleport link to Gnomeregan from the busy pirate port. The goblin engineer calls himself a master of his craft and keeps transponders tied to an experimental pad in the fallen gnome city. His device gives Horde forces a perilous route into Dun Morogh. Scooty holds court among Booty Bay’s wharves and workshops as one of the Steamwheedle Cartel’s most ambitious tinkerers. While many goblins favor gunpowder and explosives, he has turned to moving matter across great distances. He calibrates transponders to keep a working link with a teleportation pad inside Gnomeregan. Horde forces rely heavily on his craft to reach the subterranean gnome stronghold without crossing dangerous Alliance territory. Keeping experimental goblin teleporters running is rarely dull. After hearing of a new gnomish rig in Gnomeregan, Scooty and his partner Sovik built the Transpolyporter 6000. Scooty cheerfully admits it has exploded a dozen or so times. Crossing continents as scattered matter carries clear physical dangers, yet Scooty remains sure of his genius. He treats every mechanical failure as a small obstacle on the road to innovation.

npc:scout-riell.text: Scout Riell. At Sentinel Hill, Scout Riell watches Westfall from the watchtower roof. She serves the People's Militia, tracking the Defias Brotherhood and calling on travelers to bring back the outlaws' red silk bandanas. Scout Riell watches the plains from the stone tower at Sentinel Hill, where banditry and harvest golems threaten Westfall. Stormwind's royal army is absent, and the crown refuses aid, leaving the People's Militia to defend the region. From the tower roof, Riell tracks the Defias Brotherhood's movements and gathers proof of their crimes. She calls on passing travelers to take red silk bandanas from the bandits.

npc:scout-thaelrid.text: Argent Guard Thaelrid. Wounded near the Pool of Ask'ar, Argent Guard Thaelrid is cut off in Blackfathom Deeps. The night elf scout entered the submerged ruins for the Argent Dawn, and now he has seen what gathers below. Reports of foul rites beneath the sea reached the Argent Dawn from the Zoram Strand. The order watches for rising evils and unnatural corruption across Azeroth, so it sent Scout Thaelrid into Blackfathom Deeps. He was to judge the threat, watch the flooded temple, and report back. Then the Dawn could decide where aid was most needed.

npc:searn-firewarder.text: Searn Firewarder. In Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides Horde shamans toward the elements. Inside Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder guides shamans seeking the elements. Many Darkspear trolls commune with spirits through witch doctors and voodoo rituals. Searn guides initiates toward distant mentors and rites for the Call of Fire, Call of Water, and Call of Air, which teach them to commune with the elemental spirits of fire, water, and air. He stands among the Horde's high command in Orgrimmar.

npc:seer-graytongue.text: Seer Graytongue. On Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Graytongue guides young tauren through their first tribal trials. Near Camp Narache in Mulgore, he teaches them to honor the Earthmother before they enter the wider world. Young tauren braves and spellweavers find Seer Graytongue atop Red Cloud Mesa. From there, he guides those setting out from Camp Narache through sacred steps, including the Rites of the Earthmother. Their trials test resolve against Mulgore’s harsh plains and dangerous beasts. Through them, Graytongue teaches honor, patience, and reverence, virtues every tauren carries into adulthood.

npc:seer-ravenfeather.text: Seer Ravenfeather. At Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa, Seer Ravenfeather guides young tauren in the ways of the spirits and Mulgore's land. At Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather teaches young tauren who have chosen the shamanic path. Red Cloud Mesa is a sacred proving ground, and she prepares new practitioners for their duties before they venture farther into Mulgore. She teaches the rites that let them commune with elemental forces and honor the Earth Mother. Seer Ravenfeather guides new shamans through their first spiritual steps and the traditional Call of Earth rite. Under her guidance, initiates prepare ceremonial saptas and seek communion with the earthen spirits among the mesa's stony outcrops. The bond they forge anchors their elemental magic.

npc:seereth-stonebreak.text: Seereth Stonebreak. Near Greatwood Vale, Seereth Stonebreak watches the land's disturbances. The orc shaman camps on the border of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens, guiding travelers against environmental ruin, rogue machines, and rising tensions in Kalimdor. Seereth Stonebreak watches over Horde lands from her camp near Greatwood Vale. An orc shaman, she follows the harmony of the elements and protects the territories of the Horde. The land's spirits cried out against goblin plunder, and the Horde sent her to Stonetalon. There, she watches the landscape and guides travelers against dangers threatening the wild frontier. Seereth Stonebreak is troubled by turmoil across the Stonetalon range. Ruthless goblin ventures and mechanical shredders cutting through ancient woodlands have badly fractured the mountains' spiritual balance. She sends Horde envoys to confront the invaders and seek counsel from elder lorekeepers, in hopes of easing the land's distress.

npc:senator-mehr-stonehallow.text: Senator Mehr Stonehallow. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Senator Mehr Stonehallow faces a trogg infestation. The Ironforge politician and Explorers' League member has come to the front lines to oversee its containment, enlisting eager adventurers to cull the beasts before they overrun the quarry. Senator Mehr Stonehallow has left Ironforge's Senate halls for Gol'Bolar Quarry. A dwarf devoted to governance and the Explorers' League's historical pursuits, he knows the dangers facing the realm. When Rockjaw troggs clawed their way from the deep rock, Stonehallow traveled to the mining pit himself. He believes debate alone will not protect the workers, so he offers bounties to capable travelers who can drive back the aggressive troggs and reclaim the quarry.

npc:senior-surveyor-fizzledowser.text: Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is a goblin researcher working from Gadgetzan in Tanaris. He investigates disruptions around the local water supply and sends adventurers to look into the disappearance of Scrimshank.

npc:sentinel-arynia-cloudsbreak.text: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. At Oracle Glade on Teldrassil, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the northern groves. She guards the enchanted waters and woodland wildlife. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak keeps watch in Oracle Glade, one of Teldrassil's most secluded reaches. Far from Darnassus, she serves the Sentinel army among ancient trees and ethereal springs, guarding the wilderness from disturbance. Disharmony stirs among Teldrassil's creatures despite the tree's sacred birth. Arynia asks passing adventurers and young night elves to look into local troubles, from strange wildlife to mystical signs around the enchanted springs.

npc:sentinel-aynasha.text: Sentinel Aynasha. Along Darkshore’s wild borders, Sentinel Aynasha scouts the dangers threatening night elven lands. She watches enemy movements and carries urgent intelligence across the frontier. Sentinel Aynasha scouts and fights with the Sentinels where night elven lands meet hostile incursions. She carries urgent messages across rough country and watches for enemy patrols. Her skill with a bow and her knowledge of survival help her cross contested ground.

npc:sentinel-elissa-starbreeze.text: Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze. In Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches over the misty coast of Darkshore. From the upper floor of a lodge across the bridge, she tracks growing threats and directs travelers toward dangers in the wilderness. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze coordinates Auberdine's defenses from across the bridge. While other Sentinels patrol Darkshore's coast and woodlands, she watches from the upper floor of a building northeast of the town inn. She keeps alert for unusual disturbances across the region. Her directions send travelers to distant places, including the Tower of Althalaxx far to the north, so threats in the shadows do not catch Auberdine unaware.

npc:sentinel-farsong.text: Sentinel Farsong. At Silverwing Grove, Sentinel Farsong helps defend Ashenvale’s southern border. She rallies champions against the Warsong Outriders in Warsong Gulch. Sentinel Farsong keeps watch at Silverwing Grove as the Warsong clan cuts lumber and advances into night elf lands. She calls Alliance champions to strike at Warsong Outriders and sends field reports to Silverwing command. Her work helps check the Horde’s expansion and protect the woods.

npc:sentinel-onaeya.text: Sentinel Onaeya. At Maestra's Post, Sentinel Onaeya guards the northern edge of Ashenvale. The night elf guardian rallies Alliance adventurers to protect the forest and aid fellow sentinels. Maestra's Post is a wayside outpost on the road from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Sentinel Onaeya guards the lodge outside the settlement and coordinates its defense. Hostile wildlife, corrupting forces, and border tensions threaten night elf settlements in the region. Sentinel Onaeya hears that Sentinel Aynasha was attacked by furbolgs while carrying an important message through Darkshore. Onaeya rewards those who protect the poisoned sentinel until her antidote takes effect.

npc:sentinel-selarin.text: Sentinel Selarin. In Auberdine, Sentinel Selarin seeks help for Ashenvale's defenders. She carries Raene Wolfrunner's appeal to the coastal settlement as dangers threaten the forest. Sentinel Selarin carries Raene Wolfrunner's appeal from Ashenvale to Auberdine. With threats mounting across Ashenvale, the garrison is stretched thin. Selarin travels north along the forest road into Darkshore to find Terenthis and ask for help from the sentinels and scouts stationed on the coast. Terenthis cannot answer Selarin's appeal in person, so she remains in Auberdine to enlist travelers passing through Darkshore. She sends capable adventurers south to Astranaar, where they can bring their blades and spells to Raene Wolfrunner's beleaguered forces.

npc:sentinel-thenysil.text: Sentinel Thenysil. In Astranaar, Sentinel Tara Thenysil watches Ashenvale and the southern road into Stonetalon. She tracks military movements and keeps scouts watching neighboring lands, with special attention on allied forces moving south. At her post in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil helps guard Ashenvale as hostility grows. Night elf lands across the region face steady encroachment, so outposts must stay in contact. While much of the garrison defends the forest road, Thenysil sends Alliance volunteers beyond Ashenvale to support distant allies. Sentinel Thenysil shares a close friendship and military bond with Kaela Shadowspear, an operative sent south into the Stonetalon Mountains. When she learns Kaela was sent with an eccentric gnome mage, Thenysil takes the strange pairing as a sign of serious trouble in the peaks. Concerned for her comrade, she sends capable travelers south with support and asks them to report on the mission.

npc:sentinel-tysha-moonblade.text: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Along Darkshore’s road, Sentinel Tysha Moonblade watches a troubled coast. The night elf scout stands west of Ameth'Aran, guiding travelers and seeking help with the restless spirits haunting the nearby ruins. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade watches the road through Darkshore. East of her lie the ruins of Ameth'Aran, where cursed Highborne ghosts and malevolent banshees linger among ancient stone pillars. Auberdine's defenses are stretched thin by dangers along the coast, so Tysha asks capable travelers to uncover the history of Ameth'Aran's fall and put down its restless dead.

npc:sentinel-velene-starstrike.text: Sentinel Velene Starstrike. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike guards central Ashenvale. She protects the sanctuary and nearby waters from rogue elementals and foul sorcerers, keeping their magic from corrupting the ancient woodland. At Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike keeps watch from Silverwind Refuge. Night elf sentinels across Ashenvale work to preserve the forest's balance and defend elven sanctuaries. Silverwind Refuge offers travelers a place to rest in the central woods, and Velene helps keep the area safe. Peace around Silverwind Refuge can be easily disturbed. Velene watches Mystral Lake, where unruly elemental spirits and reckless mage summoners upset the wilderness. She directs champions against rogue water elementals and the careless spellcasters who disturb the spirits of the land.

npc:serge-hinott.text: Serge Hinott. In Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott brews mixtures for the Forsaken war effort. The Forsaken alchemist works alongside Apothecary Lydon, preparing concoctions, antidotes, and reagents for the Royal Apothecary Society. Serge Hinott brews remedies and other mixtures for the Forsaken in Tarren Mill. He works beside Apothecary Lydon, whose work includes chemical development and plague research against nearby human settlements such as Southshore. Hinott handles specialized brewing, including restorative salves and antidotes for field agents and scouts who face poisons or other toxic mishaps.

npc:shanda.text: Shanda. In Aldrassil, Shanda guides young night elf priests in the ways of Elune. She serves the Sisterhood of Elune in Shadowglen, teaching prayers, wards, and rites as her students prepare to defend Teldrassil. Shanda guides young night elves devoted to Elune from within Aldrassil. While druids tend Teldrassil's roots and boughs, priestesses keep the Kaldorei close to the White Lady. Shanda teaches new initiates to call on lunar grace for healing and protective wards, preparing them to face the corruption creeping into the World Tree's boughs. Young priests who awaken to their calling in Shadowglen come to Shanda to prove their devotion and learn their first prayers. Through rites such as In Favor of Elune, she tests their resolve, gives them blessed regalia, and teaches basic incantations. Her students learn to tend the wounded with a gentle hand and stand firm against the shadows.

npc:shandris-feathermoon.text: Shandris Feathermoon. Shandris Feathermoon is the General of the Sentinel Army and, for ten thousand years, Tyrande Whisperwind's right hand. She now commands night elf military forces throughout Kalimdor from Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the coast of Feralas. Shandris Feathermoon is one of the oldest defenders of the night elves. For ten thousand years she has served at Tyrande Whisperwind's side as the high priestess's right hand among the Sentinels, through the long vigil that followed the Sundering. Following the Great Sundering and the founding of the Sentinels, Shandris became an indispensable commander within the night elf military. Today, General Feathermoon serves as the supreme field commander of the Sentinel army. Stationed on Sardor Isle, she oversees Feathermoon Stronghold, an imposing elven fortress that keeps watch over the primal wilds of Feralas. From this island outpost, she monitors the encroaching threats of savage gnolls, lingering Gordunni ogres, hate-fueled satyrs, and the expanding power of the Horde in southern Kalimdor.

npc:shari-stilwell.text: Shari Stilwell. In Brill, Shari Stilwell trains Forsaken in the paladin's path. She is stationed in Tirisfal Glades, where the undead who endure the Light's pain learn holy and martial discipline. In Brill, Shari Stilwell guides Forsaken who seek the path of holy warriors. The Light brings the undead excruciating pain, yet she trains those willing to endure it. She helps newcomers find their footing in Tirisfal Glades, through early training and the adjustments of Forsaken life. Those she guides seek a place within the Forsaken kingdom. Shari bears the same family name as Daphne, Merissa, and Jordan Stilwell, a renowned smith among the living in the southern kingdoms. Whether the fall of Lordaeron tore Shari from these kin, or whether their bond is only distant, remains unknown amid the Scourge's devastation.

npc:shelene-rhobart.text: Shelene Rhobart. Along Tirisfal's road, Shelene Rhobart trains leatherworkers at a Deathguard waystation. She supplies cured hides and leathercraft training for the Forsaken's military and logistical efforts across the blighted lands. At a Deathguard waystation southeast of Brill, Shelene Rhobart works along the main road toward the ruins of Lordaeron. Practical crafts still matter in undeath, for survival and war. She turns pelts from Tirisfal's prowling beasts into tough hides, armor, straps, and field gear for Forsaken patrols facing the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders.

npc:shindrell-swiftfire.text: Shindrell Swiftfire. Astranaar’s defense reaches beyond Ashenvale’s forest. Shindrell Swiftfire, a night elf sentinel and scout, watches from the town at the heart of night elf operations in Ashenvale. Alert to changing dangers along Kalimdor’s western reaches, she directs capable Alliance adventurers toward threats on the coast and nearby mountain passes, helping coordinate local defense against dangers from sea and wilds. From Astranaar’s winding walkways, Shindrell Swiftfire watches the frontiers beyond Ashenvale. Sentinels face Horde logging incursions from the east and south, while Shindrell keeps watch beyond the woodland itself. Travelers arrive from Darkshore or set out toward Stonetalon’s jagged ridges, and she helps ensure Astranaar is not left undefended against danger from the flank. On Ashenvale’s northwestern shore, the troubled Zoram Strand draws Shindrell’s attention. Hostile naga have emerged from the ocean depths, a grave mystery and a direct threat to Kaldorei settlements. Shindrell sends seasoned fighters to investigate the shoreline and coordinate with scouts near the coast, seeking to contain the serpentine invaders before they gain a lasting foothold on ancient night elf lands.

npc:shoni-the-shilent.text: Shoni the Shilent. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent sends a crew beneath Westfall. She leads the gnomish effort to reclaim Gnomeregan and seeks power for the machines meant to break a path back into the city. Shoni the Shilent directs a gnomish assault crew from Stormwind’s Dwarven District. With Gnomeregan held by troggs, she plans to retake the city and sends operatives into the tunnels beneath Westfall for the parts her crew needs. Shoni’s plan depends on the gnomes’ gyrodrillmatic excavationators, heavy machines built to break through Gnomeregan’s underground borders and open a way for an assault. The machines lack power, so she seeks the intact Gnoam Sprecklesprocket from a working goblin shredder deep in the Deadmines. She also sends adventurers into Gnomeregan to dismantle its robots for spare parts to repair her fleet.

npc:sicco-thermaplugg.text: Mekgineer Thermaplugg. In ruined Gnomeregan, Mekgineer Thermaplugg rules from a massive mechanical battle suit. Once High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque’s trusted advisor, he brought about the city’s irradiation in a bid for power. The fallout transformed him into a leper gnome and left him deranged, ruling the ruined halls. For many years, Mekgineer Thermaplugg served as chief advisor to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, who trusted him completely. In secret, Thermaplugg coveted the High Tinker’s office. Even Mekkatorque cannot say what finally drove him to betray that trust. The High Tinker can only note that Thermaplugg would have had both power and wealth in time.

npc:sida.text: Sida. In Menethil Harbor, Sida lives apart from her estranged husband, Einar Stonegrip. She spends her days in the Wetlands port and sometimes ventures into the marshes, where she recently lost her bag near Ironbeard's Tomb. Sida lives in Menethil Harbor, the Alliance port in the Wetlands, apart from Einar Stonegrip. Their marriage is strained, and Einar refuses to travel to Menethil while Sida remains there. She still sometimes ventures beyond the coastal settlement into the Wetlands. On a recent trip toward Ironbeard's Tomb, she lost her personal bag.

npc:sirra-von-indi.text: Sirra Von'Indi. In Darkshire, Sirra Von'Indi studies the records that hold Duskwood's history. The town's historian knows ancient languages and helps decipher mysterious documents and the region's past. In Darkshire Town Hall, Sirra Von'Indi keeps the settlement's archives. While the town guard faces threats in the woods, he studies old texts and preserves the history of Grand Hamlet from before shadow fell across the region.

npc:sister-aquinne.text: Sister Aquinne. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne studies beneath the Priesthood of Elune at the Temple of the Moon. The novice acolyte serves in the Temple Gardens. Sister Aquinne studies with the Priesthood of Elune in the night elf capital. She is stationed in the Temple Gardens, beneath the Temple of the Moon, learning from the High Priestess and elder sisters. When a once-great creature of the forest needed help, Aquinne sent willing travelers to Priestess A'moora inside the temple to learn what had to be done.

npc:skorn-whitecloud.text: Skorn Whitecloud. At Bloodhoof Village, aging tauren hunter Skorn Whitecloud guides young hunters and aids travelers facing Mulgore’s dangers. Skorn Whitecloud lives at Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, where he guides young hunters in the ways of the hunt. He teaches respect for the plains’ wild creatures. Aspiring hunters prove themselves against cunning flatland prowlers, then take the claws to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff. Skorn wants those who take up bow or spear to understand the balance between predator and prey.

npc:skuerto.text: Skuerto. Skuerto is a dwarven scout stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Sent there by Archmage Malin alongside Apprentice Kryten, he aids the Alliance in the field, helping secure magical relics on Malin's behalf. Skuerto, a dwarf of Ironforge, works as a scout in the dangerous Arathi Highlands. Stationed alongside Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, he works under the direction of Archmage Malin to recover arcane reagents and potent magical artifacts that once belonged to Malin's old master, Archmage Trelane. Despite the harsh conditions of the Highlands, Skuerto takes considerable pride in his wilderness scouting and reacts poorly to anyone questioning his competence. His work regularly brushes up against regional perils, from the hostile Syndicate and Boulderfist ogres to dangerous ancient entities tied to the land.

npc:smith-argus.text: Smith Argus. At Goldshire's forge, Smith Argus keeps travelers and local smiths supplied. He repairs gear, teaches new smiths, and sends horseshoes to Redridge while coordinating with Stormwind craftsmen. Smith Argus works the forge near the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Gnolls, kobolds, and Defias bandits threaten the area, but Argus keeps the local militia and passing adventurers equipped. He mends armor and makes sturdy tools. As a blacksmithing trainer, he teaches new smiths to work copper and bronze. Goldshire's central position makes Smith Argus a link in Stormwind's regional supply. Craftsmen in nearby settlements turn to him for specialized gear and raw materials. Farrier Verner Osgood in Redridge depends on Argus for crafted horseshoes for pack animals and cavalry. Metalworkers in Stormwind's Dwarven District also arrange deliveries through him.

npc:solm-hargrin.text: Solm Hargrin. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Solm Hargrin teaches rogues the quiet arts. The dwarf trains young dwarves and gnomes, and holds that honor among thieves matters as tensions rise across Azeroth. Solm Hargrin trains rogues at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He welcomes young dwarves and gnomes, deciphers coded messages for them, and teaches techniques such as Eviscerate. Ironforge relies on mountaineers and warriors, but Solm knows some threats call for quieter methods. He teaches loyalty and honor among thieves as the world grows more unsettled.

npc:sprite-darter.text: Sprite Darter. Sprite Darters are small, iridescent faerie dragons native to the lush canopy of Feralas. Revered for their innate spiritual and magical qualities, they flit gracefully among the ancient trees. Recently, these rare creatures have become targets for local Grimtotem tauren who seek to capture and exploit them. Sprite Darters are elusive, winged woodland beasts native to the ancient forests of Feralas. Characterized by their gleaming, iridescent wings and mysterious spiritual essence, they embody the whimsical yet fierce magical ecology of Kalimdor's deep forests. Though generally peaceful and shy, their innate resistance to magical forces and natural power make them significant to those attuned to the wilderness. In recent times, the reclusive Sprite Darters have faced an unprecedented threat. The aggressive Grimtotem tauren clan inhabiting Feralas has begun rounding up and caging large numbers of these rare creatures for enigmatic purposes. Concerned night elves like Kindal Moonweaver actively recruit allies to disrupt the cages and liberate the trapped hatchlings before the Grimtotem bend them to their will. Beyond night elf efforts to safeguard them, the darters have caught the eye of outside observers studying primal power. Witch Doctor Uzer'i, a troll spiritualist operating out of Camp Mojache, takes a keen interest in the natural energies and muisek contained within the Sprite Darters, seeking their essence to unravel the unique magic thriving throughout Feralas.

npc:stitches.text: Stitches. Along Duskwood's western road, Stitches marches toward Darkshire, crushing the Night Watch and unwary travelers in his path. Near Abercrombie's shack, northeast of Raven Hill Cemetery, Stitches sets out east along the road toward Darkshire. Unholy sorcery and harvested corpses made the undead abomination, whose immense strength and malice overwhelm the Night Watch checkpoints. He tears through the defense camp across from Vul'Gol Ogre Mound and the outpost outside the Rotting Orchard, slaughtering travelers and town defenders along the way.

npc:supervisor-raelen.text: Supervisor Raelen. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen keeps timber moving toward Stormwind. She manages the laborers, tracks daily quotas, and oversees the lumber supply. Supervisor Raelen directs the woodcutters at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Marshal Patterson and the camp’s wagons. The camp stands on the edge of eastern Elwynn, near the Redridge Mountains, where the work brings its share of trouble. Raelen coordinates the crews and keeps them focused on their quotas despite hazards in the surrounding woods. She sees that gathered timber is processed, bundled, and sent on toward Stormwind.

npc:suzetta-gallina.text: Suzetta Gallina. At the Gallina Winery in Stormwind City, Suzetta Gallina tends the family wine business. Suzetta Gallina helps run the Gallina Winery along Stormwind's Canals. The shop offers wines imported from across the kingdom or crafted there. Her family supplies taverns, nobles, and common folk. Suzetta is no figure in high politics, but her work keeps the capital's trade moving through troubled times.

npc:syral-bladeleaf.text: Syral Bladeleaf. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf guides night elves arriving from Shadowglen. As a resident of Teldrassil, she speaks for the Council of the Forest and directs them to local caretakers, herbalists, and elders who watch over the crown's boughs. Syral Bladeleaf helps direct new arrivals through Dolanaar beneath Teldrassil's canopy. She speaks for the Council of the Forest, sending night elves to community leaders and herbalists in the village and nearby wilderness. Her guidance leads travelers to Denalan, a botanist at Lake Al'Ameth, and helps them replenish supplies for the village elders. In Dolanaar, Syral carries out the Council of the Forest's work for the village. She helps see that medicinal elixirs reach those in need and that disruptions to the local ecosystem receive swift attention.

npc:syurna.text: Syurna. In Darnassus, Syurna trains night elf rogues in the Cenarion Enclave. She guides aspiring scouts, spies, and covert operatives, then sends new rogues on trials of stealth and cunning. Syurna trains those who move unseen through Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, she teaches rogues evasion, lockpicking, and lethal strikes. The Sentinels display the Kaldorei’s martial strength, while the Sisterhood of Elune holds its spiritual wisdom. The Kaldorei also depend on shadows and stealth, and Syurna sharpens the eyes and blades that guard Teldrassil. Syurna tests young operatives beyond the lessons taught in the enclave. She sends promising initiates into deeper fieldwork to see whether they have the instincts to survive beyond the World Tree’s boughs and serve the Alliance in perilous frontier lands.

npc:tabetha.text: Tabetha. Tabetha is a reclusive, powerful human mage dwelling deep within Dustwallow Marsh at an isolated farmstead in the Quagmire. Far from the politics of Dalaran or Theramore, she instructs aspiring spellcasters and aids those seeking mastery over potent arcane and occult relics. Hidden away in the sodden expanse of Dustwallow Marsh north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a secluded shack alongside her apprentices. Surrounding herself with alchemical vials and ancient tomes, she has deliberately chosen solitude over the academic hierarchies of the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite her remote location, her mastery of the arcane is renowned enough that spellcasters across Kalimdor brave beasts and mire alike to seek her guidance. Tabetha stands notably apart from factional hostilities. While human by birth, she turns away neither Alliance nor Horde initiates who demonstrate the will to learn, providing tutelage to mages and assisting warlocks with dangerous bindings such as the Orb of Orahil. Her past connects her to figures like Menara Voidrender, revealing an extensive history with esoteric magic that transcends simple faction allegiance.

npc:tai-jin.text: Tai'jin. At the Razor Hill barracks, Tai'jin guides young Darkspear priests in their spiritual traditions. She teaches the balance of light and shadow and rites such as the Hex of Weakness. Tai'jin guides young priests from the Razor Hill barracks as they set out into Durotar. Orcs here turn chiefly to shamanism or warlock arts, while Darkspear trolls bring their communion with spirits and loas to the Horde. Tai'jin teaches the first principles of priesthood, the balance of light and shadow, and the spiritual heritage of troll culture.

npc:taiga-wisemane.text: Taiga Wisemane. Taiga Wisemane is a tauren elder residing in Shadowprey Village along the rugged western coast of Desolace. Watchful of demonic meddling across the barren wastes, he works to thwart the Burning Blade cult entrenched in the region. He directs Horde champions to disrupt demonic rituals and seal open gateways before the Burning Legion gains ground. Though Shadowprey Village is predominantly a Darkspear troll fishing settlement tucked away against the ocean, Taiga Wisemane has taken up station there to monitor the dark sorceries stirring across Desolace. He remains acutely aware of the spiritual corruption bleeding into the soil, keeping his focus fixed eastward where shadow cults and demonic remnants fester among ancient ruins.

npc:takar-the-seer.text: Takar the Seer. East of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer keeps a lone camp in the Barrens. Though surrounded by Horde lands, he remains loyal to the Alliance and shares occult knowledge with certain travelers. Takar the Seer lives alone beneath a simple tent east of Camp Taurajo. Tauren braves and orc patrols watch the surrounding Barrens, yet leave his remote clearing undisturbed. He distrusts curious Horde visitors but rarely starts a fight, keeping watch on the horizon and to himself. His camp lies far from Stormwind's politics. Takar the Seer shares his knowledge with a few visitors from beyond his camp. Alliance warlocks who come from the Eastern Kingdoms seek his cryptic counsel when they try to bind dangerous beings from beyond this world. His understanding of hidden forces and the craft of souls draws these practitioners to his remote, perilous camp.

npc:takata-steelblade.text: Takata Steelblade. Takata Steelblade is an orc warrior stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Dispatched from Orgrimmar by Keldran alongside Maurin Bonesplitter, he spearheads the Horde's local campaign against demonic corruption. His primary focus is eradicating the regional satyr population affiliated with the sinister Burning Blade. Takata Steelblade was sent from the capital to Desolace under direct orders from Keldran, an influential figure in Orgrimmar committed to uncovering and purging demonic subversion. Operating out of the isolated Tauren encampment of Ghost Walker Post, Takata coordinates military efforts against the Legion-aligned forces plaguing the barren wastes. While his companion Maurin Bonesplitter attempts to track and dismantle the clandestine Burning Blade cultists directly, Takata focuses on their demonic allies: the satyrs. Takata has orchestrated aggressive strikes against Desolace's corrupted satyrs, decimating their ranks to break the cult's local power structure and halt their spreading taint.

npc:tal.text: Tal. At Thunder Bluff, Tal tends the Horde's chief wind rider roost above the plains of Mulgore. He sends seasoned wyverns carrying travelers across Kalimdor. Tal tends the wind rider roost on Thunder Bluff's central mesa, linking the tauren capital with the rest of the Horde. He cares for the loyal wind riders, or wyverns, keeping them healthy and well-fed for long journeys across Kalimdor. From the roost, he sends messengers to Camp Taurajo and scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar. The flights keep the towering mesa city in touch with its allies.

npc:talen.text: Talen. At his camp by the Zoram Strand, Talen searches for kaldorei relics along the coast. Nearby naga and Horde outposts make the work dangerous. At a camp beside the Zoram Strand, Talen studies the past instead of taking up arms. Naga and Horde outposts make the coast dangerous, but he keeps searching the ruins beneath the waves and sands for lost kaldorei relics. He depends on travelers to face the Wrathtail naga and recover artifacts, including pristine statuettes and the Ring of Zoram, held by their leader Ruuzel.

npc:tallow.text: Tallow. At Tarren Mill, Tallow watches the contested front lines for the Dark Lady and the Horde. The Forsaken warrior helps organize strikes against Alliance threats in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tallow stands with the Forsaken and Horde forces holding Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Conflict stirs across the region, with Southshore humans nearby, Syndicate outlaws on the roads, and hostile wildlife beyond the town. Tallow sends capable adventurers against the Boulderfist ogres of the Arathi Highlands to test their strength. Then he directs them to aid the besieged outpost of Hammerfall.

npc:talvash-del-kissel.text: Talvash del Kissel. Talvash del Kissel is a down-on-his-luck gnome jeweler who fled the fall of Gnomeregan and now resides in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Plagued by debt and persistent rumors following the loss of his home, he seeks capable adventurers to help recover lost treasures and restore shattered relics. His keen eye for precious gems and ancient baubles makes him a valuable contact for those plumbing the depths of Uldaman. Once a respected jeweler in the technological heart of Gnomeregan, Talvash saw his livelihood obliterated alongside his home when the troggs overran the underground city. Escaping with the surviving refugees to the dwarven capital of Ironforge, he set up camp in the Mystic Ward. Unfortunately, relocation did not treat him kindly. Rumors of questionable dealings and unpaid obligations quickly piled up, sinking the craftsman into deep financial distress. Unable to rebuild his trade through conventional means, Talvash relies on freelance adventurers to retrieve lost assets and salvage his ruined reputation. Despite his misfortunes, Talvash has lost none of his gem-cutting precision or appraisal acumen. When explorers in the Badlands uncover an ancient, shattered necklace deep within the Titan vault of Uldaman, Talvash proves to be one of the few craftsmen in the Eastern Kingdoms capable of understanding its intricate enchantments. Restoring such power requires rare components and painstaking labor, but Talvash is eager to ply his trade—both to clear his debts and to prove his enduring skill.

npc:tammra-windfield.text: Tammra Windfield. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield guides Horde travelers in honoring the land's renewal. The tauren watches over the wilderness and the safety of her kin in the Stonetalon Mountains. Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde among the crags of Stonetalon. Harpies, Venture Company loggers, and predators threaten the settlement. Tammra Windfield watches over the mountain wilderness and the travelers who enter. Her gentle manner carries the resolve needed to keep a home safe in such rugged country. Tammra honors the Earth Mother by watching nature's steady rhythm of growth and decay. She asks travelers to tend the cycle of rebirth and bring forth new life, working against the harm conflict and exploitation cause in Stonetalon. For Tammra, protecting the land means healing it so life can flourish in scarred mountain soil. Tammra's concern reaches beyond the wilds to the companions and kin who travel Stonetalon's dangerous trails. When word comes that travelers or family have vanished among the crags, she is among the first to seek reliable aid. Sun Rock Retreat endures through loyalty and mutual protection, as well as harmony with nature.

npc:tannok-frosthammer.text: Tannok Frosthammer. At Thunderbrew Distillery outside Kharanos, Tannok Frosthammer waits anxiously for supplies from Coldridge Valley. Trogg attacks have cut off the roads to Anvilmar. Tannok Frosthammer watches deliveries and listens for news at Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Troggs have surged through Coldridge Pass, cutting off the usual route from Coldridge Valley and regular word from Anvilmar. Hands Springsprocket, a gnome tinkerer, carries supplies and news through the dangerous, snowy pass. Tannok shares the quiet worry of many Bronzebeards as subterranean troggs creep closer to their doorsteps.

npc:tarindrella.text: Tarindrella. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella watches over Teldrassil's sheltered woods. The dryad works with night elf protectors to investigate corruption among the World Tree's wildlife. Tarindrella dwells in Shadowglen, a protected glade atop Teldrassil. Dryads are fierce caretakers of nature, born of the demigod Cenarius. Many live deep in ancient Kalimdor forests such as Ashenvale, but Tarindrella watches over this young grove. She bridges the wild spirits and young night elf defenders taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil. Her chief concern is a taint creeping through the forest. She sends reliable adventurers to drive back local pests and gather clues to its source. Teldrassil is the new crown of the night elf people, yet sickness has reached its groves. Furbolgs once lived peacefully in their homes; now they have gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Grells and grellkin tainted by wicked Fel Moss infest the hills around Shadowglen. Tarindrella suspects the moss is behind these changes. She directs initiates to confront the grells and bring back samples, hoping to halt the corruption before it overtakes the young grove.

npc:tarrel-rockweaver.text: Tarrel Rockweaver. At Menethil Harbor’s bridge, Tarrel Rockweaver anxiously waits for news of his wife, Merrin. The dwarf fears for her safety after she joined an inland archaeological expedition. Tarrel Rockweaver watches the bridge at Menethil Harbor, where trade and military shipments pass. His wife, Merrin Rockweaver, joined Prospector Whelgar’s prestigious archaeological expedition deeper in the Wetlands. Violent raptors overran the excavation site and cut off regular communication. Stranded in town, Tarrel begs travelers to scout east toward Whelgar’s Excavation Site and learn whether Merrin survived.

npc:tatternack-steelforge.text: Tatternack Steelforge. On the Barrens frontier, Tatternack Steelforge offers work to travelers who can handle raw metal and dangerous wildlife. The orc smith studies local ores and seeks to arm Horde forces against threats across the plains. Across the Barrens, Horde outposts need weapons to face wild beasts, centaur raiders, and hostile quilboar. Tatternack Steelforge brings his people's metalworking knowledge to the frontier. He seeks practical weapons and unusual geological specimens to strengthen the Horde's foothold against those threats.

npc:tenaron-stormgrip.text: Tenaron Stormgrip. High in Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves through their people's recent history. He also asks them to gather water from a moonwell. Tenaron Stormgrip guides young night elves on Aldrassil's winding wooden platforms. From high in Shadowglen's central tree, he watches the local woods and their moonwells. He teaches novices about their spiritual bond with the World Tree. Tenaron sends initiates to gather a phial of water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Along the way, he teaches them what followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Their journey carries on through Teldrassil and into Darnassus.

npc:teronis-corpse.text: Teronis' Corpse. On an island in western Ashenvale, Teronis' Corpse lies in Lake Falathim. The night elf scout left Astranaar to find Dartol's Rod and help cleanse the forest. Teronis was sent from Astranaar to recover Dartol's Rod. Raene Wolfrunner gave the night elf scout this charge, seeking an ancient relic that could cleanse corrupted woodland magic. Teronis searched the waters of Lake Falathim, but hostile murlocs swarmed the island and killed him. His journal remains there, while the murlocs took the rod's radiant gemstone.

npc:thadius-grimshade.text: Thadius Grimshade. Thadius Grimshade is a Wildhammer dwarf diviner dwelling within the mage tower of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Though he parted ways with Aerie Peak long ago to study esoteric and darker magical arts, he remains loyal to his kin at heart. Unlike most Wildhammer dwarves who prefer the open skies and roaring winds of the Hinterlands, Thadius Grimshade makes his home inside Nethergarde Keep. Driven by a thirst for arcane divination and darker mystic lore, he relocated to the edge of the tainted Blasted Lands to pursue his esoteric studies. Despite his brooding discipline and separation from his clan, he retains a deep fondness for his homeland and gryphonkind, offering his rare scrying talents to those who come seeking aid on behalf of Aerie Peak.

npc:thalia-amberhide.text: Thalia Amberhide. Thalia Amberhide is a tauren residing at Freewind Post in the jagged canyon of Thousand Needles. A loyal friend to her kin, she waits with mounting concern for the safe return of Lakota Windsong from the clutches of the Grimtotem clan. Perched atop the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Thalia Amberhide is a quiet presence among the bustling tauren settlement. Her heart is heavy with worry for her close companion, Lakota Windsong, who was taken captive by Arnak Grimtotem and his treacherous kin. Thalia relies on passing Horde adventurers who brave the canyon depths to find Lakota, break her bonds, and guide her safely back up the lifts to the haven of the mesa.

npc:tharek-blackstone.text: Tharek Blackstone. In Kharanos, Tharek Blackstone keeps dwarven tools flowing to local craftsmen. Beldin Steelgrill at Steelgrill's Depot is his main customer, and Tharek also helps travelers find work around town. Tharek Blackstone keeps his forge busy in Kharanos, repairing gear and making tools for local workers. His main customer is Beldin Steelgrill, whose mechanostrider depot just outside town needs a steady supply of heavy wrenches, gears, and replacement tools. Tharek hires passing travelers to carry finished crates to the depot, so he can keep up with the work at his forge. Tharek has earned the respect of people across Dun Morogh through his work at the anvil. He holds no formal military title, but people in town turn to him for odd jobs, supply runs, and help coordinating local efforts.

npc:tharnariun-treetender.text: Tharnariun Treetender. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches Darkshore’s wilds for signs of sickness. The night elf naturalist studies the corruption spreading through local plants and animals, seeking ways to protect them. In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender watches the woods beyond the port. Hostile satyrs and foul shoreline washaways threaten the village, but his work centers on the natural world around it. He believes neglecting nature invites ruin, so he studies the decline of the local woods and searches for ways to fight the sickness spreading across the forest floor.

npc:the-defias-traitor.text: The Defias Traitor. At Sentinel Hill, The Defias Traitor has given up the Brotherhood's hidden base to save his life. The captured outlaw is held beneath the watchtower after the People's Militia caught him stealing Farmer Saldean's wagon.

npc:theldurin-the-lost.text: Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost is a reclusive, half-mad dwarf wandering the scorched expanses of the Badlands. Formerly aligned with the insidious Twilight's Hammer cult, he fled their ranks with stolen sacred relics after realizing the horror of their designs. Perched in the barren hills of the Badlands, clutching bags of explosives in wild paranoia, Theldurin is far more than a simple mad hermit. He was once an initiate of the Twilight's Hammer cult. When the sinister cabal sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, Theldurin recoiled in terror, rejected their mad teachings, and fled into the desert. He carried with him the Scroll of Myzrael, desperate to prevent his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. Though the escape cost him his sanity, his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

npc:therylune.text: Therylune. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Therylune waits for a chance to escape her captors. Twilight's Hammer cultists have trapped the dryad at the ancient site, and she needs a traveler's help to reach safety. Therylune is a dryad, a daughter of Cenarius who guards nature. She came from the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor to the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Twilight's Hammer cultists have gathered at the ancient excavation and ambushed her. Surrounded by their swarms, she cannot fight her way free alone. She needs an escort through the cultists and out to safety.

npc:therysil.text: Therysil. At the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale, Therysil waits for word of her sister. The dryad is devoted to protecting nature, but Therylune has been taken by the Twilight's Hammer cultists. Therysil keeps watch near the waters of the Shrine of Aessina in Ashenvale's ancient woods. As a dryad and daughter of Cenarius, she is bound to defend the wild and its spirits. Her thoughts now turn to Therylune, captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult. Therysil waits anxiously for a wandering ally who can help rescue her sister.

npc:thor.text: Thor. At Sentinel Hill, Thor keeps Westfall linked to Stormwind by gryphon flight. His trained mounts carry travelers and urgent messages above the dangerous roads. Thor tends the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill, linking Westfall's defenders with the rest of the kingdom. The People's Militia faces bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems on the ground. Thor's gryphons carry travelers and military dispatches above the perilous roads. Reports from Gryan Stoutmantle and urgent requests for aid can reach the court in Stormwind far faster than a ground messenger.

npc:thorgas-grimson.text: Thorgas Grimson. Inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, Thorgas Grimson trains new hunters. A seasoned outdoorsman of Dun Morogh, he believes the frozen wilds teach survival best. Thorgas Grimson welcomes new mountaineers and scouts inside Anvilmar. He teaches young hunters to leave dry lectures behind and learn in the freezing winds. With bow or gun in hand, they track Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

npc:thorgrum-borrelson.text: Thorgrum Borrelson. Above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson tends the gryphons that carry travelers across Loch Modan. His roost links the valley with Ironforge and the mountain passes nearby. Thorgrum Borrelson keeps the gryphon roost on the bluff above Thelsamar. His trained gryphons carry the Alliance across Loch Modan, where troggs and gnoll packs threaten the roads. They fly through South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, and onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

npc:thorvald-deepforge.text: Thorvald Deepforge. At the Valley of Kings, Thorvald Deepforge arms travelers bound for Loch Modan. He helps defend the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Thorvald Deepforge supplies weapons at the Valley of Kings. Troggs and roaming wildlife threaten the mountain passes between Khaz Modan's interior and its outlying lands. Travelers from Dun Morogh and those heading deeper into Loch Modan can find blades and axes here to defend dwarven lands.

npc:thran-khorman.text: Thran Khorman. At Anvilmar, Thran Khorman trains new warriors for the dangers of Coldridge Valley. Thran Khorman drills dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes on the grounds of Anvilmar. Gruff and demanding, he has little patience for anyone who lacks the grit for front-line fighting. Though the Third War has ended, troggs press into Coldridge Pass, and danger still fills the mountains. Thran insists on relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield so Ironforge’s defenders stay ready.

npc:thunderaan.text: Thunderaan. Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Adventurers who recover these relics can seek out Highlord Demitrian in Silithus to unleash him once more. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. The Prince was ambushed and betrayed by Ragnaros's powerful lieutenants, Baron Geddon and Garr, before being struck down by the Firelord's hammer, Sulfuras. Although defeated, Thunderaan's essence proved too mighty for Ragnaros to fully absorb. Unable to entirely devour the Prince of Air, Ragnaros sealed what little remained of Thunderaan's essence inside a talisman of elemental binding. To prevent the Prince from ever reforming, the Firelord shattered the talisman into two flawless halves. He entrusted one piece to Baron Geddon and the other to Garr, hiding both within the volcanic depths of the Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.

npc:tommy-joe-stonefield.text: Tommy Joe Stonefield. At the river west of Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield longs for Maybell Maclure. Their families have feuded for years, so he relies on secret notes and quiet banks to keep their love hidden. Tommy Joe Stonefield waits by the river west of Stonefield Farm, looking toward the Maclure homestead across the water. The Stonefields and Maclures have clashed for years over land, pride, and farmyard squabbles. Their elders keep the feud alive, but Tommy Joe has fallen in love with Maybell Maclure. The two cannot meet openly without angering both households. Gramma Stonefield, Tommy Joe’s sympathetic grandmother, helps them exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

npc:tormus-deepforge.text: Tormus Deepforge. At Ironforge's Great Forge, Tormus Deepforge keeps weapons flowing to the Alliance. He coordinates iron deliveries and arms defenses across Khaz Modan and beyond. Tormus Deepforge oversees the Bronzebeard clan's metalwork beside the Great Forge fires. He still hammers steel himself, but he also mourns Sturgy Ironband, his mentor. Dark Iron dwarves overran Sturgy's smithing compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh after a load of strange umbral ore arrived there.

npc:torwa-pathfinder.text: Torwa Pathfinder. Torwa Pathfinder is a lone tauren hunter and tracker camped at the entrance to Un'Goro Crater, just below the ramp descending from Tanaris. He observes the basin's primordial wildlife, studying the dangerous predators that rule the jungle floor. Adventurers seeking to test their mettle against the crater's legendary beasts often seek his guidance. Perched at the eastern base of the crater where the desert sands of Tanaris give way to humid jungle steam, Torwa Pathfinder serves as an informal warden for newcomers. He respects the wild forces of Un'Goro, understanding that careless wanderers quickly become fodder for the local fauna. His campsite provides a rare moment of respite before travelers dive into the sweltering depths. Much of Torwa's attention is consumed by Lar'korwi, a notoriously cunning and fierce raptor roaming the northern reaches of the crater. Torwa understands that brute strength alone cannot bring down such an apex predator. Instead, he instructs hunters to study its feeding habits, using fresh carcase meat and glands to craft a bait potent enough to lure the beast out into the open. Beyond hunting the crater's apex raptors, Torwa maintains a deep curiosity regarding the toxic flora and aggressive ape colonies that inhabit the basin. He directs travelers to harvest venom from volatile bloodpetals and observe the strength of dominant beasts like the mighty gorilla U'cha, constantly analyzing how nature's deadliest adaptations function in isolation.

npc:treshala-fallowbrook.text: Treshala Fallowbrook. In Darnassus, Treshala Fallowbrook waits at home for news of her husband. Heralath Fallowbrook has gone far away, into Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. On the second floor of a Tradesmen's Terrace workshop, Treshala Fallowbrook waits for word from her husband. Heralath journeyed to Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens, where thorny growth surrounds the quilboar's warrens. Their marriage is marked by a pendant of bonding, which Heralath carried with him.

npc:tsunaman.text: Tsunaman. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tsunaman watches the currents of Kalimdor for signs of unrest. He works with the Horde against forces that threaten the waters. Near the path from Sun Rock Retreat down to the Charred Vale, Tsunaman serves the Tribunal of the Tides, high-ranking servants aligned with the Tidehunter, Neptulon. He works with the Horde to watch for elemental unrest throughout Kalimdor, especially disturbances spreading from the submerged caverns of Blackfathom Deeps. Tsunaman hates fire in every form. The burning lands of the Charred Vale and incursions by fire elementals keep him fuming. Around camp, he sometimes marches to nearby cooking fires and campfires and smacks them out with a heavy fist of water.

npc:tyrion.text: Tyrion. Inside Stormwind Keep, Tyrion watches the court and aids covert work. The gnome works with Elling Trias to gather intelligence and counter plots against the kingdom. Tyrion keeps to the halls of Stormwind Keep, watching the palace and staying in touch with contacts beyond official oversight. Elling Trias, a cheese merchant in the Trade District, trusts Tyrion with sensitive matters. Trias runs a discreet information network and sends reliable operatives to Tyrion when the House of Nobles' bureaucracy must be bypassed.

npc:ukor.text: Ukor. Near the eastern path outside the Valley of Trials, Ukor rests after carrying supplies from Razor Hill. The training grounds already had plenty, and he hopes the provisions can still help his people. Ukor rests by the eastern road outside the Valley of Trials, tired from carrying food south from Razor Hill. Orc peons often spend their days cutting lumber or hauling rocks under harsh taskmasters. Ukor chose to bring provisions to the recruits on his own initiative. He crossed Durotar's red plains, where scorpids and boars prowl, only to find the training grounds already well-stocked. His bundle was not needed. Now he asks passing young adventurers to carry the provisions back north to Innkeeper Grosk.

npc:ula-elek.text: Ula'elek. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek works armor for warriors across the Horde. The Darkspear smith joins forces with Thun'grim Firegaze, shaping specialized gear from traditional troll craft and trophies gathered across Kalimdor. Ula'elek is a skilled armorsmith serving the Darkspear in Sen'jin Village. Nearby quilboar and sea crawlers threaten the coastal settlement, so the tribe needs sturdy armor and working blades. Ula'elek's skill also draws seasoned warriors from across the Horde. Young warriors who visit Thun'grim Firegaze at his overlook in the Barrens are sent south to Sen'jin Village. The veteran trusts Ula'elek to forge Brutal Gauntlets for battle-hardened fighters. To make them, Ula'elek calls for rare materials, especially swollen, uncloven hooves from the satyrs draining the forest's magic in northeastern Ashenvale.

npc:umpi.text: Umpi. In Tarren Mill, Umpi endures Apothecary Lydon's experiments. The frog is kept in the Royal Apothecary Society's workshop as a test subject for toxins and plague brews. Umpi is a frog in Tarren Mill who bears the cost of Apothecary Lydon's experiments. For Lydon, testing his formulas requires living flesh, and he gives Umpi lethal brews such as the Elixir of Suffering and the Elixir of Agony. The poisons kill her, but Lydon re-animates her so she can face another dose for the Royal Apothecary Society.

npc:undertaker-mordo.text: Undertaker Mordo. At Deathknell's crypt, Undertaker Mordo greets newly awakened Forsaken. He tells them they are free of the Lich King's control and sends them toward Queen Sylvanas's cause. Bodies that never stir go to the fire. Undertaker Mordo tends the crypt in Tirisfal Glades as corpses break free of the Scourge. Newly awakened Forsaken find him in a world they no longer recognize. He tests their sanity, tells them what they have become, and directs them toward service under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. Some bodies brought to the crypt never wake. Mordo soon casts them into the fire. Those who stir meet his dry impatience and little ceremony. If they have kept their wits, he sends them up the steps and down the road to Shadow Priest Sarvis at the chapel, where Sarvis explains their new existence. The mindless zombies overrunning the north of the village are Sarvis's concern. He sends the newly risen to destroy them.

npc:ur-kyo.text: Ur'kyo. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo guides priests in the ways of shadow and light. The Darkspear regard him as their spiritual leader and greatest priest, and he teaches their traditions in the Horde capital. Ur'kyo guides Darkspear mystics and visiting practitioners from the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. After fleeing the Echo Isles, the Darkspear made a home in Durotar alongside Thrall's Horde. Their sacred traditions remain vital to the tribe, and Ur'kyo keeps those ancestral practices alive through his teaching. Priests who come to Ur'kyo find a patient instructor in faith and old rites. He teaches the Hex of Weakness and the defensive ward called Shadowguard. Horde priests also turn to him to learn about the coalition's varied spiritual ways, from troll voodoo and ancestral customs to foreign disciplines.

npc:uzzek.text: Uzzek. Uzzek watches the eastern Barrens from southwest of Far Watch Post. The battle-hardened orc survived many skirmishes across Kalimdor and now tests and trains promising Horde warriors crossing the plains. Uzzek trains young warriors southwest of Far Watch Post, near the eastern edge of the Barrens. He endured brutal combat in the recent wars and now tests those learning to defend themselves. To prove their skill, they face the savage wildlife and raiders that trouble the crossing.

npc:valstag-ironjaw.text: Valstag Ironjaw. At Menethil Keep, Valstag Ironjaw helps guard the routes between Loch Modan and the coast. He keeps the garrison informed of dangers along the trade passages. Valstag Ironjaw serves with the dwarven garrison inside Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor. The marsh around the keep is dangerous, with Dragonmaw orcs and ravenous wildlife threatening communications and supplies. Valstag helps coordinate defenses along the main roads, especially the perilous passage through Dun Algaz toward Loch Modan. Hostile forces crowd the Algaz Gauntlet, putting travelers and supply convoys between Menethil Harbor and Loch Modan at risk. Valstag sends capable adventurers against the brigands and orcs in the passes. He carries military reports between forward scouts and commanders such as Captain Stoutfist.

npc:vanndar-stormpike.text: Vanndar Stormpike. At Dun Baldar, Vanndar Stormpike leads the Stormpike Expedition into Alterac Valley. He searches its frozen peaks for ancient relics and raw resources, waging an unyielding Alliance war against the Frostwolf orcs. Vanndar Stormpike leads the dwarven excavation into Alterac Valley as a veteran mountain king of Ironforge. After the Third War, he marched the Stormpike Guard into the northern mountains to seek hidden mineral riches and long-lost titan artifacts. He made Dun Baldar his fortified base, claiming the valley as ancestral ground and rightful Alliance territory. From there, he directs military outposts, defensive bunkers, and frontline pushes. Vanndar is determined that no retreat will ever be sounded under his watch. Vanndar's mining and prospecting reached into the Frostwolf clan's home, starting a brutal mountain war. The orcs demanded that he withdraw, but he refused to yield an inch, vowing Alterac Valley would belong to the dwarves. From his throne room deep within Dun Baldar, with marshals and bodyguards at his side, Vanndar oversees the defense against Frostwolf incursions. He also sends Alliance champions to break enemy lines and claim the valley.

npc:varok-saurfang.text: Varok Saurfang. In Orgrimmar, Varok Saurfang commands the Horde's war forces under Warchief Thrall. The veteran of the Old Horde's wars lends the young Horde his strength and experience. Varok Saurfang carries the Old Horde's wars into the present. Few living warriors match his record, and many regard him as unstoppable in battle. Now High Overlord in Orgrimmar, he helps hold together Thrall's newborn Horde. Varok Saurfang defends the Horde and enforces Thrall's rule against threats. He does not seek battle for its own sake. He despises warmongering and fights for honor and the Horde's preservation.

npc:velarok.text: Velarok. Velarok Windblade is a lone human swordsman camped amid the ash and cinder of Searing Gorge, flanked by the mutilated corpses of Dark Iron dwarves. He seeks vengeance against the local Dark Irons for the brutal murder of his father, recruiting passing travelers to forge a weapon of retribution. His single-minded hunger for vengeance drives everything he asks of those who help him. Found southeast of Thorium Point, Velarok Windblade presents himself as a grieving human warrior stranded in the perilous wastes of the Searing Gorge. Surrounding his camp are the bloody, battered corpses of Dark Iron dwarves who crossed his blade. According to Velarok, these clan dwarves slaughtered his father in cold blood. Consumed by hatred, he enlists travelers to gather materials to assemble the Torch of Retribution, an enchanted weapon of vengeance against the Dark Irons and the minions of Ragnaros.

npc:velora-nitely.text: Velora Nitely. In the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Velora Nitely works the forge for the Forsaken and the Horde. Once among Lordaeron's finest armorsmiths, she now makes dry jokes that rarely land. Velora Nitely works near the anvils in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where she makes armor for the Horde. Before the Third War devastated the north, Lordaeron celebrated her as an exceptional armorsmith. Undeath took her life and warmth, but left her technical skill untouched. She works with Horde crafters across continents, including Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens. Her craft includes reinforcing heavy battle plate and forging the formidable Brutal Legguards from hardened materials such as Dragonmaw shinbones. Velora Nitely keeps trying to make jokes at the forge, though her humor rarely lands. Many of her somber Forsaken kin brood over their cursed fate, but she still makes room for levity. Death seems to have ruined her comedic timing: her quips sound flat, morbid, and thoroughly unfunny to the living and the dead alike. She keeps cracking them undeterred.

npc:ventaari-brightwish.text: Ventaari Brightwish. Ventaari Brightwish is a Skyborne resident of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. She greets travelers from across Azeroth and offers the quest The Gift of Skysight. Residing in Thendal Village upon the soaring cliffs of Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish is one of the local Skyborne. While she shares a surname with Belathaan Brightwish, her own duties center around aiding newcomers who find their way to the village, extending hospitality to both the Alliance and the Horde as she initiates visitors into the traditions of her people through tasks like The Gift of Skysight.

npc:verna-furlbrow.text: Verna Furlbrow. Verna Furlbrow waits beside her broken wagon near Westfall’s northern border. Bandits drove her from her family’s pumpkin patch, and the road to Elwynn Forest has left her stranded. Verna and her husband farmed pumpkins in northern Westfall until lawlessness drove them from their land. After outlaws took the farm, they loaded what they could onto their cart and set out for Elwynn Forest with their horse, Old Blanchy. Their wagon broke down just down the road from the abandoned Jansen Stead. Unable to repair the axle or continue, Verna now faces the elements, bandit raids, and scavengers. She depends on travelers to keep her household fed and guarded. Verna still welcomes those who have been driven to the roadside. Known for creating Westfall Stew, she shares meals and warm fires with wandering transients and refugees who have suffered similar fates. To fill her cooking pot, she needs ingredients gathered from the fields, including boar snouts, murloc eyes, okra, and stringy vulture meat. She makes hearty meals for the destitute from what the harsh frontier provides.

npc:veron-amberstill.text: Veron Amberstill. At Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill tends the rams Ironforge riders trust. Veron Amberstill breeds and trains mountain rams at Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh. Their sure footing and thick coats suit the steep slopes and mountain blizzards of Khaz Modan. He raises them to carry dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. Veron offers standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves. Riders from other peoples must prove loyalty to Ironforge's throne before he parts with a ram.

npc:veronica-nials.text: Veronica Nials. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Veronica Nials directs Stromgarde's defense as her kingdom crumbles. She faces Syndicate treachery and Boulderfist ogres in the Arathi Highlands. After the Third War, Stromgarde shattered, and its people faced invading Boulderfist ogres and the Syndicate's treachery. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Veronica Nials commands the surviving Stromgarde defenders. She directs Alliance champions against Syndicate leaders, including Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl. She also seeks the badges of fallen soldiers so their grieving families can learn what became of them. When Rhag Garmason and the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr asked Stromgarde for help, Captain Nials had to refuse. Dark Iron saboteurs had devastated the Thandol Span, but her troops could not spare a single blade beyond the Arathi Highlands. Honor and duty bound them to defend their homeland while Stromgarde remained occupied.

npc:vesprystus.text: Vesprystus. At Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus sends travelers between Teldrassil and mainland Kalimdor. He tends the hippogryph roost at the great World Tree's base. At Teldrassil's southern base, Vesprystus tends the Rut'theran roost. Trained hippogryphs carry travelers from the isolated elven boughs toward Darkshore and the mainland. A magical portal also links Rut'theran to Darnassus in the canopy above. Across the strait, Vesprystus works with the flight master at Auberdine to carry sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers into Kalimdor.

npc:vidra-hearthstove.text: Vidra Hearthstove. In Thelsamar, Vidra Hearthstove cooks local specialties at the Stoutlager Inn. She often relies on traveling adventurers to gather ingredients for her famous blood sausages. Vidra Hearthstove cooks for locals and travelers at the Stoutlager Inn in Loch Modan. Sharing a surname with the innkeeper, she helps keep Thelsamar well provisioned. Her signature dish, Thelsamar blood sausages, calls for fresh game from the surrounding wilderness: boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

npc:volcor.text: Volcor. Volcor lies wounded in Blackwood Den, deep in southern Darkshore. The night elf scout depends on his bear Grimclaw and Auberdine's defenders to escape the hostile furbolgs. Volcor is a night elf scout wounded inside Blackwood Den. While tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe through its underground lair, he was ambushed and badly hurt. He could not fight past the hostile furbolgs alone, so he sent Grimclaw, his loyal bear companion, into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help in Auberdine.

npc:vorn-skyseer.text: Vorn Skyseer. At Camp Narache, Vorn Skyseer welcomes young tauren beginning their journeys. He lives among the tents on Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore and introduces newcomers to camp life. At Camp Narache, Vorn Skyseer greets young tauren beginning their rites of passage. They prepare to leave Red Cloud Mesa for the wider valleys of Mulgore, and his kind words and welcome help them settle into camp. Vorn Skyseer leaves the camp's defense to its braves. He lives quietly and without hurry, watching over the plains of his homeland.

npc:warcaller-gorlach.text: Warcaller Gorlach. Warcaller Gorlach patrols Orgrimmar, calling Horde champions to distant battlefronts. He rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands at outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Warcaller Gorlach walks Orgrimmar's thoroughfares, carrying the Horde's calls for expansion and defense. He gives orders among the city's people, seeking volunteers ready to test their mettle. Some he sends to the contested canopy of Ashenvale. Others he directs toward Camp Mojache in Feralas, where scouts face the wilderness. He also calls warriors to distant campaigns in the Plaguelands. As threats rise abroad, Gorlach calls on those in the capital to take up arms.

npc:warlord-goretooth.text: Warlord Goretooth. Warlord Goretooth is the commanding orc officer stationed at Kargath in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. From his watchtower, he coordinates the Horde's frontier campaigns against the neighboring Dark Iron dwarves and monitors the volcanic menace of Blackrock Mountain. Though strict in military matters, he can occasionally be found relaxing around the camp's bonfire. Perched atop the watchtower of Kargath, Warlord Lunk Goretooth directs Horde operations on the hostile eastern frontier. Kargath serves as Orgrimmar's primary staging ground against the threats lurking within Blackrock Mountain and the surrounding ravines. Goretooth oversees patrols, coordinates scout forces like the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and issues direct kill orders targeting the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leadership. When he descends from his lookout, the stern commander shows a lighter side, frequently warming himself by the camp bonfire and trading quips with the camp's Forsaken casters before returning to duty. Goretooth views the Dark Iron dwarves as a clear and present threat to Horde interests in the Eastern Kingdoms. Rather than engaging in defensive posturing, he pursues aggressive war plans against General Angerforge and Emperor Dagran Thaurissan's forces entrenched within Blackrock Depths. Recognizing the gravity of assaulting such an ancient subterranean stronghold, he frequently defers strategic matters to veteran orcs like Eitrigg in Orgrimmar, seeking seasoned wisdom before sanctioning further pushes into the mountain.

npc:warmaster-laggrond.text: Warmaster Laggrond. Outside Alterac Valley, Warmaster Laggrond prepares Horde fighters for the Frostwolf clan. He commands from the valley’s entrance in the Alterac Mountains, where warriors answer the call to aid the Frostwolves. Warmaster Laggrond directs the Horde's fight against the Stormpike Expedition at Alterac Valley's entrance. In the bitter cold, he admits only capable fighters to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde. Warmaster Laggrond sends arriving combatants through the Proving Grounds before they enter battle. As warriors fight across the frozen peaks, he measures their standing and honors those who earn renown among the Frostwolves.

npc:warsong-outrider.text: Warsong Outrider. On the road east from Ashenvale, the Warsong Outrider watches the Horde's frontier. She scouts for the Warsong clan, watches travelers, and sends intelligence to its forward encampments. She keeps watch unless someone provokes her. The Warsong Outrider watches the road between Ashenvale and Azshara's shattered ruins. Far from Splintertree Post and the lumber camps, she tracks troop movements along the route. Her bow and toxic stingers are ready, but she fires only at Alliance trespassers who attack her.

npc:watch-captain-parker.text: Watch Captain Parker. At Three Corners, Watch Captain Parker guards the road and travelers bound for Lakeshire. He patrols the junction and watches the gnoll packs gathering nearby, an early line of defense for those heading into town. At Three Corners, Watch Captain Parker watches the roads between Elwynn Forest, Duskwood, and Redridge. Stormwind has few troops to spare, and little official help reaches the region. Parker and other lone watchmen must keep the crossroads clear of bandits, prowling predators, and raiding gnolls. Gnoll camps gathering north and east of Parker’s post draw his attention. As the packs press closer to the road, he sends able-bodied travelers to warn Deputy Feldon in Lakeshire. The Redridge gnolls grow bolder, threatening supply convoys and refugees seeking shelter in town. A lonely roadside post can be grim, yet kindness reaches Three Corners. Darcy, a server at the Lakeshire Inn, sends Parker a warm lunch while he patrols. Touched by her kindness, Parker asks the traveler who brought it to fetch a bouquet from Lakeshire’s herbalist and take it back to Darcy. He asks that the herbalist not be told who the flowers are from or for.

npc:watcher-backus.text: Watcher Backus. Along Duskwood's road, Watcher Backus keeps watch for danger and suspicious traffic tied to Stormwind's political intrigues. He patrols between Darkshire and Manor Mistmantle, watching for undead and strange travelers. Watcher Backus walks a solitary beat north of Darkshire, passing near Manor Mistmantle. Like the rest of the Night Watch, he struggles against Duskwood's curse. Stormwind's garrison gives the region little support, so local volunteers guard its misty paths on their own. Backus keeps beast and ghoul at bay along the road.

npc:watcher-dodds.text: Watcher Dodds. At Duskwood's central crossroads, Watcher Dodds keeps watch for the Night Watch. From his roadside outpost, he watches for danger and asks travelers to thin the giant spider population. Watcher Dodds guards the crossroads for the Night Watch, under Commander Althea Ebonlocke. His post stands where the roads from Darkshire, Raven Hill, and Deadwind Pass meet. Darkshire's palisades shelter the town, but Dodds keeps watch beyond them, amid wolf packs, ravenous ghouls, and oversized spiders. From his roadside camp, he watches for threats and asks passing mercenaries to kill spiders emerging from the undergrowth before they overrun the roads.

npc:wilder-thistlenettle.text: Wilder Thistlenettle. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, Wilder Thistlenettle drinks alone with old grief. He once entered Moonbrook’s Deadmines with his brother and their mining crew, but a cave-in left him the sole survivor. Wilder Thistlenettle drinks away his sorrow in an alehouse near the Dwarven District’s southeastern gates. Years ago, he joined his brother and their companions in the deep lodes of Moonbrook’s Deadmines. A cave-in sealed the rest of the crew underground, and Wilder barely reached the surface alive.

npc:wiley-the-black.text: Wiley the Black. At the Lakeshire Inn, Wiley the Black keeps out of sight. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle and shares what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood. Wiley the Black keeps to the Lakeshire Inn, away from Westfall's turmoil and Redridge's gnoll-infested borders. He owes his life to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia, who once saved him. Stoutmantle grumbles that he should have let Wiley rot.
