When the militia needs insight into the Defias conspiracy, it turns to Wiley. He reluctantly shares covert intelligence to repay his debt.

npc:willem.text: Willem. Outside Northshire Abbey, Willem sends recruits to meet the valley's threats. He serves under Marshal McBride in the Stormwind Army, with the Defias Brotherhood pressing into Northshire. Deputy Willem watches the gates of Northshire Abbey, where the Stormwind Army keeps a foothold in the valley. The kingdom's soldiers are spread across many territories, leaving local defense to small groups like Marshal McBride's garrison. Willem meets incoming volunteers and sends them to aid residents and guard the valley's edges. The Defias Brotherhood is Willem's most pressing concern. Red-bandana bandits have entered Northshire, stolen supplies, threatened farmer Milly Osworth, and taken footholds among nearby vineyards and hills. Willem offers bounties on known cutthroats such as Garrick Padfoot, hoping to break their leadership before they can take the abbey grounds.

npc:williden-marshal.text: Williden Marshal. Williden Marshal is the ambitious human leader of Marshal's Expedition, based out of Marshal's Refuge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Driven by the lure of rare flora, mysterious crystals, and profitable scientific research, he brought his team into the crater only to watch their lower camps overrun by the basin's colossal beasts. Williden Marshal brought an entire scientific expedition deep into Un'Goro Crater seeking fortune and discovery. Intrigued by accounts of alien crystals, uncataloged plants, and untapped resources, he established multiple forward camps across the valley floor. However, the primeval wilderness quickly turned against them. The savage beasts of the crater dismantled their research posts, forcing Williden and his survivors to retreat up into the northern cliffs to establish Marshal's Refuge. Despite being driven to the crater's mountainous edge, Williden refuses to pack up and abandon his investment. From the relative safety of the refuge, he hires passing adventurers to delve back into the savage lowlands to recover lost food crates, expensive scientific instruments, and his personal expedition journal. Though often known simply as 'Wil' to close comrades like Spark Nilminer, he takes the venture seriously—insisting on recovering their work even as titanic predators stalk the valley beneath them. Williden is not the only Marshal in the crater: Hol'anyee Marshal shares his name and works alongside him at Marshal's Refuge. Together they chose the untamed primeval crater of southern Kalimdor, and Williden remains entirely convinced that Un'Goro's crystal deposits and ancient mysteries hold the true fortune.

npc:winna-hazzard.text: Winna Hazzard. Winna Hazzard is an eccentric Forsaken researcher stationed at Bloodvenom Post in Felwood. Accompanied by a feline companion and known for bouts of maniacal laughter, she studies the blighted ecosystem and conducts unsettling experiments with the zone's corrupted fauna. Winna Hazzard represents the Forsaken interest in Felwood's unnatural decay. Stationed in the Horde enclave of Bloodvenom Post, she spends her time observing the local wildlife and formulating experiments utilizing tainted waters and venomous samples. Her jovial, manic demeanor often masks callous motives, evident when she uses tainted liquids drawn from the land to corrupt the small kitten that stays by her side.

npc:winstone-wolfe.text: Winstone Wolfe. At Ravenholdt Manor, Winstone Wolfe keeps watch over the estate grounds. The human operative belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's secretive organization, hidden between Hillsbrad and the Alterac Mountains. Winstone Wolfe works among Lord Jorach Ravenholdt's syndicate at Ravenholdt Manor. Quiet and watchful, he handles business around the manor and watches its grounds and groundskeepers. Only those with discretion and talent walk there undisturbed.

npc:witch-doctor-jin-zil.text: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. In Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil turns dark voodoo against the Horde's enemies. The Darkspear troll mystic lives in a cave in the southern Stonetalon Mountains and is a longtime comrade of Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan. In a cave east of Malaka'jin, Jin'Zil practices the ancient arts of jungle trolls, far from his tribe's coastal home. Bubbling cauldrons and captive prisoners fill his cavern. He gathers exotic reagents from the Stonetalon crags, weaving blessings and curses to defend the Horde's mountain camp. Jin'Zil is an old friend of senior Horde scouts Darsok Swiftdagger and the shadow hunter Rokhan. Darsok leads frontline skirmishes against night elves and harpies. Jin'Zil fights the war through spirit and alchemy, using forest magic and volatile voodoo to weaken threats before they reach the camp gates.

npc:witch-doctor-uzer-i.text: Witch Doctor Uzer'i. Witch Doctor Uzer'i is a jungle troll mystic residing at Camp Mojache in the primordial forests of Feralas. Dedicated to advancing the magical capabilities of the Horde, he researches techniques to trap and harness the muisek—the spiritual essence of powerful natural creatures. By capturing these ancient forest spirits, Uzer'i seeks to channel the raw primal energies traditionally favored by night elves directly into enchanted weapons. Rooted in traditional troll spiritualism, Witch Doctor Uzer'i has spent considerable effort studying the natural magic inherent to the untamed wilderness of Feralas. He argues that night elves have drawn upon the spirits of forest beasts for millennia, and believes the time has come for the Horde to seize those same primal forces. Central to his study is the concept of muisek: the vibrant spiritual essence that remains within a creature. To harness it, Uzer'i crafts specialized vessels capable of rapidly shrinking fallen beings before their escaping spirit disperses, allowing the essence to be stored and studied. Extracting muisek was merely the first phase of Uzer'i's broader ambition. Gathering resilient sinew, enchanted minerals, and petrified splintered logs from the very creatures whose spirits he trapped, the witch doctor fused physical materials with bound muisek. Through these rites, he learned to permanently bind ancient forest spirits into arms and armaments, providing the Horde with magically charged weapons. Beyond his ritual craftsmanship, Uzer'i maintains a deep curiosity regarding hidden places of power throughout Azeroth, actively tracking rumors of the ancient, submerged Sunken Temple.

npc:wizlo-bearingshiner.text: Wizlo Bearingshiner. Wizlo Bearingshiner is a goblin tinkerer stranded at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. The sole survivor of a centaur attack on his caravan, he recruits travelers to recover a valuable Hypercapacitor Gizmo from the wreckage. Staying alongside the tauren at Whitereach Post along the canyon road, Wizlo Bearingshiner faces an unwelcome delay. Centaur attacked his caravan, leaving him as its only survivor. His clients are waiting for their wares, and he worries that he will not deliver them in time. Wizlo's best gizmo hangs around the neck of a fierce panther caged beside his ruined caravan north of Whitereach Post. Even the centaur avoid the beast. Wizlo offers travelers the cage key and a reward for recovering the hypercapacitor, though he admits he has yet to work out what the device actually does.

npc:wizzle-brassbolts.text: Wizzle Brassbolts. Wizzle Brassbolts is a gnome engineer stationed alongside his fellow tinkerers out on the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Working with the gnomish racing team at the Mirage Raceway, he seeks durable local materials to reinforce their experimental rocket cars. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnomish and goblin engineering takes the form of high-speed rocket car races. Wizzle Brassbolts works as part of the gnomish raceway crew, striving to keep their vehicles intact against blistering speeds and abrasive salt. To bolster their machines, he recruits adventurers to hunt the local wildlife—such as the sturdy turtles wandering the basin—harvesting their hard shells to build new fuel tanks strong enough to hold his brother's corrosive new rocket fuel. Wizzle maintains close ties with friends across the continents, including Pilot Longbeard, who sends couriers out with racing helmets for the brothers. With help like that, Wizzle keeps the gnomish team supplied despite their remote, inhospitable testing ground on the Shimmering Flats.

npc:wizzlecrank-s-shredder.text: Wizzlecrank's Shredder. In Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank's Shredder sits trapped among Venture Company operators. Pilot Wizzlecrank climbed inside the machine to steal it, but it will not move without a key. Its engine must be started before the goblin can try to escape. Deep in Sludge Fen, Wizzlecrank waits inside a motionless shredder. The Venture Company machine is surrounded by hostile mercenaries in the polluted basin. Wizzlecrank climbed aboard to steal it, then learned he needed a key to unlock its movement column. When another shredder operator asked if all was well, he panicked and blamed a mechanical problem. Now he remains sealed inside, with guards and overseers nearby, hoping someone will fetch the key before the Venture Company grows suspicious.

npc:wrenix-the-wretched.text: Wrenix the Wretched. Beside his strange apparatus in Ratchet, Wrenix the Wretched helps crack tough locks. The goblin tinker offers tools to open secure caches. Wrenix the Wretched works beside his machinery in Ratchet, the goblin port on the Barrens coast. As a tinker of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he knows mechanisms and contraptions, and how to bypass locks and salvage what lies beyond them. Rogues and scouts working the coast can turn to him for help. Wrenix keeps his gizmotronic apparatus close at hand. He uses it and his mechanical skill to supply thieves' tools and lock-picking instruments. Those seeking to recover stolen Southsea pirate contraband along the Merchant Coast can put them to use.

npc:wynne-larson.text: Wynne Larson. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson supplies mages across the kingdom with robes. Human clothier Wynne relies on local craftsmen since Dalaran and Quel'Thalas fell in the Third War, and points spellcasters toward rare materials for enchanted garments. Before the Third War, Dalaran and Quel'Thalas supplied the finest woven fabrics and enchanted vestments. Their destruction crippled the old trade routes and arcane textile production. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Wynne Larson now works with local tailors and enchanters such as Lucan Cordell. Together, they meet the city's growing demand for robes and spellwoven gear. Novice and journeyman mages seeking arcane garments come to Wynne's shop. She knows what materials are needed for vestments such as Manaweave Robes and Astral Knot Garments. To find those materials, she sends arcane practitioners into dangerous places to recover rare reagents like pristine spider silk. Her work helps keep Stormwind's mages outfitted despite shortages from the north.

npc:xavathras.text: Xavathras. Xavathras is a vicious satyr commander residing among the tents at the Ruins of Constellas in Felwood. Leading a band of Jadefire satyrs, he oversees the corruption of an ancient moonwell in service to his master, Xavaric. Within the tainted glades of Felwood, the Ruins of Constellas have fallen into the clutches of the Jadefire satyrs. Stationed in an encampment pitched amidst the elven stonework, Xavathras directs the defilement of a nearby moonwell on behalf of another cruel satyr, Xavaric. By poisoning the pure waters with demonic energy, Xavathras deepens the corruption that grips the forest. His presence poses a direct threat to any attempts to restore the woodland, earning the ire of night elves like Eridan Bluewind who mark him for death.

npc:yeh-kinya.text: Yeh'kinya. Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll scholar residing at Steamwheedle Port on the desert coast of Tanaris. Claiming to seek ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers, he dispatches willing adventurers across Azeroth on missions to gather lost troll relics. Lounging among the goblins and dockworkers of Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya presents himself as a quiet student of history and spirits. He recruits travelers to track down obscure magical items across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, from ancient eggs in the Hinterlands to stone prophecy tablets buried in the ruins of Zul'Farrak. While he claims these errands serve peaceful academic inquiry into ancient troll history, his specific focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion from watchful onlookers.

npc:yvette-farthing.text: Yvette Farthing. In Brill, Yvette Farthing shares the Gallows' End Tavern with her father, Coleman. A Forsaken, she carries the memory of a love cut short by the Scourge. Yvette loved Thurman Agamand, heir to the prosperous Agamand Mills, before the Third War ruined Lordaeron. As the Scourge plague drew near, Yvette and her father, Coleman, begged Thurman to leave the estate with them. He refused, devoted to his family's legacy. Yvette and Thurman both perished and rose into undeath. Yvette found a place among the free-willed Forsaken in Brill, but she did not know Thurman's final fate.

npc:zaldimar-wefhellt.text: Zaldimar Wefhellt. On Goldshire's upper floor, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches young mages their first spells. When they outgrow his lessons, he sends them to Stormwind City for further training. Upstairs at the Lion's Pride Inn, Zaldimar Wefhellt teaches novice mages the first arts of arcane, fire, and frost. When an apprentice outgrows those lessons, he sends them north to the Mage Quarter in Stormwind, where Jennea Cannon can teach them more.

npc:zamja.text: Zamja. In Orgrimmar’s Drag, Zamja teaches Horde travelers to cook. The Darkspear troll trains cooks to make meals from beasts of Kalimdor. Zamja works in the Drag, where she cuts meat and teaches Horde travelers to cook. Cooking helps travelers in the rugged lands of Durotar and the Barrens turn raw game into rations. Cooks who have mastered basic recipes can seek further training in Gadgetzan, to the south.

npc:zangen-stonehoof.text: Zangen Stonehoof. At the High Rise bonfire, Zangen Stonehoof tends the flames and aids tauren kin across Kalimdor. Each evening, he keeps the central fire burning in Thunder Bluff. Zangen Stonehoof tends the communal bonfire atop Thunder Bluff's High Rise. Each evening, as twilight falls over Mulgore, he lights the fire above the city's highest bluffs. The flames give warmth to the tribes gathered beneath High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. Zangen also keeps ties with allies beyond Mulgore's mesa, helping with spiritual and ritual work across the continent. Zangen helps Rau Cliffrunner, who is stationed south in Thousand Needles. When Rau needed water from a night elf moonwell for sacred rituals, Zangen enlisted dependable Horde adventurers to cross the contested forests of Ashenvale. They secured a filled phial from the ancient groves and sent it south to Freewind Post. Zangen helps preserve ancient rites and support scattered tauren posts.

npc:zankaja.text: Zankaja. In Orgrimmar, young orc woman Zankaja waits anxiously for word of her mate, Dogran. He was assigned to duty at the Crossroads, along the dangerous frontier of the Barrens. Zankaja waits for news of Dogran, her mate, in Orgrimmar. Dogran earned a promotion and went south to bolster the outpost at the Crossroads in the Barrens. The assignment honors a warrior, but the frontier is harsh, with quilboar, centaur, and aggressive beasts. When Dogran failed to send word or return as expected, Zankaja began asking travelers to seek news of him.

npc:zardeth-of-the-black-claw.text: Zardeth of the Black Claw. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Zardeth of the Black Claw protects a hidden warlock cabal from scrutiny. He dwells in the chambers beneath the Slaughtered Lamb and poses as an ordinary patron. When curious nobles look too closely, he makes sure their inquiries end for good. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, tunnels shelter those who practice darker arts while the Mage Quarter's spires study arcane discipline in the open. Zardeth of the Black Claw works from these crypts, guarding warlocks who hide right beneath the city guard's nose. The Alliance condemns fel magic, so the cabal survives by keeping its presence secret and removing threats before royal investigators arrive.

npc:zargh.text: Zargh. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Zargh sells meat and sends choice cuts to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sells cured meat, shank, and game from the surrounding plains. Travelers heading into the wilderness can find provisions at his shop. He also sends choice cuts across Durotar to Innkeeper Gryshka in the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar.

npc:zarlman-two-moons.text: Zarlman Two-Moons. In central Mulgore, Zarlman Two-Moons guides Bloodhoof Village's spiritual life. While Baine Bloodhoof tends its daily affairs, Zarlman communes with the spirits and guides young tauren through the Rite of Vision. Zarlman Two-Moons tends the spirits while Baine Bloodhoof commands Bloodhoof Village's defenses and temporal needs. The village looks to Zarlman for harmony with the spirit world. He joins the plains' everyday struggles with the voices of ancestors and honors the Earth Mother and ancestral wisdom. Zarlman guides maturing tauren through the Rite of Vision, a traditional trial each must undertake. He teaches initiates to prepare sacred draughts and heed ancestral portents. Young hunters, shamans, and warriors seek their destined path and spirit guides through the rite. Zarlman teaches them that strength on the plains means little without spiritual clarity.

npc:zarrin.text: Zarrin. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin teaches the ways of Kaldorei cooking. He tends an open hearth on Teldrassil, where young night elves and visitors learn to prepare meals from the tree's native flora and fauna. Behind Dolanaar's inn, Zarrin tends an open cooking fire and teaches Kaldorei culinary arts. Teldrassil's native plants and animals provide food for those who live here. Zarrin shows visitors how to forage and prepare meals at home.

npc:zenn-foulhoof.text: Zenn Foulhoof. East of Dolanaar, Zenn Foulhoof asks travelers for forest reagents. The night elves watch him closely.

npc:zevrost.text: Zevrost. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Zevrost trains warlocks in fel magic. He guides Horde initiates through summoning rites and the handling of dark artifacts. In the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar, Zevrost is one of the chief mentors for Horde warlocks in Thrall’s capital. Orcs remain wary of fel magic after their past demonic corruption, so practitioners work under strict watch. Zevrost teaches the discipline needed to command demons without yielding to their corruption. He says fel ruins only those who lack inner strength. Zevrost guides warlocks beyond spells and curses, opening the way to greater dark undertakings. Initiates seeking advanced implements such as the Orb of Orahil, or the means to summon a fiery Felsteed, often come through his hands. He sends ambitious practitioners to other masters, including Menara Voidrender in the Barrens, so they can push their command of shadow magic to its limits.

npc:zjolnir.text: Zjolnir. In Sen'jin Village, Zjolnir raises raptors for Darkspear riders and trusted Horde champions. His trained mounts carry deep cultural pride for troll riders. Near Sen'jin Village's pens, Zjolnir raises the fierce raptors the Darkspear favor as mounts. Predatory and temperamental, they need an expert hand before they can be raised and saddled for war. Zjolnir freely gives these prized mounts to fellow trolls who have learned the riding arts. Other Horde members must first earn the Darkspear tribe's exalted trust before he will entrust them with one of his raptors.

npc:zor-lonetree.text: Zor Lonetree. At Grommash Hold, Zor Lonetree studies the Horde’s concerns beyond Durotar. His knowledge of Alliance politics helps the court judge foreign affairs across Kalimdor. Zor Lonetree watches beyond Durotar from Grommash Hold. A shrewd advisor to the Horde’s high leadership, he has an unusually keen understanding of human and Alliance politics. When foreign curiosities reach Orgrimmar, he studies them; when trouble stirs among the land’s spirits, he directs travelers toward it. He has examined noble jewelry recovered from human settlements and followed disturbances among the spirits of the Stonetalon Mountains, keeping the warchief’s court informed on both political and spiritual matters.

npc:zureetha-fargaze.text: Zureetha Fargaze. In the Valley of Trials, Zureetha Fargaze watches for threats to young Horde recruits. Alongside Foreman Thazz'ril in Durotar, she sends them to uncover and root out the Burning Blade cult hidden in the valley. Zureetha Fargaze watches for dangers beyond the work and discipline Foreman Thazz'ril oversees. The Burning Blade cult has secretly entered the Valley of Trials, corrupted lesser demons, and gathered strength in the nearby Burning Blade Coven. She sends untested adventurers to recover medallions from the cultists, confirm their presence, and disrupt their early efforts. Then she directs seasoned recruits farther into Durotar.

topic:agamaggan.text: Agamaggan. Agamaggan the Great Boar was one of the colossal Ancient Guardians who walked Azeroth in its earliest days. He fell ten thousand years ago fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients, and his sacrifice helped save Azeroth from ruin. Where his blood and body crashed into the earth, vast networks of thorny vines arose, creating the Razorfen and granting life and purpose to his descendants, the quilboar. Ten thousand years ago, during the War of the Ancients, the mighty demigod Agamaggan came forth to battle the Burning Legion. The colossal boar fought with terrifying ferocity, and though he ultimately fell in combat, his actions helped save Azeroth from ruin. Where Agamaggan collapsed in the southern Barrens, his colossal corpse reshaped the land. His spilled blood soaked into the soil, causing enormous, impenetrable brambles and thorny vines to burst upward from the dry earth. These tangled thickets became known as the Razorfen. The quilboar revere the site as their holiest ground, viewing the labyrinth of Razorfen Kraul as his resting body and Razorfen Downs as his gaping skull. Scattered throughout the Barrens are crystallized Blood Shards, believed to be the physical remnants of the demigod's spilled blood, pulsing with lingering primal energy that quilboar geomancers and shamans harness for power. Agamaggan is revered as the divine progenitor of all quilboar. They view the surrounding brambles not merely as homes, but as the living armor left behind by their creator to shelter them from hostile neighbors. Quilboar tribes believe their god's spirit watches over them, granting martial vigor to their warriors and earth magic to their geomancers. In turn, they aggressively defend the thorns against encroaching tauren, orcs, and centaur, convinced that their sacred duty is to guard the fallen body of the boar god who birthed them.

topic:alliance.text: Alliance. The Alliance is a grand coalition of mortal races bound by shared ideals of honor, duty, and the defense of order across Azeroth. Born out of the ashes of the northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its current heart beats in Stormwind City, united alongside the dwarves of Ironforge, the exiled gnomes, and the night elves of Kalimdor. The modern Alliance descends from the original Alliance of Lordaeron, founded when Sir Anduin Lothar led Stormwind refugees north during the Second War to unite the Seven Kingdoms, dwarves, and high elves against the Old Horde. While the Scourge and the Third War decimated the north—leaving Lordaeron in ruins and driving the survivors into scattered resistance—the restored Kingdom of Stormwind rose to fill the void. Today, Stormwind stands as the preeminent seat of human leadership, carrying the banners of honor and faith into a fractured world. The faction's backbone in the Eastern Kingdoms relies on the steadfast bond between humans and the dwarves of Ironforge under King Magni Bronzebeard. Alongside the dwarves reside the gnomes, driven from Gnomeregan by a devastating trogg uprising. Guided by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, the exiled gnomes lend their brilliant engineering to the Alliance war effort, believing the coalition's survival is paramount to ever reclaiming their irradiated home. Across the Great Sea, the reclusive night elves abandoned millennia of isolation after the Battle of Mount Hyjal. Reeling from the loss of their immortality and engaged in bitter territorial clashes against the Horde over logging in Ashenvale, the kaldorei allied with their newfound mortal companions. Though cultural friction remains—and some traditionalists decry the presence of humans and dwarves in ancient forests—the Alliance provides vital military and diplomatic cooperation to safeguard Kalimdor against demonic remnants and Horde expansion. Despite its outward strength, the Alliance is beset by internal strain. King Varian Wrynn vanished under mysterious circumstances en route to a diplomatic summit, leaving his young son Anduin on the throne under Highlord Bolvar Fordragon's regency. Relations with former human allies are fractured: the maritime kingdom of Kul Tiras keeps its distance, while Sylvanas Windrunner's undead Forsaken now hold the ruins of Lordaeron.

topic:brotherhood-of-northshire.text: Brotherhood of Northshire. The Brotherhood of Northshire is a holy human clerical order dedicated to the Church of the Holy Light, based out of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Originally known as the Clerics of Northshire, the order suffered catastrophic losses during the First War before being reformed under Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Today, the Brotherhood serves as both a spiritual sanctuary and the primary training ground for fledgling Alliance defenders. Centuries ago, pious missionaries traveled south from Lordaeron into the kingdom of Stormwind, establishing Northshire Abbey to minister to the people and soothe the realm through the Holy Light. Originally known as the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, their compassion was legendary—they even tended to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars. When the Orcish Horde crossed through the Dark Portal, the clerics marched bravely to the front lines without armor or weapons to heal fallen soldiers. Because their healing sustained the Stormwind Army, the orcs ruthlessly targeted them. The order was decimated, the abbey was ransacked and burned, and the surviving clerics were forced to flee north across the sea to Southshore with Sir Anduin Lothar. The slaughter of the Northshire clerics sent shockwaves through the human kingdoms. Realizing that faith alone could not withstand an axe without armor and martial discipline, Archbishop Alonsus Faol resolved to create warriors who possessed both the sacred powers of the Light and the martial mastery of a knight. Drawing upon the surviving clerics and devout knights, Faol formed the Knights of the Silver Hand, giving rise to humanity's first paladins. In this way, the sacrifice of Northshire's fallen healers became the very foundation for the holy warriors who broke the Horde in the Second War. Following the reclamation of Stormwind and the destruction of the Dark Portal, Archbishop Faol oversaw the rebuilding of Northshire Abbey and reorganized the order as the Brotherhood of Northshire. Now in 25 ADP, Northshire Abbey stands as a quiet yet vital center where new recruits gather to begin their service to the realm. Under figures like Priestess Anetta, Brother Sammuel, and Brother Paxton, the Brotherhood attends to the spiritual health of the valley, preserves ancient texts in their library, and trains the next generation of defenders to confront brigands, wolves, and the gathering shadows across Elwynn Forest.

topic:centaur.text: Centaur. Centaur are a violent, horse-bodied humanoid race whose nomadic clans dominate the arid plains of central Kalimdor. Born from the tragic union between the demigod Zaetar and the earth princess Theradras, they spent centuries driving the tauren toward extinction before the newly arrived orcish Horde intervened. Centaur legend traces the race to the caverns of Maraudon beneath Desolace. There, Zaetar, one of the immortal sons of the demigod Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, daughter of the elemental lord Therazane, sired the first centaur. Upon their emergence, the barbaric offspring turned on their father and killed him. Grief-stricken, Theradras trapped Zaetar's spirit within the winding caverns of Maraudon, yet she shielded her vicious children, who swiftly multiplied across Kalimdor. Following their emergence, the centaur expanded outward from Desolace, waging a brutal war of attrition against Kalimdor's native populations. The nomadic tauren suffered the most: driven from their fertile ancestral homeland of Mulgore, they were chased relentlessly across the Barrens. Centaur warbands treated the tauren as prey, burning settlements and hunting them for sport. By the time of the Third War, centuries of relentless pursuit had brought the tauren to the precipice of extinction, leaving them desperately fleeing endless marauders across the savannah. Everything shifted when Warchief Thrall and the newly arrived orcish Horde landed upon Kalimdor. Thrall formed a pact with Cairne Bloodhoof, uniting orcish steel with tauren might. Together, they crushed the aggressive Kolkar warbands, broke their grip on the plains, and enabled the tauren to safely establish Thunder Bluff and reclaim Mulgore. This alliance ended the nomadic exile of the tauren and established a debt of blood and honor that permanently bound them into the Horde. Despite their staggering defeats, centaur remain an active threat across central Kalimdor. Their society is divided into warring clans—primarily the Kolkar, Gelkis, Magram, and Maraudine—each led by a khan and locked in perpetual blood feuds over territory and water. While their internal squabbles keep them from uniting into an unstoppable horde, aggressive raiding parties continue to strike at trade caravans and settlements across Durotar, the Barrens, Thousand Needles, and the borders of Mulgore.

topic:defias-brotherhood.text: Defias Brotherhood. The Defias Brotherhood is a widespread criminal network of bandits, brigands, and assassins waging an underground insurgency against the Kingdom of Stormwind. Originally formed by the artisans of the Stonemasons Guild who were cheated of their pay for rebuilding the capital, they have devolved into violent outlaws terrorizing the southern farmlands. From their hidden redoubt deep beneath Westfall, they aim to overthrow the corrupt House of Nobles and lay waste to the kingdom. Following the Second War, the Stonemasons Guild was hired to rebuild Stormwind from smoldering ruins into a grand stone capital. When their masterwork was finished, the House of Nobles refused to deliver the promised payment, citing crushing wartime debt. Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef spoke out on behalf of his workers, demanding fair restitution, but the nobles responded by ordering the Stonemasons Guild disbanded. The ensuing riots in the city streets ended with the laborers driven out of Stormwind into exile. Stripped of their livelihood and outlawed, VanCleef and the desperate workers banded together, binding their faces in red silk to represent the blood of the wronged, and turned to highway robbery to claim what they believed they were owed. With the royal army overextended, VanCleef turned the neglected farmlands of Westfall into the Brotherhood's base of operations. The bandits overran the hamlet of Moonbrook and commandeered the abandoned subterranean tunnels of the Deadmines. Defias agents seized local mines, driven farmers from their homesteads with reprogrammed harvest golems, and salted the earth to starve the region. With the Crown unable or unwilling to send soldiers to protect rural citizens, local farmers formed The People's Militia out of Sentinel Hill to fight a desperate war of attrition against an enemy that now outmans and outguns them.

topic:druid.text: Druid. Druids are guardians of the natural world who draw power directly from the wild spirits, the celestial bodies, and the Emerald Dream. Master shapeshifters, they adopt the forms of primal beasts to protect the land or mend grievous wounds. Practiced primarily by the night elves, newly revived among the tauren and kept alive by the Skyborne, druids place the preservation of nature above all mortal allegiance. Druidism is far more than a martial art; it is an ancient way of life rooted in deep communion with nature and the demigod Cenarius. Druids wield raw natural energies, commanding roots to entangle their foes, directing the celestial brilliance of the moon and stars, and invoking restorative flora to knit bone and flesh. Their duty is to preserve the cosmic balance and protect the unfettered wild from exploitation and corruption. The defining hallmark of the druid is the supernatural art of shapeshifting. Through spiritual devotion, practitioners channel the primal aspects of Azeroth's beasts. They take on the thick hide of the bear to withstand crushing assaults, slip into the lithe form of the feline predator to strike from the shadows, or adopt aquatic and avian shapes to traverse sea and sky. While transformed, their animal mouths can rarely form mortal words, yet their physical prowess rivals the apex predators of the wild. First taught to Malfurion Stormrage by Cenarius ten thousand years ago, mortal druidism was later formalized under the Cenarion Circle. Headquartered in sacred Moonglade, the Circle watches over druidic practices across Kalimdor, standing independent of mortal factions and political squabbles. While long dominated solely by night elf men who spent centuries slumbering in the Emerald Dream, the aftermath of the Third War saw both night elf women and the tauren welcomed into its fold. Druidism reached the Skyborne long ago. When the Shal'nan's rebellion rose against Prince Tortheldrin in Eldre'Thalas, the common folk who joined it took up nature magic, influenced by the Cenarion Circle to the north, while Tortheldrin scorned it as beneath the Highborne. Their descendants still practice it: the Nightclaw Druids of Shadowgale Forest on Zephras Isle keep largely to themselves, apart from the other Skyborne factions.

topic:druids-of-the-fang.text: Druids of the Fang. The Druids of the Fang are a splinter sect of night elf druids who succumbed to corruption deep within the Wailing Caverns. Originally disciples of the visionary Naralex, they abandoned the Cenarion Circle after their master's connection to the Emerald Dream turned into a foul nightmare. Under the self-proclaimed Lord Serpentis, they now wield serpent-like forms and seek to remake the Barrens into their own twisted paradise. The Barrens was not always an arid wasteland, and Naralex sought to return it to the lush, verdant sanctuary it once was. Naralex led a dedicated order of young druids into the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns, tapping into the natural underground fissures and subterranean springs. By entering an induced slumber, Naralex hoped to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into the waterways, nursing the scorched savannah above back to vibrant life.

topic:dwarf.text: Dwarf. Dwarves are a stout, resilient race carved from the living stone of ancient titan-forged earthen, now inhabiting the snow-capped mountain kingdoms of Khaz Modan and beyond. Known for their mastery of stonework, metallurgy, and devastating frontline combat, they stand as one of the Alliance's fiercest and most dependable pillars. Under the reign of King Magni Bronzebeard, their sprawling subterranean capital of Ironforge serves as the beating heart of dwarven society. Long ago, the subterranean titan-forged known as earthen awoke from an eons-long slumber within the vaults of Uldaman, transformed by the Curse of Flesh into beings of blood and bone. Taking the name dwarves, they reclaimed the high crags of Khaz Modan—named in honor of the titan Khaz'goroth—and carved the majestic subterranean stronghold of Ironforge beneath the peaks of Dun Morogh. Endowed with incredible natural fortitude, a sharp eye for stone and ore, and a penchant for roaring hearths and heady ale, dwarves approach craftsmanship and warfare with identical tenacity. Dwarven unity shattered centuries ago following the death of High King Modimus Anvilmar. Civil war erupted across Ironforge among three rival factions: the Bronzebeard clan, the Wildhammer clan, and the Dark Iron clan. After the Bronzebeards secured the mountain and drove out their kin, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan of the Dark Irons launched a disastrous war of vengeance against both rivals. Driven to desperation beneath the Redridge Mountains, Thaurissan accidentally summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, immolating his own realm into the volcanic wastes of Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes. The surviving Dark Irons were enslaved beneath Blackrock Mountain, while the devastated Wildhammers migrated north to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands. When the orcish Horde surged across the continent during the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard sealed Ironforge's gates against brutal sieges while dwarven forces took up arms alongside the Alliance of Lordaeron. Renowned for heavy plate armor, deadly muskets, and fearless gryphon riders, dwarven warriors played a vital role in shattering the Horde. Today, the Kingdom of Ironforge remains one of the Alliance's most stalwart defenders, welcoming their displaced gnome cousins into their halls while actively unearthing the titan ruins of Khaz Modan to unravel the mysteries of their ancient origins.

topic:earth-mother.text: Earth Mother. The Earth Mother is the supreme, benevolent creator deity worshipped by the tauren, revered as the living embodiment and architect of Azeroth's land and elements. In tauren myth, she shaped the mountains, plains, and seasons and set the sun and moon in the sky as her watchful eyes. Her presence permeates everyday tauren culture, guiding their reverence for nature, duty to the elements, and hopes for the afterlife. Tauren creation myths tell that before day and night existed, the Earth Mother set about shaping Azeroth as a haven for her coming children. Scraping her nails across newly raised mountains sparked the world's first fires, while her hands carved rivers and ocean beds. Her laughter gave breath to the wind, and by lifting the primordial fogs into the sky, she brought the first rains, which coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil. Aided by the friendly elements, the Earth Mother brought forth twins: An'she, the sun, and Mu'sha, the moon. To rest while keeping them safe, she placed the radiant twins into her eyes, creating day, night, and the cycle of the seasons as she opened and closed each lid. Later, she pressed her heart against the fertile earth, breathing the song of life into the land to create the shu'halo, the first tauren. She charged the twins and the elements with teaching the young mortals how to hunt, build, dance, and live in harmony with the wilds. In time, the Earth Mother set An'she and Mu'sha in the sky, where the sun and moon keep watch over the land by day and by night. Tauren say that her spirit now dwells in the rivers, trees, plains, and mountains of the world, and that every lesser nature spirit springs from her and returns to her in the end. Tauren believe her spirit cradles Azeroth still. Her ear is attuned to the winds, hearing the prayers of her children, and her heart beats within the deep stone. Tauren hunters, shamans, and druids direct their thanks to her for every kill and harvest, believing that all life originates from her embrace and that every tauren's spirit returns to her soil upon death.

topic:elemental-plane.text: Elemental Plane. The Elemental Plane is an interconnected pocket dimension forged by the titans to imprison Azeroth's chaotic elementals. Divided into four distinct realms—Skywall, Deepholm, the Abyssal Maw, and the Firelands—it confines the primordial spirits away from the mortal world. Though sealed long ago, cracks in its barriers allow violent elemental incursions and catastrophic summonings into Azeroth. In the ancient days, the elementals served as lieutenants of the Old Gods. When the titans triumphed, they banished the elemental lords and their myriad servants into an isolated realm known as the Elemental Plane, divided into four domains tailored to each primal force: Skywall for air, Deepholm for earth, the Abyssal Maw for water, and the Firelands for fire. With the elementals' departure, nature calmed, and Azeroth's surface finally knew peace. Banishment did not temper the fury of the elementals. Confined within their prison, the primordial powers wage endless wars against one another across the boundaries of their domains. The barriers separating Azeroth from the Elemental Plane are formidable, but not unbreakable. Two centuries ago, during the desperate climax of the War of the Three Hammers, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan pierced the veil to summon Ragnaros the Firelord from the Firelands, an apocalyptic event that ruptured the Redridge Mountains and forged Blackrock Mountain. In recent days, volatile cracks have opened across Kalimdor. Dimensional rifts repeatedly manifest in Silithus, Un'Goro Crater, Azshara, and Winterspring, disgorging waves of hostile elementals eager to test the defenses of the mortal world.

topic:furbolg.text: Furbolg. Furbolgs are a hulking, reclusive race of bear-men native to northern Kalimdor who lived in harmony with nature and the night elves for millennia. In the wake of the Third War, demonic corruption and lingering fel magic have driven nearly every tribe into a frenzied madness. Today, former friends have become vicious territorial predators, with only a tiny handful of tribes clinging to their sanity. Furbolgs are an ancient people of Kalimdor who have long revered the wild god Ursoc. During the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago, tribal packs united under chieftain Unng Ak to fight alongside night elves and tauren against the first demonic invasion. Following the Great Sundering, they chose seclusion deep in the northern woodlands, maintaining peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens while living in simple harmony with the wild. The Third War shattered the furbolgs' tranquil existence. The passage of the Burning Legion through Kalimdor left lingering fel taint across the soil and canopy of Ashenvale and Felwood. Simple-minded and deeply attuned to the land, the bear-men absorbed this corruption directly. Their wizened shamans were overthrown or silenced by bloodthirsty firebrands who channeled fel moss, dark talismans, and corrupt alchemy, transforming peaceful gatherers into rabid raiders who now attack travelers and night elf settlements on sight. Across northern Kalimdor, nearly every major tribe has succumbed: the Gnarlpine across Teldrassil, the Blackwood of Darkshore, the Thistlefur and Foulweald in Ashenvale, and the Deadwood and Winterfall of the northern highlands. Yet a few hold the line. Deep within the fortified tunnels connecting Felwood, Winterspring, and Moonglade, the Timbermaw tribe fiercely guards its sanity. Wary and isolated, the Timbermaw defend their hold against their crazed northern kin, desperate to preserve what remains of their uncorrupted culture.

topic:house-of-nobles.text: House of Nobles. The House of Nobles is the hereditary aristocratic council that helps administer the kingdom of Stormwind from Stormwind Keep. Holding immense leverage over regional land, taxation, and trade, their refusal to pay the rebuilt city's laborers ignited the bloody riots that gave birth to the Defias Brotherhood. Composed of Stormwind's most powerful patrician bloodlines, the House of Nobles serves as the primary advisory body to the Crown. Because the aristocracy owns the majority of the arable land throughout Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, they wield outsized authority over commerce, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. While the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon officially rule the kingdom, the council routinely ties the throne's hands in red tape, asserting the power to stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial administration. Following the Second War, the House of Nobles contracted Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef and the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild Stormwind City from its ashes. However, the nobility simultaneously incurred staggering debts while expanding the kingdom's military frontier south into Stranglethorn. When the gleaming capital was finished, the nobles balked at the invoice and refused to pay the workers their full wages. Enraged by the betrayal, the masons rioted in the streets, prompting the nobility to banish the guild, driving the ruined workers into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood.

topic:human.text: Human. Humans are an adaptable and resilient mortal race who have shaped much of the Eastern Kingdoms' history. Once unified under the ancient Empire of Arathor, their civilization fractured into the Seven Kingdoms, with Stormwind now standing as humanity's primary surviving bastion within the Alliance. Millennia ago, early humans lived as scattered, nomadic tribes constantly threatened by the Amani forest trolls. Recognizing that disunity would mean extinction, Warlord Thoradin of the Arathi tribe united the disparate clans through diplomacy and conquest, establishing the Empire of Arathor with its fortress capital at Strom. During the Troll Wars, the beleaguered high elves of Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor, teaching one hundred humans the arts of arcane magic. Together, they broke the troll armies, securing humanity's dominion over the central continents and laying the foundation for future mortal alliances. As Arathor grew secure and prosperous, its outlying settlements became powerful, self-sufficient city-states. Over time, the centralized empire splintered into seven distinct realms: Gilneas, Alterac, Dalaran, Lordaeron, Kul Tiras, Stormwind, and Stromgarde (the original home of Strom). While these nations traded vigorously with dwarves, gnomes, and elves, peace was fragile. Territorial disputes, border skirmishes—such as the perennial mountain feuds between Alterac and Stromgarde—and courtly intrigue consumed the kingdoms, creating deep rivalries that persisted until external catastrophes forced their hand. The arrival of the orcish Horde through the Dark Portal shattered humanity's internal squabbles. Stormwind was razed during the First War, its refugees fleeing north to warn the other realms. In response, King Terenas Menethil II helped forge the Alliance of Lordaeron, combining the strength of mankind, dwarves, gnomes, and high elves to defeat the Horde in the Second War. Though Stormwind was painstakingly rebuilt, tragedy struck again when the Scourge plague ravaged Lordaeron and Dalaran fell during the Third War, leaving the northern human realms in smoking ruin. Today, Stormwind stands as the strongest remaining human kingdom and the linchpin of the grand Alliance. However, peace remains elusive. King Varian Wrynn has mysteriously vanished while en route to a diplomatic summit, leaving his ten-year-old son, Anduin Wrynn, crowned king while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon serves as regent. To the north, the survivors of Lordaeron are scattered or dead, while Gilneas hides behind its colossal Greymane Wall, leaving Stormwind to bear the weight of mankind's defense.

topic:hunter.text: Hunter. Masters of wilderness survival and deadly marksmanship, hunters roam the untamed reaches of Azeroth alongside fierce beast companions. Armed with bows, rifles, or crossbows, they excel at harassing enemies from a distance while relying on clever traps and primal aspects to control the flow of battle. Whether tracking elusive quarry across snowcapped peaks or stalking prey through dense forests, they live by their wits and connection to nature. At the heart of every hunter lies an instinctual empathy for the primal world. Unlike those who exploit nature or isolate themselves within stone bastions, hunters immerse themselves entirely in untamed lands. They study the habits, movements, and strengths of predatory beasts, earning their respect rather than breaking their spirits. Through patient bonding, a hunter tames dangerous creatures—such as fierce prowling cats, stubborn mountain bears, and sharp-eyed raptors—turning wild animals into steadfast allies that defend them to the death. On the battlefield, hunters dictate the terms of engagement from a safe distance. Armed with bows, heavy crossbows, or calibrated rifles, they unleash deadly volleys that pierce through heavy armor before an attacker can even draw near. Their finely honed senses make them peerless trackers, capable of tracing the faintest footsteps, scents, and disturbances left by quarry. When foes attempt to close the distance, hunters deploy frost and flame traps, disorienting ambushes, or agile evasive maneuvers to keep enemies right where they want them. The path of the hunter manifests differently among the various cultures of Azeroth. Night elf Sentinels embody ancient marksmanship and stealth beneath the canopy of Ashenvale, utilizing bows and shadowcraft in quiet harmony with the wilderness. Dwarven riflemen brave the freezing crags of Dun Morogh alongside hardy bears, mastering the engineering of gunpowder. Across Kalimdor, Tauren and Orc trackers honor ancient nomadic customs, running down their prey with sacred respect and calling upon bestial spirits to guide their shots. In Elwynn Forest, young humans learn the trade from seasoned trackers like the dwarf Tordrin Sternblade in Northshire Valley and Josephine Carson in Goldshire, and the Skyborne learn to track and tame the beasts of Zephras Isle.

topic:leper-gnome.text: Leper gnome. Leper gnomes are the tragic, mutated survivors of Gnomeregan's catastrophic irradiation during the Third War. Maddened by toxic fallout and lingering fumes, most have sworn fealty to the usurper Mekgineer Thermaplugg, fiercely defending their ruined city against all outsiders. When trogg invaders breached Gnomeregan during the Third War, Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to flood the city with radioactive toxins. Thermaplugg claimed the poison would exterminate the troggs while sparing the gnomish population. Instead, the catastrophe wiped out eighty percent of the city's inhabitants. Those who survived within the sealed lower levels were warped in mind and flesh by toxic fallout, mutating into pale, pustulant wretches dubbed leper gnomes. Thermaplugg himself succumbed to the poisonous fallout, losing both his complexion and his sanity. Naming himself techno-overlord and King of Gnomeregan, he gathered the crazed survivors in the Tinkers' Court. In their fractured mental state, many leper gnomes perceive all surface dwellers as trogg intruders, driving them to attack returning rescue parties with frantic savagery. They pilot salvaged mechanical constructs and assemble volatile ordnance, guarding Thermaplugg's twisted kingdom with fanatical devotion. While the majority remain trapped within Gnomeregan's contaminated corridors, a handful of leper gnomes have found their way into the wider world. Driven by desperation or dark ambition, individuals have turned up among the Dark Iron dwarves in Blackrock Depths, operated machinery for the Venture Company in Stonetalon, or taken up service as lab assistants under the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society in the bowels of the Undercity.

topic:lich-king.text: Lich King. The Lich King is the lord and psychic master of the undead Scourge, ruling from the Frozen Throne far to the north in Icecrown. Originally forged by the demon Kil'jaeden from the spirit of the orc shaman Ner'zhul, the entity eventually lured Prince Arthas Menethil into corruption, culminating in their fateful union atop Northrend's icy peaks. When the orc shaman Ner'zhul attempted to flee the dying world of Draenor, he fell directly into the clutches of Kil'jaeden the Deceiver. The demon lord tore Ner'zhul's body to shreds but bound his tormented soul into a block of diamond-hard ice cast out of the Twisting Nether. Flung into Azeroth, the glacial monolith struck the northern wastes of Northrend, forming the Frozen Throne. Kil'jaeden intended the Lich King to forge an unstoppable undead vanguard that would dismantle the mortal kingdoms without succumbing to the infighting that ruined the Orcish Horde. Instead, armed with immense telepathic power, Ner'zhul immediately began plotting his own bid for freedom. Watching dreadlords kept close vigil over the entity, forcing Ner'zhul to act in secret. Reaching out with his mind, he ensnared the exiled Kirin Tor archmage Kel'Thuzad, who established the Cult of the Damned in Lordaeron. Through cauldrons of tainted grain, the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the northern kingdoms. The crisis drew in Prince Arthas Menethil, whose desperation to save his people led him into ruthless brutality, culminating in the infamous slaughter of Stratholme. Blinded by vengeance against the dreadlord Mal'Ganis, Arthas pursued his quarry into Northrend, where the cursed runeblade Frostmourne waited to steal his soul and turn him into the Scourge's premier death knight. Though forced to summon Archimonde and hand temporary command to the Burning Legion, the Lich King anticipated the demons' hubris. Arthas manipulated the demon hunter Illidan Stormrage into claiming the Skull of Gul'dan and slaying Tichondrius, ultimately contributing to Archimonde's ruin at Mount Hyjal. In the aftermath, a desperate Kil'jaeden tasked Illidan with destroying the Frozen Throne. As cracks in the icy spire weakened Ner'zhul's power—allowing Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken to break free—the Lich King summoned his champion home. Arthas returned to Northrend, defeated Illidan at the foot of Icecrown, ascended the spire, and shattered the ice to merge with Ner'zhul into a single terrible consciousness.

topic:light.text: Light. The Light is a boundless primal cosmic force whose energy connects and suffuses all living things across creation. Manifested in the mortal realm as Holy magic, it responds to willpower, meditation, and unyielding faith to mend flesh, shield allies, and purge darkness. The Light is an omnipresent force of living energy. When brought into Azeroth, it manifests as Holy magic. Its power flows through living souls as a connective tissue, binding mortal hearts together. While mortals often personify it as a conscious protector, the Light fundamentally answers the absolute conviction of the soul calling upon it. To channel the Light requires intense self-abnegation, disciplined meditation, and unshakable willpower. Practitioners—most famously the priests of the Church of the Holy Light and the holy paladins—train for years to become clear, empty vessels for its radiance. Through their devotion, the Light manifests as restorative warmth to mend mortal wounds, brilliant wards to shelter the innocent, or searing fire to strike down demons and the risen undead. While humanity and the dwarves revere the Light through formal scripture, other cultures access its brilliance through different spiritual traditions. The night elves channel sacred moonlight through devotion to the goddess Elune, weaving holy magic that cleanses and protects. The tauren honor the sun deity An'she in their own spiritual traditions.

topic:llane-wrynn-i.text: Llane Wrynn I. King Llane Wrynn I was the ruler of Stormwind during the catastrophic First War, whose reign ended with the fall of the kingdom and his own tragic murder. A beloved and proud monarch, his steadfast refusal to believe his friend Medivh had betrayed humanity ultimately doomed his defense of the capital. Born to King Barathen Wrynn, young Prince Llane grew up alongside Anduin Lothar and Medivh. In their youth, the three companions ventured into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale and clashed with the Gurubashi trolls there. In time, Llane ascended to the throne as Stormwind's king. When mysterious, green-skinned creatures emerged from the southern swamps, King Llane dispatched Lothar to investigate the Black Morass. What began as minor skirmishes erupted into the First War as the Horde overran the forests of Duskwood, Westfall, and Redridge. Messengers sent to Lordaeron and other northern human kingdoms were dismissed, their pleas undermined by Stormwind's historic isolationism and aristocratic intrigue. Despite these disadvantages, Llane organized an audacious counterattack alongside Lothar that broke the Horde's initial siege of Stormwind, dealing the invaders their first major defeat.

topic:mage.text: Mage. Mages are scholarly spellcasters who bend the fabric of reality through arcane study, hurling destructive fire, controlling frost, and raw arcane energy. While physically fragile and cloaked only in cloth, their mastery over teleportation, conjuration, and battlefield crowd control makes them formidable allies and terrifying foes. Their discipline requires immense mental dedication, balancing immense destructive potential against the perilous history of arcane misuse. The path of the mage demands intellect, focus, and years of rigorous study. Rather than communing with spirits or relying on divine faith, magi treat magic as a precise cosmic science. By drawing upon arcane energies, a practitioner can weave raw destructive power, summon searing bursts of flame, or chill the surrounding air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Because heavy armor disrupts the delicate somatic gestures and mental focus required for incantations, mages wear light cloth, relying instead on wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells to protect themselves. Human magical heritage began nearly three millennia ago during the Troll Wars, when high elven sorcerers instructed one hundred humans of the Empire of Arathor to turn the tide against the Amani. As the number of human practitioners multiplied, fearful mundane citizens drove many magi to establish the magocracy of Dalaran. Under the governance of the Kirin Tor, Dalaran became the central archive of magical study for the northern kingdoms, formalizing the traditions of combat magic that later supported the Alliance of Lordaeron through the First and Second Wars. Arcane practitioners have never enjoyed uncomplicated trust. From the ancient cataclysm wrought by the Highborne to the catastrophic fall of Dalaran during the Third War, magic's volatile nature evokes widespread wariness. The Church of the Holy Light has historically treated wizardry with skepticism, and conservative knights have often viewed arcane spellcrafters as damned souls or a necessary evil on the battlefield. Despite this suspicion, civil and military leaders recognize that a capable magus offers invaluable battlefield supremacy, swift mass transportation, and essential countermeasures against supernatural threats. The arcane is not the Alliance's alone. Troll and Forsaken mages serve the Horde, and orcs who take up the art begin under the Darkspear mage Mai'ah in the Valley of Trials, who teaches that patience and careful judgment matter more than raw power. Among the Skyborne, the High Order descends from the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas. Their ages in Skywall cost them much of their ancestors' arcane knowledge, and with the wind spirits gone from Zephras Isle they seek to recover it. Skyborne mages fight for the Alliance.

topic:muradin-bronzebeard.text: Muradin Bronzebeard. Muradin Bronzebeard was the brother of King Magni Bronzebeard and Brann Bronzebeard, as well as a renowned warrior, diplomat, and co-founder of the Explorers' League. Revered across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron alike, he is believed to have died in the frozen wastes of Northrend when Prince Arthas Menethil claimed the cursed runeblade Frostmourne. Muradin fought with distinction during the Second War, acting as the vital liaison between the mountain halls of Khaz Modan and the Alliance of Lordaeron. He helped hold Ironforge during the Horde's siege and marched alongside Alliance forces all the way through Blackrock Spire to the Dark Portal. In the peaceful years that followed, Muradin settled into Capital City as Ironforge’s official ambassador. Jovial yet formidable, he became a fixture in the palace, growing close to King Terenas Menethil and taking it upon himself to tutor young Prince Arthas in the arts of swordplay and combat. Beyond politics and war, Muradin possessed a restless curiosity. Alongside his brothers, he helped establish the dwarven Explorers' League, dedicated to uncovering lost titan relics and chronicling the distant corners of the world. He fell in love with the desolate, windswept continent of Northrend, making frequent journeys north to sketch ancient architecture and document its fierce inhabitants. It was Northrend's rugged mysteries that ultimately drew him on his final expedition, seeking out lore, relics, and the whispered legend of a forgotten runeblade.

topic:old-god.text: Old God. The Old Gods are colossal, malevolent horrors of flesh and madness who ruled Azeroth in its primordial dawn. Though vanquished and bound deep beneath the crust by the Titans, their ancient whispers still corrode mortal minds, twist nature, and drive doomsday cults to unearth their prisons. Long before mortal records began, Azeroth was dominated by the Old Gods, colossal entities of chaotic flesh such as C'Thun. They embedded themselves into the planet's crust, commanding elemental armies and insectoid swarms. When the Titans arrived, their armies fought an apocalyptic war against them. Rather than destroying them, the Titans bound the Old Gods in vast, subterranean prisons to keep them dormant forever. Even chained beneath miles of stone and enchanted wards, the Old Gods have never truly slept. Their psychic malice seeps continually into the world, corrupting the vulnerable. It was their collective malice that slowly drove Neltharion the Earth-Warder mad during the War of the Ancients, twisting the noble dragon into Deathwing. When Queen Azshara and her Highborne drowned beneath the raging waters of the Great Sundering, an Old God answered their desperation, transforming them into the serpentine naga.

topic:paladin.text: Paladin. Paladins are holy warriors who blend martial prowess with the power of the Holy Light. Clad in heavy plate, they protect the innocent, heal the wounded and strike down wicked foes. Humans and dwarves carry the Silver Hand's legacy for the Alliance, and among the Horde, Forsaken who served the Light in life still answer its call, though it burns them. The paladins were originally established during the Second War by Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Having witnessed the devastation wrought upon the pious Clerics of Northshire during the First War, Faol recognized that healers alone could not survive the brutality of orcish warfare. He gathered virtuous knights of Lordaeron and trained surviving clerics in the ways of martial combat and divine magic. Baptized as the Knights of the Silver Hand and led by Uther the Lightbringer, these champions provided both physical defense and spiritual renewal to the kingdoms of humanity. Where priests act as the voice of the Holy Light—preaching faith and tending the spirits of the common folk—paladins serve as its martial arm. Their profound conviction grants them miraculous powers: they project emboldening auras, seal sanctified blessings upon their allies, and mend fatal injuries. In combat against unholy horrors, the Light burns through their strikes, allowing paladins to incinerate undead and demonic entities with righteous fury. The fall of Lordaeron during the Third War scattered the original order, yet the ideals of the Silver Hand endure. In the south, the humans of Stormwind and the stalwart dwarves of Ironforge have taken up the mantle. Training in sanctuaries like the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries, these paladins pledge their swords and shields to uphold justice and defend the Alliance from the gathering shadows. Not every knight of Lordaeron stayed in the grave. Some Forsaken who served the Light in life still hold to their vows, and the Light still answers them, though it sears their dead flesh with every prayer. Aramis Hammerhand trains these risen paladins in the chapel at Deathknell, Shari Stilwell continues their instruction in Brill, and an order of Forsaken paladins, Tyr's Watch, holds Bandarion Keep in western Tirisfal. Theirs is a lonely road: they wield the very power that burned their people, and Sylvanas Windrunner tolerates their order while watching it closely.

topic:priest.text: Priest. Priests are spiritual guides and conduits of immense unseen power who shape belief, mend flesh, and guard souls. Channeling the radiant energies of faith or plumbing the terrifying depths of the Void, they serve as the vital heart of any war party. Across Azeroth, their traditions range from the Church of the Holy Light to the Moon Goddess's Sisterhood and shadowy Forsaken cults. Priests guide the spiritual destiny of their communities. While physical combatants test their mettle with steel, priests draw power directly from conviction. Through divine connection, they soothe grievous wounds, raise fallen companions from death's threshold, and weave mystic barriers to repel incoming harm. Their presence on the field often marks the difference between survival and annihilation. The priesthood is not solely an instrument of benevolence. Just as life holds both illumination and darkness, the priest walks a perilous line between divine restoration and mental devastation. Those who master the holy arts call down searing righteous vengeance to smite enemies, while practitioners of Shadow magic delve into the Void to dominate minds, twist willpower, and inflict agonizing pain from afar. No single faith defines Azeroth's priests. Among humans, dwarves and gnomes, the Church of the Holy Light codifies a philosophy of virtue, having adapted its fragile Clerics of Northshire into a hardened order after the First War. In Kalimdor, the night elven Sisterhood of Elune honors the Mother Moon with starlight and grace, while troll witch doctors beseech the primal Loa. Among the newly risen Forsaken, many have turned from former dogmas toward the Cult of the Forgotten Shadow, preaching that darkness and light must exist in delicate equilibrium.

topic:rogue.text: Rogue. Rogues are masters of stealth, espionage, and sudden, lethal combat who dictate the terms of engagement from the shadows. Relying on light leather armor, dual-wielded blades, and brewed toxins, they strike unawares before vanishing back into the dark. Across Azeroth, they serve as scouts, assassins, pickpockets, and agents for factions and hidden syndicates alike. Rogues eschew the heavy plate and open confrontation of traditional frontline warriors. Clad in lightweight leather to remain completely silent and mobile, they stalk their quarry unseen. When they engage, they seize the opening moments through precision and surprise, aiming for vital organs or exposed joints. Utilizing an ever-flowing pool of energy and rapid weapon combinations, a rogue softens up an enemy with carefully chained strikes before unleashing a catastrophic finishing blow. A blade alone is rarely enough for a professional cutpurse or killer. Rogues are skilled alchemists of lethal concoctions, hand-crafting venomous coatings to numb limbs, slow escapes, or rapidly sap the vitality of their targets. Coupled with lockpicking tools, thrown weapons, and distracting trickery, they excel at slipping past fortified perimeters, disarming traps, and infiltrating vaults that would stump a company of soldiers. While many rogues operate as lone wolves, highwaymen, or street-level thugs, the finest operatives belong to organized intelligence networks and assassin guilds. Stormwind relies on the clandestine operatives of SI:7, and the Forsaken utilize the relentless Deathstalkers. In Orgrimmar, the shadowy remnants of the Shattered Hand serve the Warchief, while the elite, neutral League of Assassins answers to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt.

topic:scarlet-crusade.text: Scarlet Crusade. Born from the shattered remnants of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade is a fanatical holy order obsessed with purging the undead from Lordaeron. Blighted by paranoia and radical zealotry, they view anyone outside their ranks as carriers of the plague and shoot outsiders on sight. From strongholds across Tirisfal Glades and the Plaguelands, their crimson banners wage a ruthless war against Scourge and living alike. When Prince Arthas betrayed Lordaeron and murdered King Terenas Menethil II, the Order of the Silver Hand was broken. Surviving paladins and priests rallied under leaders like Alexandros Mograine, Saidan Dathrohan, and General Abbendis to reclaim their ruined homeland. Reorganizing their forces at Hearthglen and Tyr's Hand, they swore to cleanse the undead scourge with holy fire. Yet as the war dragged on, tragedy and suspicion festered within their ranks. What began as a desperate resistance soon devolved into an unyielding, xenophobic crusade. As the Crusade's dogma hardened into religious madness, moderate commanders recoiled. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus and his followers argued that retaking the north required alliances across Azeroth, seeking aid from the dwarves, gnomes, and night elves. Rejected by the zealots, Tyrosus and other disillusioned knights abandoned the order to form the Argent Dawn, remaining faithful to the pure, inclusive tenets of the Holy Light. Meanwhile, the Scarlet Crusade seized the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades as their heart of power, slaughtering travelers and refugees under the hysterical belief that all who walk the Plaguelands carry the Scourge's contagion.

topic:shadow-council.text: Shadow Council. The Shadow Council was the secret cabal of warlocks and necrolytes that orchestrated the corruption of the Old Horde on Draenor and guided its invasion of Azeroth. Founded by Gul'dan under the direction of the Burning Legion, the cult manipulated clan chieftains from behind the scenes until Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer purged their stronghold in Blackrock Mountain. Before the crossing into Azeroth, Gul'dan brought together a clandestine assembly of warlocks, necrolytes, and opportunistic chieftains to manipulate the orcish clans. By elevating Blackhand the Destroyer as a malleable figurehead, the Shadow Council ruled the Old Horde from the dark. They disseminated fel magic across Draenor and fed the blood of the demon Mannoroth to the clans, binding the orcs to the will of the Burning Legion. The Shadow Council entered a pact with Medivh—the Guardian possessed by Sargeras—to breach the barrier between worlds. Through the Dark Portal, the Council guided the Horde into the Kingdom of Stormwind. From their sanctum in Blackrock Spire, the warlocks oversaw the war effort.

topic:shaman.text: Shaman. Shaman are spiritual mediators who commune with the primordial forces of earth, air, fire and water. Balancing raw nature through totems, lightning and ancestral healing, they are the spiritual core of orc, tauren and troll culture under Warchief Thrall. Dwarves walk the path too, as the Wildhammer long have, and the Skyborne Windshapers seek to restore their people's bond with the winds. Unlike priests who revere the divine or mages who bend the arcane, shaman interact directly with the primal forces of nature. The elements of earth, air, fire, and water are inherently chaotic and locked in perpetual conflict. A shaman does not enslave these forces, but petitions and negotiates with them, serving as a balance keeper between primal fury and the mortal world. Through wooden and stone totems planted into the soil, shaman channel these elemental bargains to protect allies, hinder foes, or mend the wounded with cleansing water. Shamanism was once the ancient foundation of orcish clan life on Draenor. However, Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Council deceived the shamans into war against the draenei, causing the elemental spirits to withdraw their favor. Stripped of their gifts, many former shaman succumbed to demonic corruption and became warlocks, nearly extinguishing the tradition entirely. Only after the Second War did Thrall, guided by Drek'Thar of the Frostwolf clan, rediscover the ancient rites. Thrall's ascension as Warchief revitalized shamanism, elevating it into the moral compass of the New Horde. Across Kalimdor, shamanic traditions vary widely among the Horde's allied peoples. Tauren mystics treat communion with the earth and the spirits as a sacred cultural anchor. Darkspear trolls approach the discipline through reverence for the loa and ancestral wild spirits, weaving voodoo and nature rites together. Across all these tribal borders, shaman stand as essential community elders, advisers, and fearsome front-line defenders. The shaman's path does not belong to the Horde alone. Among the dwarves, the Wildhammer of Aerie Peak have long called on storm and stone, and Wildhammer earthseers such as Earthseer Farsen bring that far-seeing craft to Dun Morogh. Dwarves of Ironforge take up the totem as well and fight for the Alliance. Far above the world, the Windshapers are the spiritual leaders of the Skyborne. The wind spirits of Zephras Isle have fallen silent, and the Windshapers train new shaman in the hope of restoring that lost bond; Skyborne who join the Horde follow their path.

topic:shan-do.text: Shan'do. Shan'do is a revered Darnassian honorific meaning "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." Traditionally used within night elven society and druidic circles, it denotes deep reverence toward a mentor who guides another along the path of wisdom and natural magic. Its direct counterpart is thero'shan, meaning "honored student." In the Darnassian language, shan'do translates directly to "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." It is far more than an occupational label: addressing an elder or mentor as shan'do expresses solemn humility, filial devotion, and enduring respect for their guidance. The title is most famously intertwined with the history of the Cenarion Circle. The demigod Cenarius was the original shan'do to Malfurion Stormrage, instructing him in the ways of nature before the War of the Ancients. In turn, Malfurion became shan'do to generations of mortal druids, to the point where "Shan'do Stormrage" is his standard styling among night elves, forest keepers, and reverent allies across Kalimdor. While most common among Cenarion druids—such as disciples addressing Naralex or the slumbering Malfurion—the honorific is fundamentally Darnassian, not exclusively religious. The title represents the bond of transmission between master and pupil, irrespective of the school of thought.

topic:stonemasons-guild.text: Stonemasons Guild. The Stonemasons Guild was the collective of master builders and artisans responsible for reconstructing Stormwind City after the Second War. Following a bitter dispute over payment with the House of Nobles that ended in deadly riots, the guild was forcibly dissolved, driving its members into exile and giving rise to the Defias Brotherhood. Led by elected Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef, the artisans of the Stonemasons Guild demonstrated a mastery of masonry that rivaled the Royal Stonecutters Union of the dwarves. Following the devastation of the First and Second Wars, the House of Nobles hired the guild to embark upon the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City from ruins, trusting them to restore the capital to its ancient grandeur. For years, VanCleef and an army of craftsmen toiled through Elwynn, raising the soaring spires of Stormwind Keep and the massive arches of the Cathedral of Light. However, royal finances collapsed under heavy military debts incurred in southern campaigns. Influenced by aristocratic politics, the House of Nobles refused to pay the guild their agreed salaries and fees. When VanCleef petitioned for restitution, the nobles answered by unilaterally disbanding the guild, sparking immense fury among the laborers who had bled to rebuild the city.

topic:stormwind-kingdom.text: Stormwind (kingdom). The Kingdom of Stormwind is the southernmost and currently foremost human realm on Azeroth, holding dominion over Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains. Sacked and shattered during the First War, it was rebuilt through blood and labor after the Second, rising to become the military and cultural center of the Alliance following the tragic collapse of Lordaeron in the north. Today, the kingdom stands beset from within and without, ruled by the ten-year-old King Anduin Wrynn under the watchful guidance of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon while its crowned monarch remains missing. Stormwind was established over a thousand years ago by descendants of the ancient Arathi empire who ventured south beyond the crags of Khaz Modan into fertile, forested valleys. Far from the northern kingdoms, the realm grew into a culture fiercely proud of its self-reliance and the Light. That independence was nearly extinguished when the Orcish Horde poured through the Dark Portal. Stormwind City burned to ash in the First War, its King Llane slain. The surviving populace fled north across the Great Sea led by Sir Anduin Lothar, rallying the northern realms into the Alliance of Lordaeron. Once the Orcish threat was crushed in the Second War, refugees returned home, hiring the Stonemasons Guild to rebuild their magnificent capital of white stone and blue banners. When the Scourge wiped out Lordaeron during the Third War, Stormwind became humanity's greatest remaining bastion.

topic:syndicate.text: Syndicate. The Syndicate is a widespread human criminal organization founded and led by dispossessed nobles of the fallen kingdom of Alterac. Operating out of fortified strongholds across the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the ruins of Stromgarde Keep, they wage an uncompromising war against both the Alliance and the Horde to restore their lost aristocracy. When the kingdom of Alterac collapsed in dishonor following King Aiden Perenolde's treachery during the Second War, its aristocracy was stripped of land and title. Refusing to accept their exile, the remaining Alteraci nobility banded together under the late king's son, Prince Aliden Perenolde. Adopting distinctive orange bandanas and standardizing their ranks with hired thugs, highwaymen, and hedge wizards, they forged the Syndicate. To the outside world, they behave like common brigands, raiding caravans, ambushing travelers, and running extortion rings. In truth, their criminal enterprises exist solely to fund an organized effort to reconquer their ancestral domains and subjugate surrounding lands. The Syndicate maintains entrenched footholds across northern Lordaeron. In the snowy Alterac Mountains, they fortified the ruined town of Strahnbrad and established encampments throughout the Uplands and Dandred's Fold. To the south, they hold the crumbling remnants of Durnholde Keep in the Hillsbrad Foothills, using it as a springboard to harass Southshore and raid supply routes.
